readers.angle_summary:
Bottom line: most of what N2 would claim here is already in prior work or follows directly from it. Only a narrow FOH-specific and protocol-specific contribution appears to remain.

(1) The exact CDE solution already ignores the time grid of the same reconstructed path. This is the classical reparametrisation (tree-like) invariance. Kidger et al. (2020, App. B) say explicitly that series differing only by a collinear inserted point have the same interpolation, that they 'would often prefer' to treat them as equal, and that an observation-intensity channel tells them apart. Kidger's thesis (Sec. 3.5.2) says this invariance 'does not completely carry through to the numerical discretisation'. With s_j = j and a fixed unit step, an NCDE 'reduces to an RNN'. torchcde's recommended practice makes the solver grid depend on the knots, whether through jump_t at the knots for adaptive solvers or step_size set to the smallest gap. Hermite cubic interpolation with backward differences (torchcde's usual choice and Log-NCDE's NCDE baseline) changes when linear knots are inserted. N2's 'per-observation nonlinearity breaks invariance' counterexample is therefore a formalisation of a known remark, not a discovery.

(2) Exact input summaries with nonlinear updates only on a coarse grid are well established: the log-ODE family (NRDE, Log-NCDE, SLiCE), Logsig-RNN (2019, 2021) and Rough Transformers. Log-signatures of a piecewise-linear path over fixed physical-time windows are exactly invariant to collinear knot insertion. This follows from Chen's identity and reparametrisation invariance (primer, Corollary 1), but no paper states it as a knot-refinement theorem. Whether the published pipelines have this invariance depends on how windows are defined:
- NRDE uses t_i = i, and Log-NCDE's intervals are 'a fixed number of observations', so both break it.
- torchcde.logsig_windows uses physical-time windows with linearly interpolated boundaries. It therefore already implements 'exact PL summary plus a fixed physical-time nonlinear clock', but never states or tests the invariance.
- Rough Transformers use a 'fixed set of time points', but the code snaps boundaries to the last observation. Their Prop. 3.1 is only approximate (≈) and is tested with random drop.
- Logsig-RNN tests downsampling and missing data separately, and trains on sequences lengthened by linear interpolation.

(3) The biggest overlap is Walker et al. (2026, arXiv 2605.30213, Online Log-NCDEs). It builds exact interval log-signatures over physical-time query partitions that do not depend on observation times, and holds them fixed when inputs are dropped. Appendix A.5 states an exact invariance to inserting or removing 'value-preserving' observations, i.e. ZOH/rectilinear-type virtual knots. It also uses count coordinates to deliberately separate repeats from real measurements. That covers the refinement-invariance and knot-vs-measurement components of N2, for a ZOH-type reconstruction. The paper also argues against reconstructions based on interpolation.

(4) Other prior pieces that must be labelled as existing results:
- ZOH is the exact solution for piecewise-linear drivers, and Mamba is an Euler discretisation of a continuous gate integral (Cirone et al. 2024).
- Exact per-segment integration of a linear SSM over piecewise-linear paths, with a small-Δt-stable formulation (Exponentially Weighted Signature, 2026).
- Discretisation-bias bounds for NCDEs (Bleistein et al.).
- Grid independence only as the mesh goes to 0 for dt-rescaled controlled ResNets (neural signature kernels).

(5) What appears not covered in this angle:
- An exact first-order-hold (linear-interpolation) learnable diagonal linear-SSM stem feeding a standard fixed-step deep SSM on a physical clock, with a stated exact invariance theorem for FOH virtual knots.
- A controlled three-way protocol that separates lossless refinement, real downsampling with an explicit statement that aliasing is not recovered, and missing observations.
- Head-to-head tests against physical-window log-ODE (torchcde), RFormer and Online Log-NCDE baselines.
If N2's gains come mostly from a coarse fixed clock over exact summaries, the existing log-ODE, RFormer and Logsig-RNN models already explain them, which points to NO_GO under the user's criterion. Candidate distinctions are FOH versus ZOH invariance and SSM versus log-signature stems, and both must be shown empirically.

Calibration numbers:
- EigenWorms, 70/15/15 resplit with 23 duplicates removed: Log-NCDE 85.6±5.1 (depth 2, step 12); NRDE 83.9±7.3 (depth 2, step 4); NCDE 75.0±3.9; LRU 87.8±2.8; S5 81.1±3.7; S6 85.0±16.1; Mamba 70.9±15.8; BD-SLiCE 86±4; LNCDE with Log-ODE 88.3±3.7; LinOSS-IM 95.0±4.4.
- Rough Transformer 90.3±0.1 (10 windows); linear-interpolation resampling plus a vanilla Transformer 64.10%.
- NRDE's own paper: depth 2, step 4 gives 83.8±3.0.
- NCDE Speech Commands (MFCC, 161×20): 89.8±2.5%.
- None of these papers report HAR, PDM or a Speech Commands resolution change.

readers.angle: Irregular and multi-rate time-series models that would be close, task-appropriate baselines for real-signal classification under downsampling and missing observations. Covered: S5 with a per-step dt, TIDES, mTAN, IP-Nets, ContiFormer, GRU-D, ODE-RNN/Latent ODE, CRU, Neural Flows, LinOSS, S7, Liquid-S4, Mamba-for-irregular work, recent 2025-2026 SSM and irregular models, plus Rough Transformer and Neural CDE, since they set the random-drop protocols and the EigenWorms drop numbers. Also collected calibration numbers for UCI-HAR and EigenWorms (with and without drop).

papers.title: TIDES: Implicit Time-Awareness in Selective State Space Models
papers.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv 2605.09742 (v1, 10 May 2026; paper marks itself as an anonymous submission)
papers.sections_read: Abstract; 1 (incl. Our approach, Contributions); 2.1-2.3; 3.1; 3.2; 4 (Fading Flash, Findings); 5.1-5.3; 6; 7; App A (block order, timescale, GLU); App B.1 (ZOH); App C.1-C.4; App D.1-D.2; App F (random-drop details, Table 7); App G
papers.mechanism: A selective diagonal complex SSM (S5-style), with Re(Lambda_k), B_k and C_k computed from each input token u_k by affine or GLU heads with RMSNorm. Im(Lambda) stays static. The step size is the physical gap Delta_k = t_{k+1} - t_k and is not learned from the input. Each block is BN, then SSM, then GELU, then GLU, with dropout and a residual connection. Can be bidirectional. Mean pooling is not stated explicitly for classification.
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH: u_k is held constant on [t_k, t_{k+1}) and integrated exactly in closed form (App B.1). There is no FOH or linear-interpolant integration.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every observation token: the input-dependent Lambda_k, B_k and C_k per token, then GELU+GLU per token in every block, plus BatchNorm over batch and time.
papers.time_handling: Physical dt as the discretization step (Delta_tilde = Delta_k, set by timestamps), with a learnable per-mode timescale scaler. Mamba baselines instead receive Delta as an extra input channel.
papers.invariance_claim: No invariance claim for representations under a grid change. The claim is extrapolation to unseen Delta values 'by construction', because Delta enters only through the discretization, and this is shown empirically (Fading Flash, and EigenWorms with r_test different from r_train). Sec 2.1 states the semigroup property for the linear part. My analysis, not claimed by the paper: one TIDES SSM layer is exactly invariant to a knot inserted on the ZOH path with value u_k, because Lambda(u_k) and B(u_k) are unchanged and ZOH steps compose. The new output token and the per-token GELU/GLU, however, change the next layer's input sequence, and a knot on a linear interpolant changes even the first layer.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Fading Flash: a global Delta in {0.1,...,2.0}, trained on [0.5,1.5]. This rescales the whole trajectory; it is not refinement of the same path. EigenWorms random drop: a different random 50% of steps dropped at each training step, tested with fixed indices at r_test in {0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9}, keeping the original timestamps. Physiome-ODE with 80% of values per channel randomly masked. UEA with no downsampling. No lossless knot refinement and no real-downsampling-with-aliasing test.
evidence_quotes: Under irregular sampling, $\tilde{\Delta}$ still varies from step to step, but it is set by the observation timestamps, not produced by a function of the input. (Sec 1, Our approach)
doubling $\Delta$ produces the same state evolution as integrating the continuous system for twice as long. (Sec 2.1)
Three projection heads compute the input-dependent SSM parameters from each input $u_{k}\in\mathbb{R}^{H}$ (Sec 3.2, Eq. 5)
Assuming the input $u(t)$ is held constant on $[t_{k},t_{k+1})$ at value $u_{k}$ , the exact solution of (8) is (App B.1, Eq. 10)
baking $\Delta$ in implicitly provides extrapolation across unseen timedeltas by construction. (Sec 4, Findings)

a different random 50% of timesteps is dropped at each training step; evaluation uses fixed indices at varying $r_{\mathrm{test}}$ , with original timestamps preserved to expose the elapsed gap. (Sec 5.3)
No data augmentation, time warping, or downsampling is applied. (App D.1, UEA protocol)
papers.reported_numbers: UEA (Walker-2024/RFormer protocol: 70/15/15 random re-split, 5 seeds), EigenWorms accuracy: TIDES 85.7+-4.0, LogNCDE 85.6+-5.1, RFormer 90.3+-0.1, LRU 87.8+-2.8, S6 85.0+-16.1, S5 81.1+-3.7, NCDE 75.0+-3.9, NRDE 83.9+-7.3, Mamba 70.9+-15.8, Transformer OOM. LinOSS-IM (95.0) is not in this table. Six-dataset average: TIDES 66.1. EigenWorms random drop (App F, Table 7; ~30k params, L=1, P=16, bidirectional, ZOH, 3 seeds, r_train=0.5), accuracy at r_test=0.1/0.3/0.5/0.7/0.9: TIDES 0.752/0.743/0.743/0.743/0.714 (mean 0.739); S5 0.419 at every r; Mamba_S 0.705/0.705/0.705/0.686/0.400; TIDES_BC 0.695/.../0.686; TIDES_full mean 0.663; RFormer 0.771/0.762/0.771/0.733/0.562 (mean 0.720). Timing (App G): TIDES at L=10k takes 342 ms/step and 11.8 GB, while RFormer is OOM at 24 GB.
papers.notes: The most recent SSM for irregular sampling and a direct 'dt-only (physical Delta) + per-token nonlinearity' comparator for N2. Its design principle ('keep discretization and expressivity on separate ledgers') is conceptually adjacent to N2 but different: expressivity remains per observation. It does not separate knots from measurements, and downsampling is only random index drop, so aliasing is not studied. S5 at 0.419 on EigenWorms-drop with this tiny config is far below the full-data results; use with caution for calibration. There may be an inconsistency: Table 1 uses the Walker protocol but omits LinOSS.

papers.title: Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling (S5)
papers.mechanism: A MIMO diagonalized continuous-time linear SSM with ZOH discretization and a learnable per-state timescale Delta, run with a parallel scan. Irregular sampling is handled by supplying a different A_bar_k (Delta_k) at each step. Layers are stacked with a GELU/sigmoid gate, then mean pooling.
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH of each sample over its step (Eq. 6). No interpolation.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every token: u'_k = GELU(y_k) * sigmoid(W GELU(y_k)) after each S5 layer. Norm, dropout and mean pooling are also computed over tokens.
papers.time_handling: dt as the step size. For irregular data, a per-step Delta_t comes from timestamps (pendulum). For a sampling-rate change, the learned Delta is rescaled globally by the rate ratio. Ablations: S5-drop (Delta_t set to 1) and S5-append (Delta_t appended as a channel).
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical and approximate: continuous-time parameterization allows applying the model at another sampling rate without retraining, by rescaling Delta. No exact invariance claim, and nothing on knot refinement.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Real downsampling: Speech Commands 16 kHz to 8 kHz by naive decimation, zero-shot. Irregular sampling: pendulum images (L=50 irregular samples from T=100). No lossless refinement and no random-drop sweep.
evidence_quotes: Parallel scans and the continuous-time parameterization also allow for efficient handling of irregularly sampled time series and other time-varying SSMs, by simply supplying a different $\overline{\mathbf{A}}_{k}$ matrix at each step. (Sec 3.3)

these models can be applied to datasets with different sampling rates without the need for re-training, simply by globally re-scaling the timescale parameter $\Delta$ by the ratio between the new and old sampling rates. (Sec 6.2)
Last column indicates 0-shot testing at 8kHz (constructed by naive decimation). (Table 2 caption)
the layer output of the activation function we apply is $\mathbf{u}_{k}^{\prime}=\mathrm{GELU}(\mathbf{y}_{k})\odot\sigma(\mathbf{W}*\mathrm{GELU}(\mathbf{y}_{k}))$ (App G.1)
S5-drop uses the same S5 architecture, but drops the dependence on the inter-sample interval, i.e. $\Delta_{t}\triangleq 1.0$ . (App F.3)
papers.reported_numbers: Speech Commands 35-way, 16 kHz / 8 kHz zero-shot (naive decimation): S5 96.52/94.53; S4-LegS 96.08/91.32; S4D-LegS 95.83/91.08; Liquid-S4 96.78/90.00; ConvNet 95.51/7.26; InceptionNet 61.24/5.18. Pendulum regression MSE x1e-3: S5 3.41 (0.27), S5-drop 6.68, S5-append 4.13, CRU (their rerun) 3.94, mTAND 65.64, ODE-RNN 7.26. (EigenWorms for S5 is reported elsewhere: 81.1+-3.7 under the Walker protocol.)
papers.notes: The canonical 'dt-only rescaling' baseline. Its sampling-rate test is real downsampling (decimation without an anti-alias filter, called 'naive'), so it mixes aliasing with the grid change. The irregular path uses ZOH of samples plus a per-token nonlinearity, so inserting virtual knots (e.g. linear-interpolated values) would change the input path under ZOH and add tokens. That is my inference; it is not tested.

papers.title: Multi-Time Attention Networks for Irregularly Sampled Time Series (mTAN)
papers.sections_read: 1; 3 (time embedding, multi-time attention, discretization); 4 (encoder-decoder, supervised); 5 (datasets, classification, Table 2); App A.1 (grep); A.3; A.4; code src/tan_classification.py (grep for reference points)
papers.mechanism: Learned time embeddings (linear + sinusoids) form query/key similarities. For each channel, a softmax-normalized kernel smoother of the observed values is computed at reference times. The resulting fixed-length sequence goes to a GRU (mTAND-Enc) or a VAE with an RNN encoder/decoder (mTAND-Full), then a classifier.
papers.input_reconstruction: None as an explicit path. It uses a learned attention kernel smoother (Nadaraya-Watson-like, normalized over the observed points) evaluated at reference points.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: The softmax attention weights depend nonlinearly on all observation times, and the normalization runs over observations. The GRU and MLP run on the fixed reference grid (128 points, linspace(0,1) in the code).
papers.time_handling: Continuous-time embedding of timestamps (normalized to [0,1]). The downstream network runs on a fixed reference grid.
papers.invariance_claim: None. Per my analysis, the softmax normalization over observations makes the interpolant depend on observation density, so inserting virtual knots changes it.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Naturally irregular data (PhysioNet, MIMIC-III), the 'Human Activity' dataset (UCI Localization Data for Person Activity), and synthetic interpolation with sparse observations. No controlled refinement or downsampling sweep.
evidence_quotes: the structure of the intermediate continuous-time function $\hat{x}_{hd}(t,\mathbf{s})$ is essentially a kernel smoother applied to the $d^{th}$ dimension of the time series. (Sec 3, Eq. 3)
The form of the attention mechanism is a softmax function over the observed time points $t_{id}$ for dimension $d$ . (Sec 3, Eq. 4)
the mTAN module can easily be adapted to produce such an output representation by materializing its output at a set of reference time points (Sec 3, Discretization)
For the classification tasks, we use $128$ reference points. (App A.4)
dim, torch.linspace(0, 1., 128), args.latent_dim, args.rec_hidden, 128, learn_emb=args.learn_emb (code src/tan_classification.py line 73)
papers.reported_numbers: Table 2: PhysioNet AUC mTAND-Enc 0.854+-0.001 and mTAND-Full 0.858+-0.004; MIMIC-III AUC 0.8419/0.8544; Human Activity (per-time-point accuracy, UCI Localization/Person Activity, not UCI-HAR smartphone) mTAND-Enc 0.907+-0.002, mTAND-Full 0.910+-0.002, ODE-RNN 0.885, GRU-D 0.862, IP-Nets 0.869. In ContiFormer's UEA random-drop Table 3, mTAN averages 0.7381/0.7118/0.6955 at 30/50/70% drop.
papers.notes: A 'fixed-clock network' precedent: the GRU runs on a fixed grid of reference times. It has no exact input integration and no invariance claim; its interpolant is density-weighted, and ContiFormer reports that its attention depends solely on time. It is the attention-style counterpart of the mandatory 'resample onto a fixed grid + backbone' baseline.

papers.title: Interpolation-Prediction Networks for Irregularly Sampled Time Series (IP-Nets)
papers.mechanism: A semi-parametric RBF interpolation network outputs, for each channel at evenly spaced reference times: a smooth interpolant, a transient component, and an intensity function (the sum of kernel weights). A cross-channel layer mixes them. A GRU prediction network runs on the regular reference grid. An auto-encoding loss is added.
papers.input_reconstruction: Normalized squared-exponential kernel smoothers (Nadaraya-Watson) at fixed reference points, plus an unnormalized intensity channel. This is not an exact interpolant.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: The GRU runs on the fixed, evenly spaced reference grid. The interpolation layer is a fixed-form kernel map with learned bandwidths and correlations.
papers.time_handling: Fixed evenly spaced reference time grid over a common interval (e.g. 48 h). Observation times enter only through the kernels.
papers.invariance_claim: None. By construction the intensity channel changes when points are added, and the normalized smoother changes when density changes (my analysis).
papers.grid_changes_tested: MIMIC-III (naturally irregular) and UWave, randomly subsampled to 10% of points.
evidence_quotes: The $T$ reference time points $r_{t}$ are chosen to be evenly spaced within that interval. (Sec 3.2)
the intensity functions $\bm{\lambda}_{d}$ to capture information about where observations occur in time. (Sec 3.2.1)
In this work, we conduct experiments leveraging a GRU network as the prediction network. (Sec 3.2.2)
we randomly sample 10% of the observations points from each time series to create a sparse and irregularly sampled data. (App A.1.2)
papers.reported_numbers: UWave 10% subsample and MIMIC-III numbers were not extracted. mTAN Table 2 reports IP-Nets at PhysioNet AUC 0.819, MIMIC-III 0.8390, and Human Activity (Localization) accuracy 0.869.
papers.notes: The oldest clear instance of 'nonlinear network on a fixed physical-time reference grid' fed by a learned resampler, with an explicit observation-intensity channel. It is close to the mandatory fixed-grid resampling baseline. The intensity channel deliberately encodes where observations occur, which is the opposite of treating virtual knots as non-information, though it gives a knot-versus-measurement handle.

papers.title: ContiFormer: Continuous-Time Transformer for Irregular Time Series Modeling
papers.sections_read: 3; 3.1 (continuous dynamics, query function, scaled dot product, expected values, CT-MHA); 3.2 (layer, sampling process); 4.2 (Table 3); C.2.1-C.2.2 (partial); D.3 (grep)
papers.mechanism: Each observation starts a key and a value trajectory evolved by a neural ODE. The query is a natural-cubic-spline interpolant of the per-observation queries. Attention logits are time-averaged integrals of q.k_i over [t_i, t], softmax over the N observations. FFN and LayerNorm follow, and the layer output is sampled at reference points before stacking.
papers.input_reconstruction: Natural cubic spline for queries and for the residual path. Keys and values are per-observation ODE trajectories, solved numerically with a fixed-step solver.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Softmax over all observations at each query time; the neural ODE vector fields inside the solver for each observation's key/value; FFN/LN at reference points, which are the input time points or task-specific times.
papers.time_handling: Continuous time via per-observation ODEs and integrals over [t_i, t]. Time is normalized to [0,1] (ablation D.6).
papers.invariance_claim: None about sampling. It claims continuous-time outputs ('almost' continuous without dropout) and gives an expressivity analysis. By my analysis, extra (virtual) observations add keys and values to the softmax, so the representation changes.
papers.grid_changes_tested: 20 UEA datasets with 30/50/70% of observations randomly dropped (NCDE protocol). EigenWorms is not included. Also irregular event sequences and a spiral interpolation task.
evidence_quotes: we define a closed-form continuous-time interpolation function (e.g., natural cubic spline) with knots at $t_{1},\ldots,t_{N}$ such that $\bm{\mathrm{q}}(t_{i})=Q_{i}$ (Sec 3.1, Query Function)
it utilizes ordinary differential equations to define the latent trajectories for each observation. (Sec 3.1)
These points are used to discretize the layer output, and can correspond to either the input time points (i.e., $\bm{\omega}$ ) or task-specific time points. (Sec 3.2, Sampling Process)
To generate irregular time series data, we follow the setting of  [30] to randomly drop either 30%, 50% or 70% observations. (Sec 4.2)
papers.code_url_and_license: No link in the arXiv HTML. It is commonly distributed in microsoft/SeqML, whose root LICENSE is MIT; the ContiFormer subfolder was not verified.
papers.notes: A task-appropriate 'resampling-free attention' baseline, too expensive for long signals (EigenWorms L=17,984). All three components rely on per-observation tokens.

papers.title: Recurrent Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series with Missing Values (GRU-D)
papers.sections_read: 2; 2.1; 2.2 (Eqs 1-6 and GRU-D updates)
papers.mechanism: A GRU with trainable decays computed from the time since the last observation. Input decay moves a missing value from its last observation toward the empirical mean. Hidden-state decay is applied before each update. The mask is fed to the gates.
papers.input_reconstruction: None. Missing entries are imputed by a decayed forward-fill toward the mean (Eq. 5), and masks are kept.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every time step or observation (GRU gates, tanh, decay nonlinearity).
papers.time_handling: The time interval delta_t since the last observation feeds exp(-max(0, W delta + b)) decays. The time step is the sequence index.
papers.invariance_claim: None.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Naturally missing clinical data (PhysioNet, MIMIC-III). No controlled refinement or downsampling.
evidence_quotes: it is known that imputing the missing value with mean or forward imputation cannot distinguish whether missing values are imputed or truly observed. (Sec 2.1)

we use an input decay $\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{\boldsymbol{x}}$ to decay it over time toward the empirical mean (which we take as a default configuration), instead of using the last observation as it is. (Sec 2.2)
This is implemented by decaying the previous hidden state $\boldsymbol{h}_{t-1}$ before computing the new hidden state $\boldsymbol{h}_{t}$ (Sec 2.2)
papers.reported_numbers: Not extracted from this paper. From other papers: CharacterTrajectories (NCDE Table 1) and UEA-drop averages in ContiFormer of 0.7284/0.7117/0.6725 at 30/50/70%; Latent ODE Human Activity (Localization) 0.806; mTAN Table 2 Human Activity 0.862; S7 Table 5 'HAR' (person activity) 83.57.
papers.code_url_and_license: https://github.com/PeterChe1990/GRU-D (not linked in the arXiv HTML), MIT.
papers.notes: The standard missing-observation baseline. It explicitly separates observed values from imputed ones through masks, which is a prior version of the 'measured vs non-measured value' distinction. It has no continuous path and applies a per-observation nonlinear update.

papers.title: Latent ODEs for Irregularly-Sampled Time Series (ODE-RNN / Latent ODE)
papers.sections_read: 3.1 (Algorithm 1); 3.2 (partial); 3.3; 3.5; 4.5 (Tables 6-7)
papers.mechanism: ODE-RNN evolves the hidden state with a neural ODE between observations and applies an RNNCell jump at each observation. Latent ODE is a VAE with an ODE-RNN encoder and an ODE decoder from z0. An optional Poisson-process likelihood models the observation times.
papers.input_reconstruction: None. Observations enter as discrete RNN updates.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: The RNNCell at every observation, plus the neural ODE vector field evaluated continuously by the solver between observations.
papers.time_handling: Time dependence comes only implicitly through ODE integration over (t_{i-1}, t_i). There is no explicit dt input.
papers.invariance_claim: None.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Subsampled MuJoCo, PhysioNet (naturally irregular), and the Human Activity (Localization) per-time-point classification task.
evidence_quotes: We define the state between observations to be the solution to an ODE [...] and then at each observation, update the hidden state using a standard RNN update (Sec 3.1)
Our model does not explicitly depend on $t$ or $\Delta_{t}$ when updating the hidden state, but does depend on time implicitly through the resulting dynamical system. (Sec 3.1)
The fact that a measurement was made at a particular time is often informative about the state of the system (Che et al., 2018). (Sec 3.3)
The data consists of 3d positions of tags attached to their belt, chest and ankles (12 features in total). (Sec 4.5)
papers.reported_numbers: Human Activity (UCI Localization Data for Person Activity, 6554 sequences x 211 points, 7 classes, per-time-point), Table 7: Latent ODE (ODE enc) 0.846+-0.013, Latent ODE (RNN enc) 0.835, ODE-RNN 0.829+-0.016, GRU-D 0.806, RNN-Decay 0.800, RNN-dt 0.797. PhysioNet AUC: ODE-RNN 0.833, Latent ODE 0.829. (This is not UCI-HAR smartphone.) On EigenWorms with 50% drop, RFormer reports ODE-RNN at 37.61.
papers.code_url_and_license: github.com/YuliaRubanova/latent_ode (not linked in the arXiv HTML), MIT.
papers.notes: A prototypical per-observation nonlinear update: every inserted virtual knot adds one RNNCell jump. The Poisson likelihood treats the fact of observation as informative, the opposite of the virtual-knot notion.

papers.title: Modeling Irregular Time Series with Continuous Recurrent Units (CRU)
papers.mechanism: A neural encoder maps each observation to a latent observation and its noise. A continuous-discrete Kalman filter with a linear SDE latent then predicts in closed form between observations (matrix exponential) and applies a Bayesian update at each observation. A locally linear transition matrix is a softmax-weighted mix of basis matrices computed from the posterior mean. A decoder produces outputs per observation.
papers.input_reconstruction: None. Observations are treated as discrete noisy measurements, and there is no input path between them.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every observation: encoder f_theta(x_t), the transition-weight network w_psi(mu_t+), and decoder g_phi.
papers.time_handling: Exact closed-form latent propagation over the elapsed time t - tau(t) (linear SDE mean and covariance).
papers.invariance_claim: None: it claims 'principled' handling of irregular times. By my analysis, a virtual interpolated point would add a Kalman update and shrink the posterior covariance, so the representation changes.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Irregularly sampled pendulum images, USHCN climate, PhysioNet interpolation/extrapolation, and partial observability.
evidence_quotes: At each time point $t\in\mathcal{T}$ , the latent observation $\mathbf{y}_{t}$ and its elementwise latent observation noise $\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{t}^{\mathrm{obs}}$ are produced by a neural network encoder $f_{\theta}$ (Sec 3.1, Eq. 3)
It is governed by the SDE in Eqn. 1, which has an analytical solution for linear, time-invariant systems as considered here. (Sec 3.2.1)

The weighting coefficients $\alpha^{(k)}_{t}$ for $k\in\{1...K\}$ are obtained from the current posterior mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{t}^{+}$ by a neural network $w_{\psi}$ with softmax output (Sec 3.4.1)
papers.reported_numbers: Pendulum MSE x1e-3 (from S5 Table 9): CRU 4.63 (1.07), f-CRU 6.16. RFormer Table 19 (synthetic sine classification, L=100) at 30/50/70/85% drop: CRU (LSD=20) 99.6/94.7/78.6/57.3 vs RFormer 98.6/97.8/96.1/85.5.
papers.notes: The linear latent propagation between observations is exact, which is the same algebra an exact SSM stem uses, but the input is a measurement update, not an integrated input path, and the nonlinearity sits on every observation.

papers.title: Neural Flows: Efficient Alternative to Neural ODEs
papers.sections_read: 2; 2.1 (ResNet, GRU and coupling flows); 2.2; 3.1 (encoder, smoothing, filtering); 4 (dataset list, grep)
papers.mechanism: Parameterizes the ODE solution curve F(t, x0) directly with invertible networks conditioned on time, replacing ODESolve in ODE-RNN, GRU-ODE-Bayes and LSTM-based encoders.
papers.input_reconstruction: None. Observations still enter as discrete RNN/GRU updates.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every observation (GRUCell/LSTM update), plus a flow network evaluated once per inter-observation interval.
papers.time_handling: Elapsed time is passed into the flow F(t, .) through time embeddings phi(t).
papers.invariance_claim: None.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Irregular benchmarks: Activity (Localization), PhysioNet, MuJoCo, MIMIC-III/IV, plus TPP and density tasks. No refinement or downsampling sweep.
evidence_quotes: they evolve the hidden state ${\bm{h}}(t)$ with an ODE, until they observe new ${\bm{x}}_{t_{1}}$ at time $t_{1}$ , when they use Equation 3 to update it (Sec 2.1)
Note that GRU flow (Equation 5) acts as a replacement to ODESolve in Equation 4. (Sec 2.1)
Unlike [16], which needs to solve the ODE for every observation, our method only needs a single pass through the network per observation. (Sec 3.1, Filtering)

papers.title: Oscillatory State-Space Models (LinOSS)
papers.sections_read: Fig. 1 caption; 2.3 (implicit and IMEX discretization); 4.1 (Table 1); App C.3 (dt sensitivity); App D (grep)
papers.mechanism: Forced harmonic oscillators y'' = -A y + B u (diagonal A >= 0), discretized with implicit (IM) or IMEX schemes and run with a parallel scan. Blocks are a LinOSS layer followed by a GLU.
papers.input_reconstruction: None. Samples u_n at t_n = n dt enter the implicit/IMEX Euler steps.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every token (GLU after each LinOSS layer).
papers.time_handling: A fixed step dt (a hyperparameter; dt = 1 in all experiments). Tokens are indexed by sample, and timestamps are not used.
papers.invariance_claim: None about sampling. It proves stability and universality.
papers.grid_changes_tested: None. Only a sensitivity sweep of the dt hyperparameter from 1e-3 to 1 on regular data.

Each block is composed of a LinOSS layer (2) [...] followed by a nonlinear transformation, specifically a Gated Linear Units (Dauphin et al., 2017) (GLU) layer in our case. (Fig. 1 caption)

papers.title: Rough Transformers: Lightweight and Continuous Time Series Modelling through Signature Patching (also workshop version: Rough Transformers for Continuous and Efficient Time-Series Modelling, arXiv 2403.10288)
papers.sections_read: 2 (problem formulation, signatures); 3 (multi-view signature, Eq 8-10); 3.1 (Prop 3.1); 4.2 (Table 4); 4.3 (Table 5); App A.1 (piecewise-linear signatures, Chen); App G.1 (Tables 15, 19); public code src/UEA/main.py and src/UEA/sig_utils.py; workshop 2403.10288 Sec 3 (grep, aliasing remark)
papers.mechanism: Builds a piecewise-linear interpolation of the input, possibly with a time channel. It computes exact truncated path signatures, global S(0, t_k) and local S(t_{k-1}, t_k), over a fixed number of windows (the 'multi-view signature'), precomputed offline. A Transformer runs on these few window tokens.
papers.input_reconstruction: Piecewise-linear interpolation. The signatures of the PL path are computed exactly (closed form per segment plus Chen's relation).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: The signature map is nonlinear (polynomial) but exact on the PL path. All learned nonlinearities (attention, MLP) run on a fixed number of window tokens whose boundaries are fixed time points. In the public code each window end is snapped to the last observed index before the boundary.
papers.time_handling: Time enters as window boundaries in the original time axis (x = linspace(0, L, L)[kept indices]), with an optional time channel. The token count is independent of the number of observations.
papers.invariance_claim: Approximate, and against time reparameterization: Prop. 3.1 says T(X) is approximately T(X') for samplings of X and X o gamma, based on reparameterization invariance of signatures and continuity. It is not an exact knot-refinement claim. Robustness to random drop is shown empirically. By my analysis, with PL signatures and window boundaries fixed at physical times using interpolated endpoints, virtual knots on the PL path would leave the features exactly unchanged. The released code snaps boundaries to observations, so its invariance is only approximate.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Random drop of 30/50/70/85% of points on EigenWorms, HR and sinusoids; 15 univariate UEA datasets with drop; a 50% drop on frequency classification in the workshop version. In the public main.py, keep_indices is sampled once per run and shared by all sequences. No lossless refinement test; real downsampling only as index drop.
evidence_quotes: To project a discretized time-series $\mathbf{X}\in\mathcal{D}$ to a continuous-time object, let $\tilde{X}$ denote the piecewise-linear interpolation of $\mathbf{X}$ . (Sec 3)

The bounds of these integrals are a fixed set of time points, meaning that the sequence length of the multi-view attention mechanism is fixed and independent of the sequence length of input samples. (Sec 3.1)

Suppose $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{X}^{\prime}$ are samplings of $\widehat{X}$ and $\widehat{X}\circ\gamma$ , respectively. Then $\mathbb{T}(\mathbf{X})\approx\mathbb{T}(\mathbf{X}^{\prime})$ . (Prop. 3.1)
indices = [np.where(x < step * i)[0][-1] for i in range(1, num_windows + 1)] (code src/UEA/sig_utils.py, _compute_global_sigs)
keep_indices = sorted(random.sample(indices, int(config.random_percentage * seq_len_orig))) (code src/UEA/main.py, executed once before the epoch loop)
the drop in performance is likely due to aliasing, i.e., the sampling rate is below the Nyquist rate (workshop arXiv 2403.10288, Sec 3 frequency classification footnote)
papers.reported_numbers: EigenWorms (own protocol, 5 seeds), Table 15: full 90.24+-2.15; 30% drop 87.86+-3.28; 50% drop 87.69+-4.97; 70% drop 83.35+-2.86; 85% drop 82.74+-2.13; Transformer OOM except at 85% drop (72.45+-3.36). Table 5 (50% drop): EigenWorms RFormer 87.69, NRDE 60.68, ODE-RNN 37.61, GRU 35.90; HR RMSE RFormer 2.96. Table 19 (sine, L=100) at 30/50/70/85% drop: RFormer 98.6/97.8/96.1/85.5. TIDES Table 7 reruns RFormer on EigenWorms (r_train=0.5): 0.771/0.762/0.771/0.733/0.562 at r_test 0.1-0.9. Preprocessing for EigenWorms: 1.11 s train signatures (Table 4).
papers.code_url_and_license: https://github.com/AlvaroArroyo/RFormer. No LICENSE file found (raw main/LICENSE returns 404), so the license is unknown.
papers.notes: The highest-overlap paper in this angle. It already combines (i) an exact functional of the piecewise-linear reconstruction and (ii) a nonlinear network on a fixed set of time windows independent of the observation count, and it states approximate sampling robustness. N2 differs as follows: a linear SSM stem instead of truncated signatures (learned exponentially decaying and oscillatory kernels versus polynomial iterated integrals); state evaluated exactly at fixed physical clock times, instead of window ends snapped to observations; a formal exact invariance to virtual knots; and an explicit three-way separation of refinement, real downsampling (aliasing) and missing data. Its aliasing remark shows the authors knew dropping below Nyquist is not recoverable. It must be a named close baseline for EigenWorms drop.

papers.title: Neural Controlled Differential Equations for Irregular Time Series (Neural CDE)
papers.sections_read: 3 (definition); 3.2; 3.3; 3.4; 3.5 (intensity as a channel); 4.1 (drop protocol, Table 1 partial); 4.3; App A.3 (grep); App B remark after Def. B.12 (spline seminorm)
papers.mechanism: The hidden state solves dz = f_theta(z) dX, where X is the natural cubic spline of the (time-augmented) data, solved with Neural ODE solvers. Observation intensity can be added as a cumulative-count channel.
papers.input_reconstruction: Natural cubic spline with knots at the observation times (Sec 3). Later torchcde work uses linear and rectilinear interpolation, which was not read here.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Continuously: the vector field f_theta(z_s) is evaluated at the ODE solver's internal steps, not at the observations per se, though solver grids are often aligned with knots in practice.
papers.time_handling: Time is a channel of the control path. There are no per-observation jumps, since the data enter through dX/ds.
papers.invariance_claim: Implicit and exact in continuous time: the solution depends only on the interpolated path. Appendix B states that adding a collinear point gives the same spline, a deliberate seminorm, and that 'we would often prefer that these time series be thought of as equal', with observational intensity used to distinguish them when needed. Numerically this holds only up to solver error.
papers.grid_changes_tested: CharacterTrajectories with 30/50/70% of observations dropped at random, independently per series (the origin of the 30/50/70 protocol); PhysioNet sepsis with and without intensity; Speech Commands MFCC (regular).
evidence_quotes: Let $X\colon[t_{0},t_{n}]\to\mathbb{R}^{v+1}$ be the natural cubic spline with knots at $t_{0},\ldots,t_{n}$ such that $X_{t_{i}}=(x_{i},t_{i})$ . (Sec 3)
This is only a seminorm as for example $((0,0),(2,2))$ and $((0,0),(1,1),(2,2))$ have the same natural cubic spline interpolation. (App B, remark after Def. B.12)
it is a deliberate choice not to: we would often prefer that these time series be thought of as equal. (App B)
(And if it they are not equal, then first augmenting with observational intensity as in the main paper should distinguish them.) (App B)
The observations to drop are selected uniformly at random and independently for each time series. (Sec 4.1)
Previous work on Neural ODEs for time series, for example [ 13 ] , has interrupted the ODE to make updates at each observation. (Sec 3.4)
papers.reported_numbers: Speech Commands (10 classes, MFCC, L=161): NCDE 89.8+-2.5%. CharacterTrajectories drop accuracies exist in Table 1 but were not fully extracted. From other papers: EigenWorms (Walker protocol) NCDE 75.0+-3.9; UEA-drop averages in ContiFormer Table 3 of 0.7142/0.6929/0.6753 at 30/50/70%.
papers.notes: Central prior art for N2's conceptual claim. NCDE already argues that a model defined on the interpolated path should treat added collinear knots as the same series, and it separates observation intensity as an extra channel. N2 must present its invariance as an efficient, closed-form (solver-free) and fixed-clock realization, not as a new principle. Log-NCDE, NRDE and SLiCE (NCDE descendants that decouple recurrent steps from the observation count) are covered by the NCDE/rough-path angle and were not re-read here.

papers.mechanism: A ContiFormer variant: per-observation keys and values are damped, driven harmonic oscillators with closed-form solutions. The query is a least-squares sinusoidal fit of the interpolation. Attention integrals are closed form, with softmax over observations i <= j.
papers.input_reconstruction: A least-squares sinusoidal expansion for the query, replacing the cubic spline. Keys and values are per-observation oscillators.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Softmax over observations and FFN at observation times, so per observation.
papers.time_handling: Continuous time through the closed-form oscillator trajectories between t_i and t_j (normalized time).
papers.invariance_claim: None about sampling. It claims universal approximation of ContiFormer attention and an E(3)-equivariance discussion.
papers.grid_changes_tested: States the UEA 30/50/70% random-drop setting. The long-context table reuses the RFormer benchmark numbers.
evidence_quotes: We model keys and values as damped, driven oscillators and expand the query in a sinusoidal basis up to a suitable number of modes. (Abstract)
We expand the interpolation function in the oscillator basis up to a suitable number of modes and obtain the coefficients $A_{k}$ , $B_{k}$ by a least-squares fit. (Sec 3, Query)
softmax over $i\leq j$ to get weights $w_{i,h}(t_{j})$ (Sec 6)

readers.angle_summary:
1) No paper in this angle tests lossless knot refinement of the same reconstructed path. All reported grid changes fall into three kinds. (a) Random index drop: the 30/50/70% protocol from NCDE, reused by ContiFormer and RFormer; RFormer adds 85%; TIDES trains at 50% and tests r_test 0.1-0.9. (b) Naturally irregular data (PhysioNet, MIMIC, the Localization 'Human Activity' set, pendulum). (c) Real downsampling by naive decimation with Delta rescaling (S5 and Liquid-S4, Speech Commands 16 kHz to 8 kHz). None separates virtual knots from real measurements, apart from the conceptual remarks listed in point 3.

2) Nonlinear updates per observation or token are universal among the SSM and RNN baselines:
- per token: TIDES (input-dependent Re(Lambda), B, C plus GELU/GLU), S5 (GELU gate), S7, LinOSS (GLU), Liquid-S4 (sample products);
- per observation: GRU-D, ODE-RNN/Latent ODE, CRU (encoder, Kalman update, transition weights), Neural Flows;
- softmax over observations: ContiFormer, OsciFormer;
- softmax or normalized kernel over observations, which makes them density dependent: mTAN, IP-Nets.

TIDES and S5 integrate a ZOH-held input exactly with physical Delta. They claim Delta extrapolation or rescaling, not refinement invariance. My analysis, not claimed by the papers: a single ZOH-exact layer is invariant to a knot inserted on the ZOH path with the held value, but the per-token nonlinearity, pooling and depth break this, and a knot on a linear interpolant breaks even the first layer.

3) Closest prior art to the N2 central claim:
- **Rough Transformer (NeurIPS 2024): substantial overlap.** It computes exact signatures of the piecewise-linear interpolant over a fixed set of time windows and runs a Transformer only on those window tokens. Prop. 3.1 gives an approximate invariance, T(X) approximately equal to T(X'), under time reparameterization. The public code snaps window ends to the last observed index and uses one drop mask per run.
- **Neural CDE (NeurIPS 2020): substantial overlap.** Its representation depends only on the spline path. App. B states that ((0,0),(2,2)) and ((0,0),(1,1),(2,2)) give the same spline and 'we would often prefer that these time series be thought of as equal', and it uses an observational-intensity channel to distinguish them when needed.
- **IP-Nets and mTAN: partial overlap.** Both run a GRU on a fixed, evenly spaced reference grid, fed by a density-dependent kernel resampler; IP-Nets adds an explicit intensity channel.

So N2 cannot claim the principle ('the representation should depend only on the reconstructed path'), nor 'nonlinearity on a fixed time grid', as new. What N2 could still claim within this angle:
- a closed-form linear-SSM FOH stem, evaluated exactly at fixed physical clock times (interpolated endpoints, not snapped);
- a stated exact invariance to virtual knots, with numerical verification;
- an explicit three-way separation: refinement, then real downsampling with its aliasing limits (RFormer's workshop version already attributes a drop to aliasing below Nyquist), then missing data;
- a cost comparison.

Analytic caution for the NO_GO criterion: resampling the linear interpolant onto a fixed grid, then any backbone, is also exactly invariant to virtual knots on that interpolant. The mandatory resampling baseline therefore shares N2's refinement invariance. Any N2 advantage must come from integrating information between clock ticks (anti-aliasing and no point-sampling loss) or from behavior under real downsampling and missing data, not from refinement invariance itself.

readers.angle: Exact discretization of linear SSMs for piecewise-linear inputs (first-order hold / triangle hold), phi-functions (exponential integrators, phi_1/phi_2 small-argument cancellation), and their use in deep SSMs (S4/S4D/S5/LRU/Mamba/Mamba-3, LS4, FlowState, irregular-time SSMs), plus canonical sources for (a) FOH exactness and semigroup/refinement invariance, (b) stable phi_2 evaluation, (c) Groenwall/variation-of-constants perturbation bounds, (d) h^2/8 linear-interpolation error, (e) aliasing under decimation. Adjacent 'exact functional of the piecewise-linear path + nonlinear processing on a window grid' models (NCDE/NRDE/Log-NCDE/Rough Transformer) were also checked because they share the same structure.
readers.angle_summary:
What is STANDARD and must be cited, not claimed:
(a) FOH is exact for piecewise-linear inputs. Sources: Franklin-Powell-Workman, Digital Control of Dynamic Systems 3e, Sec. 6.3.2 'A Non-Causal First-Order-Hold Equivalent: The Triangle-Hold Equivalent'; MATLAB c2d('foh') docs ('exact match ... for piecewise linear inputs', also called 'ramp-invariant'); Hochbruck & Ostermann 2010, Acta Numerica, Sec. 2.2. In H&O Example 2.6 the s=2, c=(0,1) exponential quadrature is named the 'exponential trapezoidal rule', with weights phi_1-phi_2 and phi_2. That is exactly the FOH. H&O Theorem 2.7 / Corollary 2.8 bound the error by sum_j h_j^2 times the integral of ||f''||, which is zero for piecewise-linear f. The semigroup property is H&O eq. 2.4. Van Loan 1978 covers block-exponential evaluation. Refinement invariance for knots inserted on linear segments follows at once from exactness plus the flow property. No SSM paper states it as a theorem. Kidger et al. 2020 (NCDE, Remark B.13) do say that inserting a collinear point leaves the interpolant unchanged, and they deliberately treat the two series as equal. Caveat: ZOH is just as exactly invariant under refinements that keep its own staircase path. So any invariance must be stated relative to the reconstruction operator.
(b) phi-function cancellation for small arguments. Sources: Higham ASNA 2e, Sec. 1.14.1 'Computing (e^x-1)/x'; Kassam & Trefethen 2005, Sec. 2 (Table 2.1; Cox-Matthews use a Taylor cutoff; K&T use a contour integral); H&O Sec. 4.
(c) Perturbation bounds via variation of constants plus exponential stability. Canonical: Gronwall 1919, Bellman 1943, H&O Theorem 2.7. FlowState v3 (Jun 2026) Prop. B.3 already proves the two-rate ZOH mismatch bound ||B||M/alpha (1-e^{-alpha T}) max(Delta, Delta') and gives a multi-layer recursion. FSSM gives FOH-vs-ZOH cumulative error bounds.
(d) The h^2/8 |x''| bound for linear interpolation: de Boor, A Practical Guide to Splines, Ch. III eq. (2).
(e) Aliasing under decimation: Shannon/Nyquist; Oppenheim-Schafer DTSP Sec. 4.6.1 (section title verified only through search snippets). Deep-SSM precedents: S4ND Sec. 4.2 (aliasing when resolution changes; bandlimiting); SS-NO Theorem 4.1 (explicit aliasing term). S4 and S5 build their 8 kHz test sets by naive decimation, so 'dt-rescaling' results mix refinement effects with real downsampling.
FOH already used in deep SSMs:
- FSSM (ICASSP 2025) derives the exact FOH coefficients for selective Mamba with variable Delta_n (eq. 5). It then implements Taylor truncations, and its Delta is input-dependent.
- Beyond-ZOH (arXiv 2604.20606) benchmarks 'FOH' in Vision Mamba using a one-term formula.
- Mamba-3 (ICLR 2026) 'exponential-trapezoidal' is not exact FOH: its weights are lambda-weighted and Delta-scaled, with lambda data-dependent. The name collides with H&O's exact rule.
- S4 (bilinear) and S4D/S5/LRU/LS4/FlowState/TIDES/S2P2 (ZOH) all apply nonlinearities at every token.
Closest structural prior to N2's combination, which N2 must cite and set itself apart from:
- Rough Transformer (NeurIPS 2024): exact signatures of the piecewise-linear interpolant over 'a fixed set of time points', then a nonlinear Transformer on that fixed window grid. It claims only approximate invariance (Prop. 3.1). Its code snaps window boundaries to observation indices.
- NRDE / Log-NCDE: exact log-signatures over intervals r_i decoupled from the data, with the nonlinear vector field evaluated on the r_i grid. In practice r_i is set to a fixed number of observations.
If r_i were fixed in physical time, these models would already be exactly knot-refinement invariant.
Not found in this angle (possibly N2-specific; other angles should confirm):
1. An explicit exact-invariance theorem for a deep network whose nonlinearities read the stem only at clock times, including the FOH partial-interval query rule.
2. A minimal counterexample showing that per-observation nonlinearities break invariance even with exact per-layer ZOH/FOH, because a nonlinearity does not commute with interpolation. FlowState B.1 instead asserts that pointwise ops 'do not introduce additional temporal discretization error'. S2P2 B.4 only notes that inputs to deeper layers vary within intervals.
3. A protocol separating virtual knots, real downsampling and missing observations.
No HAR or PDM numbers were found in this angle.

papers.title: Exponential integrators
papers.sections_read: Sec.1 Introduction (part); Sec.2.1 Preliminaries (semigroup eq. 2.4); Sec.2.2 Linear problems; exponential quadrature (eqs. 2.7-2.18, Lemma 2.4, Examples 2.5-2.6, Theorem 2.7, Corollary 2.8); Sec.4 Implementation issues (intro), Sec.4.5 Hints on mathematical software
papers.mechanism: Variation-of-constants for u'+Au=f; approximate f inside the integral by its Lagrange interpolation polynomial at nodes c_i. The resulting weights are combinations of the entire functions phi_k(z)=int_0^1 e^{(1-theta)z} theta^{k-1}/(k-1)! dtheta. With s=2, c1=0, c2=1 the 'exponential trapezoidal rule' has weights b1=phi_1-phi_2 and b2=phi_2, which is exactly the FOH / triangle-hold discretization.
papers.input_reconstruction: Polynomial (Lagrange) interpolation of the forcing at quadrature nodes. For s=2, c=(0,1) this is linear interpolation between step endpoints (FOH).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: N/A for linear problems (Sec.2.2). For semilinear problems, at stage/step points of the integrator.
papers.time_handling: Arbitrary variable step sizes h_n; the error constant is independent of the step-size sequence.
papers.invariance_claim: No invariance claim. Exactness follows from the Theorem 2.7 error bound, which vanishes when f^{(p)}=0 on every step (p=2 for linear f). The semigroup property is eq. 2.4.
papers.grid_changes_tested: None (analysis for arbitrary step sequences).
evidence_quotes: A first scheme is obtained by approximating the function f within the integral by its interpolation polynomial in certain non-confluent quadrature nodes c1,...,cs. (Sec.2.2, eq. 2.9)

Example 2.6. For s = 2 we obtain the weights b1(z) = c2/(c2-c1) phi1(z) - 1/(c2-c1) phi2(z), b2(z) = -c1/(c2-c1) phi1(z) + 1/(c2-c1) phi2(z). The choice c1 = 0 and c2 = 1 yields the exponential trapezoidal rule.
||un - u(tn)|| <= C sum_{j=0}^{n-1} h_j^p int_{tj}^{tj+1} ||f^(p)(tau)|| dtau ... with a constant C that depends on T, but is independent of the chosen step size sequence. (Theorem 2.7)
These functions satisfy phi_k(0) = 1/k! and the recurrence relation phi_{k+1}(z) = (phi_k(z) - phi_k(0))/z, phi_0(z) = e^z. (eq. 2.11)
This operator has the properties of a semigroup, namely e^{-0A} = I and e^{-tA}e^{-sA} = e^{-(t+s)A}, t,s >= 0. (eq. 2.4)
papers.reported_numbers: None.
papers.code_url_and_license: N/A (points to EXPINT, phipm, Expokit, SPARSKIT in Sec.4.5)
papers.notes: This is the canonical citation for (a) FOH exactness via phi_1/phi_2 weights, for the semigroup property, and for error bounds of type (c). Naming warning: H&O's 'exponential trapezoidal rule' is the EXACT FOH. Mamba-3's 'exponential-trapezoidal' is a different, non-exact rule. N2 should cite H&O Ex. 2.6 for the stem formula and not present phi_2 weights as new.

papers.title: Mamba-3: Improved Sequence Modeling using State Space Principles
papers.sections_read: Abstract; Sec.1; Sec.2.2 SSM preliminaries; Sec.3.1 (Table 1, 3.1.1 ZOH / exponential-Euler / exponential-trapezoidal, Prop. 1, Remarks 2-3, 3.1.2 implicit convolution); Sec.5.4; Sec.6; App. A (Prop. 5, A.2 error rate, A.3 lambda ablation)
papers.mechanism: Exponential-adjusted discretization for LTV SSMs. The transition uses a right-endpoint approximation. The state-input integral is approximated by Euler (Mamba-1/2 'exponential-Euler') or by a generalized trapezoid: h_t = e^{Delta A}h_{t-1} + (1-lambda_t)Delta e^{Delta A} B_{t-1}x_{t-1} + lambda_t Delta B_t x_t, with data-dependent lambda_t=sigma(u_t).
papers.input_reconstruction: None explicit. The trapezoid is a quadrature on the integrand e^{(tau_t-tau)A}B(tau)x(tau) using endpoint values. It is not exact for linear x (exact FOH would use phi_1-phi_2 and phi_2 weights).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every token (Delta_t, A_t, B_t, C_t, lambda_t are projections of the current token; per-token MLP/gates).
papers.time_handling: Delta_t is a learned, data-dependent step (softplus projection), not physical time.
papers.invariance_claim: None about sampling. Claims O(Delta^3) local error only if lambda_t=1/2+O(Delta_t), and reports that NOT enforcing this constraint works better.
papers.grid_changes_tested: None (language modeling).
evidence_quotes: Approximating the state-input integral in equation (16) by the general trapezoidal rule yields the recurrence ... where lambda_t in [0,1] is a data-dependent scalar (Prop. 1, Sec.3.1.1)

This is a second-order discretization of the state-input integral and its error scales as O(Delta_t^3) under standard stability assumptions, provided that the trapezoidal parameter satisfies lambda_t = 1/2 + O(Delta_t). (Remark 3)
However, our ablations indicate that not enforcing this constraint is better for empirical performance. (Remark 3)
While the Mamba-1 paper reports ZOH discretization, the implementation follows https://github.com/state-spaces/mamba/issues/129 . (Table 1 footnote)

Our new discretization framework and the two instantiations, exponential-Euler and exponential-trapezoidal, are, to the best of our knowledge, novel for structured SSMs used in deep learning. (Sec.3.1.1)

These are exactly Delta(phi_1-phi_2) and Delta phi_2. To avoid the inverse, the implementation uses Taylor truncations (FSSM: B1=B2=Delta B/2; FSSM+: first-order corrections).
papers.input_reconstruction: Linear interpolation (FOH) between adjacent tokens (noncausal: uses x_{n+1}); the last token uses the ZOH form.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every token (selective Delta_n, B_n, C_n from linear(x_n); Mamba block nonlinearities).

Noticed that the discrete parameter B1,B2 has the inverse of Delta A, in order to avoid computing the inverse, we refine the approximation by using the series representation of matrix exponential function (Sec.III-C)
FSSM is designed for tasks where the entire input sequence is available beforehand, enabling the use of correlations between adjacent tokens. (Sec.I)
Noticed that FSSM has the same order of error as SSM, but has a lower upper bound of cumulative error. (Sec.III-D)
