papers.notes: Direct prior art for 'exact FOH discretization of a (selective) deep SSM with variable step Delta_n'. N2 cannot claim to be the first FOH SSM layer. Differences: FSSM's Delta is data-dependent, its implemented coefficients are truncated Taylor approximations (not exact), and it has no sampling invariance, fixed clock, or stable small-argument phi_2 evaluation.

papers.title: Beyond ZOH: Advanced Discretization Strategies for Vision Mamba
papers.sections_read: Abstract; Sec.1; Sec.2 Related work; Sec.3.1-3.4 (ZOH, FOH eqs. 5-6, BIL, POL, HOH eq. 13, RK4, fused kernel); reference list
papers.mechanism: Swaps the ZOH in Vision Mamba's selective scan for FOH, bilinear, polynomial, higher-order hold or RK4 inside a fused CUDA kernel. The FOH is written as A_bar=e^{A Delta}, B_bar=A^{-2}(e^{A Delta}-I-A Delta)B in a one-term recurrence h_{t+1}=A_bar h_t + B_bar x_t, i.e. only the phi_2 part of the true two-term FOH.
papers.input_reconstruction: Stated: FOH = linear interpolation between samples; also polynomial and n-th order holds. The implemented FOH formula is incomplete.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every token (ViM blocks).
papers.time_handling: Fixed/selective Delta on image-patch sequences; no physical time.
papers.invariance_claim: None.
papers.grid_changes_tested: None (ImageNet-1k, CIFAR-100, ADE20K, COCO).
evidence_quotes: First-order hold (FOH) assumes that the input x(t) varies linearly between two samples, rather than being held constant as in ZOH. (Sec.3.3)
Our results demonstrate that POL and HOH yield the largest gains in accuracy at the cost of higher training-time computation. (Abstract)
The original Mamba CUDA kernel only supported ZOH. We extend the hardware-aware algorithm to support all discretization methods evaluated in this work (Sec.3.4)
papers.reported_numbers: Not recorded (vision benchmarks).
papers.notes: Further evidence that 'FOH in Mamba' is already explored (benchmark only). Cites Zhang & Chong 2007 (ICCAS) and Åström & Wittenmark for FOH.

papers.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces (S4)
papers.sections_read: Sec.2.3 discrete-time SSM; Sec.3.4 architecture; Sec.4.3 'Sampling resolution change' + Fig.5 table (SC10); App. D.5 Speech Commands note
papers.mechanism: Bilinear discretization of a DPLR SSM with step Delta; a linear mixing layer and pointwise nonlinearities between layers.
papers.input_reconstruction: Implicit uniform samples u_k=u(k Delta); bilinear (trapezoid) approximation, not exact for any hold.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every sample/token (nonlinear activations between layers).
papers.time_handling: Global step Delta; resolution change by rescaling Delta.
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical: 'automatically adapts to data sampled at different rates' via Delta change. No exactness claim.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Real downsampling: 0.5x frequency on SC10 at test time (zero-shot).
evidence_quotes: Conceptually, the inputs u_k can be viewed as sampling an implicit underlying continuous signal u(t), where u_k=u(k Delta). (Sec.2.3)
Without re-training, S4 achieves 96.3% accuracy at 0.5x the frequency on Speech Commands 10 (Fig. 6), simply by changing its internal step size Delta (Sec.4.3)
Nonlinear activation functions are also inserted between these layers. (Sec.3.4)
papers.reported_numbers: SC10 (10-class subset; Fig.5 table): S4 MFCC 93.96, raw 16k 98.32, 0.5x test 96.30. Baselines: NRDE 89.8 / 16.49 / 15.12; CKConv 95.3 / 71.66 / 65.96; Performer 80.85 / 30.77 / 30.68; ExpRNN 82.13 / 11.6 / 10.8. App. D.5: authors ask that the SC35 numbers (Table 11 of their ref [19]) be cited instead.
papers.notes: This is the canonical dt-rescaling baseline (the 'step-size rescaling' in N2's title).

papers.title: On the Parameterization and Initialization of Diagonal State Space Models (S4D)
papers.sections_read: Sec.2 background; Sec.3.1 Discretization; Sec.3.4 discretization paragraph; Sec.5.1 ablation summary
papers.mechanism: Diagonal SSM with bilinear or ZOH discretization; the Vandermonde kernel is decoupled from the discretization choice.
papers.input_reconstruction: Uniform samples; ZOH (exact for staircase) or bilinear.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every token (S4 block).
papers.time_handling: Global Delta.
papers.invariance_claim: None beyond inheriting S4's rate change. Notes that better integration rules (e.g. trapezoid) may exist.
papers.grid_changes_tested: SC 8 kHz zero-shot (numbers reproduced in S5 Table 8).
evidence_quotes: In discrete time, we view an input sequence u0,u1,... as uniformly-spaced samples from an underlying function u(t) and must approximate this integral. (Sec.3.1)
For example, it is well-known that simple rules like the Trapezoid rule [18] can dramatically reduce numerical integration error when the function has bounded second derivative. (Sec.3.1)
Different discretizations (Section 3.1) do not make a noticeable difference (Sec.5.1)
papers.reported_numbers: SC35 16 kHz / 8 kHz zero-shot (as reported in S5 Table 8): S4D-LegS 95.83 / 91.08; S4D-Inv 96.18 / 91.80; S4D-Lin 96.25 / 91.58.
papers.notes: Records that ZOH vs bilinear barely matters on standard (fixed-grid) tasks. FOH is not considered.

papers.title: Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling (S5)
papers.sections_read: Sec.2.1; Sec.3.2 (ZOH eq. 6); Sec.6.2 Speech; Sec.6.3 Variable observation interval; App. A (JAX discretize); App. F.2-F.3; App. G.1 architecture
papers.mechanism: MIMO diagonal SSM, ZOH with a learnable vector Delta and a parallel scan. Irregular sampling is handled by passing a per-step Delta_t. Nonlinearity after each layer: GELU(y_k) * sigma(W GELU(y_k)).
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH (piecewise constant).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every observation/token.
papers.time_handling: dt as step size (per-step Delta_t for irregular data); global rescaling of Delta for a new rate.
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical zero-shot transfer to a new sampling rate by rescaling Delta. No exactness claim.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Real downsampling (SC 16 kHz to 8 kHz by naive decimation, zero-shot); irregular observation times (pendulum); ablations S5-drop (Delta=1) and S5-append (dt as a channel).
evidence_quotes: As S4 and S5 methods are parameterized in continuous-time, these models can be applied to datasets with different sampling rates without the need for re-training, simply by globally re-scaling the timescale parameter Delta by the ratio between the new and old sampling rates. (Sec.6.2)
Last column indicates 0-shot testing at 8kHz (constructed by naive decimation). (Table 2 caption)
S5 does so by supplying a different Delta_t value to the discretization at each step. (Sec.6.3)
u'_k = GELU(y_k) (elementwise) sigma(W * GELU(y_k)) (App. G.1)
papers.reported_numbers: SC35 test accuracy, 16 kHz / 8 kHz zero-shot (naive decimation), mean of 3 seeds: S5 96.52 (0.16) / 94.53 (0.10); S4-LegS 96.08 / 91.32; S4-FouT 95.27 / 91.59; Liquid-S4 96.78 / 90.00; ConvNet 95.51 / 07.26; InceptionNet 61.24 / 05.18.
papers.notes: This is the per-observation-nonlinearity plus physical-dt design that N2's counterexample targets. The 8 kHz test mixes true decimation with possible aliasing, so it is not a lossless-refinement test.

papers.title: FlowState: Sampling-Rate-Equivariant Time-Series Forecasting
papers.sections_read: Abstract; Sec.3 (3.1 SSM encoder, 3.2 FBD, 3.3 Delta scaling); Sec.4 Sampling-Rate Equivariance; App. B.1 formal analysis (Assumptions B.1-B.2, Prop. B.3, pointwise ops, FBD, end-to-end bound, multi-layer remark); App. B.2 (part)
papers.mechanism: S5-style ZOH SSM encoder with an output gate and an MLP per layer, plus a functional-basis (Legendre) decoder. Encoder and decoder Deltas are scaled by factors s_Delta to match the sampling rate.
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH, stated explicitly: u_tilde(t)=u(floor(t/Delta)Delta).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every sample (output gate, residual, norm, MLP 'act independently at each time step').
papers.time_handling: dt rescaling: Delta_bar = s_Delta * Delta, with separate encoder and decoder factors.
papers.invariance_claim: APPROXIMATE equivariance. Single layer: ||s^(Delta)(T)-s^(Delta')(T)|| <= ||B||M/alpha (1-e^{-alpha T}) max(Delta, Delta') for Lipschitz input and exponentially stable A (Prop. B.3). End-to-end O(max Delta); multi-layer recursion E_l <= L_l E_{l-1} + C_l max(Delta, Delta').
papers.grid_changes_tested: Real rate changes: ETT1m vs ETT1h (subsampled) context, unseen sampling rates in GIFT-Eval. No lossless refinement test.
evidence_quotes: for a sampling interval Delta>0, the continuous input is replaced by the piecewise-constant reconstruction (App. B.1, eq. 19)
The discretized SSM is by definition exactly equivalent to the sampled solution of the continuous-time system driven by u^(Delta) (Åström and Wittenmark, 2013). (App. B.1)

These operations act independently at each time step and therefore do not introduce additional temporal discretization error. They may, however, amplify or attenuate the mismatch produced by the SSM state. (App. B.1, pointwise operations)
Therefore, FlowState is approximately sample-rate equivariant, with an approximation error vanishing as max{Delta,Delta'} -> 0. (Sec.4)
A full multi-layer proof requires tracking both the propagated mismatch from previous layers and the fresh ZOH discretization error introduced at each subsequent SSM layer. (App. B.1 remark)
papers.reported_numbers: Not recorded here (GIFT-Eval; qualitative ETT1m/ETT1h figures). No HAR/EigenWorms/SC.
papers.notes: This is the main 'dt-only rescaling' comparator, and it already contains the variation-of-constants perturbation bound (fact c). N2 must cite Prop. B.3 rather than re-derive it as new. Key contrast: FlowState's claim that pointwise ops add no temporal error is exactly what N2's counterexample disputes across layers, because a nonlinearity does not commute with interpolation and the next layer's ZOH reconstruction depends on the grid.

papers.title: Deep Latent State Space Models for Time-Series Generation (LS4)
papers.sections_read: Sec.3.1 SSM preliminaries; Sec.4 method (4.1-4.4, pseudo-code); grep of experiments for irregular/interpolation
papers.mechanism: VAE whose prior, generative and inference blocks are S4-style SSMs, computed as FFT convolutions, with GELU/LayerNorm per step.
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH ('signals are constant during the sampling interval'); mentions the bilinear estimate of e^{A Delta}.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every time step (GELU after each SSM block).
papers.time_handling: Uniform Delta (a convolution kernel requires a uniform grid).
papers.invariance_claim: None.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Interpolation/extrapolation on PhysioNet/USHCN (missing values), not grid refinement.
evidence_quotes: where A_bar=e^{A Delta}, B_bar=A^{-1}(e^{A Delta}-I)B with the assumption that signals are constant during the sampling interval. (Sec.3.1)
which can be compactly denoted, with a final GELU non-linearity, as (Sec.4.1, eq. 8)
papers.reported_numbers: Not recorded.
papers.notes: Checked because of the 'LS4' hint. It uses no FOH and has no sampling-rate mechanism beyond uniform ZOH.

papers.title: HiPPO: Recurrent Memory with Optimal Polynomial Projections
papers.sections_read: Sec.2.4 discretization; Sec.3 timescale robustness (Prop. 3); Sec.4.2 timescale robustness experiments (Table 2); App. B.3 ODE discretization (Euler, backward Euler, bilinear, GBT, ZOH, LegS step-size invariance, ablation)
papers.mechanism: Online polynomial projection ODEs. HiPPO-LegS dc/dt = (1/t)Ac + (1/t)Bf is timescale-equivariant. Discretized by the generalized bilinear transform (GBT); ZOH is described as a closed form for constant input.
papers.input_reconstruction: Implicit f(k Delta t)=f_k; GBT/bilinear used in experiments; ZOH defined for constant input between steps.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every step (HiPPO memory inside an RNN cell with gates/nonlinearity).
papers.time_handling: Adaptive Delta t from timestamp differences for missing or irregular data. The LegS recurrence is independent of Delta t.
papers.invariance_claim: EXACT continuous-time dilation equivariance for LegS (Prop. 3). Its GBT discrete recurrence does not depend on Delta t. This is invariance to time scaling, not to knot refinement.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Character Trajectories: test sampling rate changed (100 Hz to 200 Hz and back), timestamp scaling, missing values up/down-sampling.
evidence_quotes: Formally, the HiPPO-LegS operator is timescale-equivariant: dilating the input f does not change the approximation coefficients. (Sec.3)

Finally, we note that this provides a way to seamlessly handle timestamped data, even with missing values: the difference between timestamps indicates the (adaptive) Delta t to use in discretization (Sec.2.4)
The RHS of equation (12) is calculated in closed-form assuming constant input f between t and t+Delta t. (App. B.3, ZOH)
We highlight that this system is invariant to the discretization step size Delta t. (App. B.3, LegS)
papers.reported_numbers: Character Trajectories OOD timescale accuracy (Table 2). 100Hz->200Hz: LSTM 31.9, GRU 25.4, GRU-D 23.1, ODE-RNN 41.8, NCDE 44.7, LMU 6.0, HiPPO-LegS 88.8. 200Hz->100Hz: 28.2 / 64.6 / 25.5 / 31.5 / 11.3 / 13.1 / 90.1. Missing values upsample: 24.4 / 28.2 / 5.5 / 4.3 / 63.9 / 39.3 / 94.5. Missing values downsample: 34.9 / 27.3 / 7.7 / 7.7 / 69.7 / 67.8 / 94.9.
papers.notes: Relevant prior on exact time-scale equivariance. ZOH is cited to DeCarlo 1989 (Linear Systems). Uses no FOH. In setting (1) the sequences are variable length so models cannot detect the sampling rate.

papers.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
papers.sections_read: Sec.2 (discretization paragraph, eq. 4); Sec.3.5.2 interpretation of Delta and A; grep for resolution/ZOH
papers.mechanism: Selective SSM. Delta, B, C are functions of the current token. ZOH formula stated (the implementation uses exponential-Euler per Mamba-3).
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH as stated; exponential-Euler in the implementation.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every token (selection projections, softplus Delta, gated MLP block).
papers.time_handling: Delta is a learned, input-dependent step, not physical time.
papers.invariance_claim: Mentions only that discretization 'can endow' resolution invariance, citing S4ND. No claim for Mamba itself.
papers.grid_changes_tested: None relevant.
evidence_quotes: Discretization has deep connections to continuous-time systems which can endow them with additional properties such as resolution invariance (Nguyen et al., 2022) and automatically ensuring that the model is properly normalized (Sec.2)
mechanically, a large Delta resets the state h and focuses on the current input x, while a small Delta persists the state and ignores the current input. (Sec.3.5.2)
papers.reported_numbers: None relevant.
papers.notes: Archetype of per-observation nonlinear selection. Inserting virtual knots changes the token count and hence the state, even with exact per-step integration.

papers.title: Resurrecting Recurrent Neural Networks for Long Sequences (LRU)
papers.sections_read: Sec.2 (S4 recurrence, ZOH paragraph); Sec.4 discussion 'Discretization changes initialization spectrum' / 'Discretization performs normalization'
papers.mechanism: Diagonal linear RNN parameterized directly (lambda = exp(-exp(nu)+i theta)) with no continuous-time discretization; argues the ODE view is unnecessary for LRA performance.
papers.input_reconstruction: None (discrete). Describes ZOH as exact under a piecewise-constant input assumption.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every token (MLP/GLU between layers).
papers.time_handling: Fixed index grid; no dt.
papers.invariance_claim: None.
papers.grid_changes_tested: None.
evidence_quotes: Under the assumption that u_ct is constant in between timestamps (which can be thought of as a modeling assumption), this numerical integration is exact (Jacquot, 2019). (Sec.2)
suggesting that the ODE discretization viewpoint (which induces parameter sharing) is not necessary to achieve S4 performance. (Sec.4)
papers.reported_numbers: EigenWorms 87.8+-2.8 (as reproduced in RFormer/TIDES tables from Walker et al. 2024).
papers.notes: Useful citation for ZOH exactness (Jacquot 2019, Modern Digital Control Systems). Its discrete-only design has no rate mechanism, so it is a natural 'no exact stem' ablation analogue.

papers.title: S4ND: Modeling Images and Videos as Multidimensional Signals Using State Spaces
papers.sections_read: Sec.3 Discretization; Sec.4.2 Resolution Change and Bandlimiting; Sec.5.3; App. B.3.1
papers.mechanism: Multidimensional S4. Resolution change is done by rescaling Delta. To avoid aliasing, basis modes whose frequency exceeds a Nyquist-type cutoff (hyperparameter alpha) are masked.
papers.input_reconstruction: Uniform samples; standard discretization rules applied to the kernel.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every pixel/token (between layers).
papers.time_handling: dt (Delta) rescaling by the relative resolution change.
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical zero-shot resolution change; explicitly acknowledges aliasing when changing resolution.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Train at low/mid resolution, test at base (upsampling direction), CIFAR-10 and CelebA; progressive resizing.
evidence_quotes: For inputs given at different resolutions, the model can then simply change its Delta value to compute the kernel at different resolutions. (Sec.3)

However, sampling rates in the spatial domain are often much lower than temporally, leading to potential aliasing when changing resolutions. A standard technique to avoid aliasing is to apply a low-pass filter to remove frequencies above the Nyquist cutoff frequency. (Sec.4.2)
theoretically, alpha=1.0 corresponds to the Nyquist cutoff if the basis functions are pure sinusoids. (Sec.4.2)
papers.reported_numbers: CIFAR-10 zero-shot: S4ND beats Conv2D by 15+ points (mid->base) and 40+ points (low->base), and FlexConv by 5+ points (mid->base) (text of Sec.5.3; table not transcribed).
papers.notes: Deep-SSM precedent for fact (e): aliasing and bandlimiting under resolution change. Cited by Mamba as the source of 'resolution invariance'.

papers.title: TIDES: Implicit Time-Awareness in Selective State Space Models
papers.sections_read: Abstract; Sec.2.1-2.3; Sec.3.1; Sec.5.1 (Table 1); Sec.5.3 Random drop; Sec.7 'A recipe for expressive irregular sequence modeling'
papers.mechanism: Diagonal SSM with ZOH (or bilinear) using the physical Delta, while Re(Lambda), B, C are input-dependent per token (selectivity moved from Delta to the decay rates).
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH (or bilinear).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every observation (input-dependent Re(Lambda), B, C projections; deep projectors).
papers.time_handling: Physical dt as step size (Delta_tilde = Delta).
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical extrapolation to out-of-distribution Delta and drop rates. No exactness claim.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Missing observations: EigenWorms random drop (train r=0.5, test r in {0.1..0.9}, original timestamps kept); Fading Flash OOD-Delta diagnostic; irregular Physiome-ODE.
evidence_quotes: The physical sampling interval Delta_k should enter the model only through the rule that converts the continuous-time generator into a discrete recurrence, where its semantics are fixed analytically rather than learned. (Sec.7)

Input-dependent Delta_tilde does not extrapolate: Mamba_S matches TIDES for r_test <= 0.7 but collapses from ~0.7 to ~0.4 at r_test=0.9; RFormer fails analogously, with its fixed signature window count baked into positional encodings. (Sec.5.3)
papers.reported_numbers: UEA Table 1 (baselines reproduced from Walker et al. 2024 / Moreno-Pino et al. 2024), EigenWorms accuracy: TIDES 85.7+-4.0, LogNCDE 85.6+-5.1, RFormer 90.3+-0.1, LRU 87.8+-2.8, S6 85.0+-16.1, S5 81.1+-3.7, Transformer OOM, NCDE 75.0+-3.9, NRDE 83.9+-7.3, Mamba 70.9+-15.8. Average over 6 UEA datasets: TIDES 66.1. EigenWorms random-drop mean accuracy: TIDES 0.739 (flat across r_test).
papers.notes: Recent nearby work: physical dt with per-token selectivity. Because nonlinear selection is applied per observation, virtual-knot insertion would still change its state, so N2's counterexample applies. Useful EigenWorms calibration and random-drop protocol.

papers.title: Deep Continuous-Time State-Space Models for Marked Event Sequences (S2P2)
papers.sections_read: Abstract; Sec.3.2-3.3 (diagonalization, ZOH update eq. 12); App. B.2 Discretization and ZOH; App. B.4 Forwards and Backwards ZOH
papers.mechanism: Stacked latent linear Hawkes layers (diagonal continuous-time SSMs with jumps at events), interleaved with position-wise nonlinearities. ZOH updates are evaluated between events and at query times for the intensity.
papers.input_reconstruction: ZOH with a choice of held value: forward (u_t) or backward (u_{t'-}).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At event times and at intensity query times (position-wise).
papers.time_handling: Physical inter-event times; intervals may end at non-event query points.
papers.invariance_claim: None. Explicitly notes ZOH is exact only in the first layer (zero input); deeper-layer inputs vary within the interval.
papers.grid_changes_tested: None (MTPP likelihood benchmarks); forward-vs-backward ZOH ablation.
evidence_quotes: For the first layer of the model, the input is zero by construction, so there is no choice to be made—in fact, since u is constant for the first layer the updates are exact. However, the input is non-zero at deeper layers, and, crucially, varies over the integration period. (App. B.4)
Note the end of the interval need not align with an event (crucial for when computing intermediate intensity values). (App. B.4)
papers.reported_numbers: Not recorded (MTPP log-likelihoods).
papers.notes: The closest statement found of the multi-layer mechanism behind N2's counterexample (deeper-layer inputs are not piecewise constant). It frames this as a modeling choice, not a grid-dependence problem.

papers.title: Stability and Discretization Error of State Space Model Neural Operators
papers.sections_read: Abstract; Sec.4 discrete framework; Theorem 4.1 + proof sketch; Sec.5.1 setup (subsampling experiments)
papers.mechanism: SSM-based neural operators (SS-NO) on periodic domains. Grid convolution is a quadrature of the continuous kernel integral. Pointwise Lipschitz activations are applied at grid points. The error recursion has an explicit aliasing term, giving a discretization error of order N^{d/2-s}.
papers.input_reconstruction: Grid samples (no interpolation for the convolution); coarse-grid states interpolated to the fine grid for comparison.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every grid point in every layer.
papers.time_handling: Uniform spatial grid of size N.
papers.invariance_claim: Approximate discretization invariance with algebraic convergence under Sobolev regularity; ISS stability.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Real downsampling (uniform stride-s subsampling of fine GRF/Burgers inputs), measured against a fine-grid reference.
evidence_quotes: split the convolution discrepancy into (i) the propagation of the current error through the discrete convolution and (ii) the pure aliasing error of replacing int_{T^d} by the grid average (Theorem 4.1 proof sketch)
We prove analytical bounds that link solution regularity to input discretization, providing a formal quantification of neural operator accuracy under real-world numerical constraints. (Abstract)
papers.reported_numbers: Relative l2 error vs resolution curves (not transcribed).
papers.notes: Shows that 'per-grid-point nonlinearity creates grid-dependent error, bounded via Lipschitz recursion plus aliasing' is already analyzed for neural operators (approximately). The N2 exactness claim is different.

papers.title: Neural Controlled Differential Equations for Irregular Time Series
papers.sections_read: Sec.3 method (time channel, initial condition); App. A.3 natural cubic splines; App. B.12-B.14 (natural cubic spline topology, Remark B.13, universal approximation)
papers.mechanism: Hidden state z solves dz = f_theta(z) dX, with X a natural cubic spline of (t_i, x_i). The neural vector field is evaluated continuously inside an ODE solver.
papers.input_reconstruction: Natural cubic spline (linear interpolation discussed in follow-ups); time included as a channel.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Continuously inside the ODE solver (solver steps, adaptive or fixed), decoupled from observation times.
papers.time_handling: Time as a channel (CDEs are otherwise reparameterization invariant).
papers.invariance_claim: Remark B.13: series that differ only by a collinear inserted point give the same spline, hence the same model output; the authors deliberately treat them as equal. Not tested; exact only up to solver error.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Random drop (30/50/70% on CharacterTrajectories); partial observation (Speech Commands MFCC, PhysioNet).
evidence_quotes: This is only a seminorm as for example ((0,0),(2,2)) and ((0,0),(1,1),(2,2)) have the same natural cubic spline interpolation. ... it is a deliberate choice not to: we would often prefer that these time series be thought of as equal. (Remark B.13)
(And if it they are not equal, then first augmenting with observational intensity as in the main paper should distinguish them.) (Remark B.13)
CDEs exhibit a tree-like invariance property [18]. What this means, roughly, is that a CDE is blind to speed at which X is traversed. (Sec.3)
papers.reported_numbers: Not transcribed (Speech Commands 35-class MFCC; CharacterTrajectories with drops).
papers.notes: Earliest explicit statement found that inserting collinear knots should leave a continuous-time model unchanged. It also proposes observational intensity to tell real measurements from virtual ones. N2 must cite this for the concept and for knot-vs-measurement.

papers.title: Neural Rough Differential Equations for Long Time Series
papers.sections_read: Sec.2.2 Log-ODE method; Sec.3 method (3.1-3.3 incl. 'Depth and Step hyperparameters'); Sec.4.1 EigenWorms (Table 1)
papers.mechanism: Piecewise-linear interpolation X of (t_i, x_i). Depth-N log-signatures of X over intervals [r_i, r_{i+1}] are computed exactly (Signatory) as preprocessing. The ODE vector field f_theta(Z)*LogSig/(r_{i+1}-r_i) is piecewise autonomous on each interval.
papers.input_reconstruction: Linear interpolation with a time channel.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: Inside the ODE solver, on intervals r_i that may be decoupled from the observation grid. In experiments r_i are fixed numbers of observations ('step').
papers.time_handling: Time as a channel; window grid r_i (formalism allows arbitrary t_0=r_0<...<r_m=t_n).
papers.invariance_claim: None explicit. States that solver steps can be decoupled from the data sampling rate.
papers.grid_changes_tested: None (step-size hyperparameter sweeps only).
evidence_quotes: The second is that as both operate in continuous time, the steps in the numerical solver may be decoupled from the sampling rate of the data (Sec.3.3)
Right: The Neural RDE utilising the log-ODE method with integration steps larger than the discretisation of the data. (Fig. 4 caption)
Recall that the depth 1 log-signature is just the increment of the path over the interval. (Sec.3.2)
papers.reported_numbers: EigenWorms (length 17,984, 6 channels incl. time; 3 repeats; Table 1). NCDE step 1: 62.4+-12.1. Step 4: ODE-RNN(folded) 35.0+-1.5, NCDE 66.7+-11.8, NRDE depth2 83.8+-3.0 (best overall), NRDE depth3 76.9+-9.2. Step 32: NCDE 64.1+-14.3, NRDE d2 67.5+-12.1, d3 75.2+-3.0. Step 128: NCDE 48.7+-2.6, NRDE d2 76.1+-5.9, d3 68.4+-8.2.
papers.code_url_and_license: https://github.com/jambo6/neuralRDEs (LICENSE not found at repo root)
papers.notes: Structurally close to N2: an exact functional of the piecewise-linear path over windows, then nonlinear dynamics on the window grid. If r_i were fixed in physical time, collinear knot insertion would leave the log-signatures, and hence the model, unchanged (Chen's identity). Not claimed or tested. N2 must cite and set itself apart from it (linear SSM stem vs signatures; physical clock; explicit exactness; knot/measurement protocol).

papers.title: Log Neural Controlled Differential Equations: The Lie Brackets Make a Difference
papers.sections_read: Sec.1-2 (NRDE background, eqs. 3-4); Sec.3 method (Log-ODE with Lie brackets, depth-1 equivalence); toy-experiment settings (grep)
papers.mechanism: Same log-ODE structure as NRDE. The vector field on each interval is built from iterated Lie brackets of the NCDE field and driven by the truncated log-signature of X over [r_i, r_{i+1}].
papers.input_reconstruction: Linear interpolation (depth-1 equivalence stated for linear X).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: In the ODE solve on each interval [r_i, r_{i+1}]; intervals set to a fixed number of observations in experiments.
papers.time_handling: Time as a channel; intervals in observation counts ('4 observations').
papers.invariance_claim: None.
papers.grid_changes_tested: None found in sections read.
evidence_quotes: NRDE and Log-NCDE take r_{i+1}-r_i to be 4 observations and the signature truncation depth N to be 2. (toy dataset setup)
Furthermore, (22) and (3) are equivalent when X is a linear interpolation. (Sec.3)
papers.reported_numbers: EigenWorms 85.6+-5.1 (as reported in RFormer/TIDES tables).
papers.notes: Important detail: in practice the 'clock' counts observations, so knot insertion would move the windows. This is the concrete difference from a fixed physical-time clock.

papers.title: Rough Transformers: Lightweight and Continuous Time Series Modelling through Signature Patching
papers.sections_read: Sec.3 (multi-view signature eq. 8, attention eqs. 9-10), Sec.3.1 incl. Prop. 3.1; Sec.4.1 long TS table; Sec.4.3 irregular; App. A.1 signatures of piecewise-linear paths/Chen; App. G.1 random drop; code src/EEG/sig_utils.py (commit 27d59ea, 2025-06-14)
papers.mechanism: Piecewise-linear interpolation of the series. Exact truncated signatures (Chen's relation) are taken globally S_{0,t_k} and locally S_{t_{k-1},t_k} at a fixed set of L_bar time points, then a Transformer and MLP run on that fixed-length sequence.
papers.input_reconstruction: Linear interpolation (optional time channel).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: On the fixed window grid t_k (L_bar points independent of input length), not at observations. In the irregular-data code, window boundaries are linspace in time but snapped to observation indices via searchsorted, and the non-overlapping variant drops the linear piece crossing each boundary.
papers.time_handling: Fixed number of windows over [0,T] (e.g. 75); time channel optional (add_time flag).
papers.invariance_claim: APPROXIMATE: Prop. 3.1 T(X) ~ T(X') for samplings of reparameterized paths (signature reparameterization invariance). No exact knot-refinement claim.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Missing observations: random drop 30/50/70/85% on EigenWorms and others; irregular univariate UEA.
evidence_quotes: The bounds of these integrals are a fixed set of time points, meaning that the sequence length of the multi-view attention mechanism is fixed and independent of the sequence length of input samples. (Sec.3.1)
Then T(X) ~ T(X'). ... Hence, the Rough Transformer is robust to irregular sampling. (Prop. 3.1 and text)
[code] steps = np.linspace(0, x.max(), num_windows + 1)[1:]; indices = [int(np.searchsorted(x, s)) - 1 for s in steps] (sig_utils.py, Signature_overlapping_irreg)
papers.reported_numbers: UEA long TS (70/15/15 re-split, baselines from Walker et al.), EigenWorms: RFormer 90.3+-0.1, LRU 87.8+-2.8, S5 81.1+-3.7, S6 85.0+-16.1, Mamba 70.9+-15.8, NCDE 75.0+-3.9, NRDE 83.9+-7.3, LogNCDE 85.6+-5.1, Transformer OOM. 50% random drop per epoch: EW RFormer 87.69, NRDE 60.68, ODE-RNN 37.61, GRU 35.90, Transformer OOM.
papers.code_url_and_license: https://github.com/AlvaroArroyo/RFormer (no LICENSE file in repo at commit 27d59ea)
papers.notes: CLOSEST prior to N2's combined structure (exact PL-path integration plus nonlinear processing on a fixed time grid). Resampling+Transformer comparisons should include it. Differences N2 can legitimately claim: a linear SSM stem (exponential memory, FOH closed form), an exact rather than approximate theorem, a query rule at clock times inside intervals rather than snapping to observations, and separation of virtual knots / downsampling / missing data. TIDES reports that RFormer collapses at 90% drop.

papers.title: Sample Rate Independent Recurrent Neural Networks for Audio Effects Processing
papers.sections_read: Abstract
papers.mechanism: Modify per-sample nonlinear RNNs (LSTM/GRU amp models) so they run approximately at other sample rates, via delay-based oversampling and fractional-delay (cubic Lagrange) interpolation of the delay line.
papers.input_reconstruction: Fractional-delay interpolation (Lagrange) of the recurrent delay line.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every audio sample (nonlinear RNN).
papers.time_handling: Sample-rate conversion factor applied to recurrent delay length.
papers.invariance_claim: Approximate sample-rate independence.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Integer and non-integer oversampling.
evidence_quotes: One limitation of such models is that they are trained on audio at a specific sample rate and therefore give unreliable results when operating at another rate. (Abstract)
we investigate several methods of modifying RNN structures to make them approximately sample rate independent, with a focus on oversampling. (Abstract)
papers.reported_numbers: None recorded.
papers.notes: Adjacent evidence that per-sample nonlinear recurrences are grid-dependent and are only approximately fixable. The follow-up arXiv 2409.15884 (undersampling via extrapolation filters) reports instability artefacts explained by linearized stability analysis.

papers.title: Interpolation Filter Design for Sample Rate Independent Audio Effect RNNs
papers.sections_read: Abstract
papers.mechanism: Fractional delay/advance filters (interpolation/extrapolation) inside the RNN feedback to run it at higher or lower rates at inference.
papers.input_reconstruction: FIR fractional-delay/extrapolation filters.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every sample.
papers.time_handling: Adjusted feedback delay length.
papers.invariance_claim: Approximate; some failure cases.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Oversampling and undersampling at inference.
evidence_quotes: RNNs have a fixed sample rate encoded in their model weights, making the sample rate non-adjustable during inference. (Abstract)
in some cases the sample rate adjustment leads to unwanted artefacts in the output signal. We analyse these failure cases through linearised stability analysis (Abstract)
papers.reported_numbers: None recorded.
papers.notes: Adjacent (audio). Supports the claim that rate adaptation of per-sample nonlinear recurrences is inherently approximate.

papers.title: Sampling-Frequency-Independent Audio Source Separation Using Convolution Layer Based on Impulse Invariant Method
papers.sections_read: Abstract
papers.mechanism: Convolution layer whose kernels come from learned analog filters, discretized by impulse invariance for any sampling frequency. Rest of the DNN unchanged.
papers.input_reconstruction: Impulse-invariant discretization (not a hold).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every sample/frame (rest of the network).
papers.time_handling: Kernel regenerated for each sampling frequency.
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical consistency at unseen sampling frequencies.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Unseen sampling frequencies in music source separation.
evidence_quotes: we propose a convolution layer capable of handling arbitrary sampling frequencies by a single DNN. (Abstract)
papers.reported_numbers: None recorded.
papers.notes: Adjacent: analog-filter linear layers adapted to the sampling rate, with per-sample nonlinearities kept. This is the audio analogue of dt-rescaling.

I keep all ratings: exact_input_integration=partial, fixed_time_nonlinearity=none, refinement_invariance_claim=partial, knot_vs_measurement_distinction=none, overall=partial. Hostile-direction check:

(a) exact_input_integration: partial, not higher. It is standard S5 exact ZOH on a uniform grid, which N2 already lists as prior work. There is no FOH/linear reconstruction, no non-uniform dt, and no explicit input path. The SSM also sees the output of a per-sample nonlinear normalizer, not the raw path. So even the first-layer linear state is not a function of the reconstructed path alone.

(b) fixed_time_nonlinearity: none. Every nonlinearity runs per input sample index. The FBD output grid (spacing set by s_Delta) is a linear readout queried on a grid. That is prior art for N2's output-query rule, not a fixed-clock nonlinearity.

(c) refinement_invariance_claim: partial, not substantial. The title claims invariance, but the body says only "similar". There is no definition, no proof and no upsampling or refinement test in v1/v2.

(d) knot_vs_measurement_distinction: none. There is no virtual-knot concept. In code (with_missing=True in the released config), NaNs are zero-filled and a mask channel is added on the uniform grid, separate from s_Delta. v1 mentions this only for CPM/MPI ("treating intermediate ones as missing", Background). A reviewer could call this an implicit missing-vs-rate split, so the record should mention it.

Record fixes:
1. The v1/v2 text does not say "ZOH" or "complex diagonal" (it writes A in R^{PxP}). This comes from the formula plus the code: a per-state trainable log_Delta vector, and a scalar s_Delta that multiplies it.

verifications.strongest_non_novelty_sentence: Sec 1 (Introduction), stated without any hedge: "The SSM encoder translates the inputs into sampling-rate invariant hidden states, while the FBD interprets them as coefficients of a functional basis, producing a continuous forecast, sampleable at any rate." A reviewer would pair it with B.1: "The only approximation relative to the original continuous signal u(t) comes from this ZOH reconstruction." Together these read as 'use a better reconstruction and you get exactness', which is the idea behind N2's stem.
verifications.corrections:
I keep all ratings as given (exact_input_integration partial, fixed_time_nonlinearity none, refinement_invariance_claim partial, knot_vs_measurement_distinction none, overall partial). I checked each in both directions.

(a) exact_input_integration = partial. FlowState integrates the linear SSM exactly, but only for a ZOH reconstruction. It has no first-order-hold (FOH) or piecewise-linear integration. A hostile point the record does not mention: suppose the inserted knots repeat the held value, so the refinement is consistent with the ZOH path. Then FlowState's first-layer state is already exactly unchanged, because exp(A*Delta/2)^2 = exp(A*Delta). The paper never says this. N2 must present 'exact integration of the reconstructed path => the linear state ignores virtual knots' as existing for ZOH, and claim only the FOH/piecewise-linear case plus what follows from it.

(b) fixed_time_nonlinearity = none. Both Eq.3 and the code evaluate the sigmoid gate, the gated MLP, the residual and the causal RevIN at every input step. The FBD is linear and reads only the final state o^N_L. Nothing is evaluated on an input-independent clock.

(c) refinement_invariance_claim = partial. The paper gives only an approximate O(max{Delta,Delta'}) upper bound. There is no exactness claim and knot refinement is never considered. However, Sec 1 calls the hidden states 'sampling-rate invariant' without qualification. The invariance framing also predates v3: v1 of Aug 2025 was titled 'FlowState: Sampling Rate Invariant Time Series Forecasting' and tested Loop Seattle subsampled from 5 to 65 min in 5-min steps. The OpenReview API search also lists two earlier related entries: R50AT6nAsM (venue 'BERT2S', title '...Sampling-Rate Invariant ... Foundation Model...') and mkOc8O6Xxa (title 'FlowState: Sampling Rate Invariant Time Series Forecasting', no venue listed).

(d) knot_vs_measurement = none. B.2 ('same underlying process, but just sampled with different rates') and Assumption B.1 (a Lipschitz u(t)) treat all samples as readings of one continuous signal. Aliasing is never discussed. Add to the record: the released granite r1 config has with_missing=True. NaNs are zero-filled and a binary mask channel is appended (code lines 694-701), and CPM appends masked future steps. So missing values are handled as masked slots on the uniform grid, which is a separate mechanism from the rate change done through s. That is not a knot-vs-measurement distinction, but N2 cannot claim to be the first to treat missing data separately from rate change.

(e) The record's note (ii) overstates the case. The multi-layer remark (Eq.49-53) already admits a 'fresh ZOH discretization error introduced at each subsequent SSM layer': the term M_l*max{Delta,Delta'}, which is the O(Delta) mismatch from re-holding per-sample outputs. The 'no additional temporal discretization error' claim covers pointwise ops at a fixed time step only (final-state comparison, Eq.34). So N2's counterexample must not be framed as refuting FlowState. What remains new for N2 is (1) a nonzero lower bound that persists even when the input path is integrated exactly and the refinement is lossless, and (2) the fact that this error vanishes once the nonlinearities move to a fixed clock. A weak point for reviewers to note: Eq.50-52 assume continuous layer-input trajectories u_{l,Delta}(t) that the discrete model never defines.

(f) Hold-convention inconsistency. Eq.1 (s_t = A_bar s_{t-1} + B_bar x_t) and the code apply B_bar to x_t at step t. That corresponds to holding x_t over the preceding interval (a ceiling convention), whereas Eq.19 uses floor. This is a one-sample shift. It does not affect FlowState's bound, but N2's exact-ZOH comparisons must fix and state the convention.

(g) Additions to grid_changes_tested. A.2 has qualitative synthetic sine tests at seasonality 8, 24 and 100 (fixed-decoder ablation); these are different signals, not the same path on a new grid. Fig.2 is also an output-rate upsampling test (1h context to 15-min forecast via s_F). D.2.3 sweeps a mismatched s; it does not change the grid.

(h) Output querying. The FBD decodes a fixed horizon in model time (prediction_length = decoder_patch_len/s in code), sampled at any Delta_F. N2's output-query rule must credit this.

(i) Metadata. arXiv comment verified: 'Proceedings of the 43rd ICML, Seoul, PMLR 306, 2026'. Versions: v1 7 Aug 2025, v2 19 Aug 2025, v3 15 Jun 2026. Licenses: the granite-tsfm LICENSE is Apache 2.0, and HF lists apache-2.0 for both ibm-granite/granite-timeseries-flowstate-r1 and ibm-research/flowstate. The ibm-research card text nevertheless says research-use / non-commercial.

(j) Prop B.3 and Eq.9 are a standard variation-of-constants ZOH bound and should be marked as existing results.

verifications.corrections:
1) ACCESS. ABSTRACT_ONLY is correct for R50AT6nAsM. However, the record leaves the mechanism fields as 'not read' even though the arXiv full texts on either side of it are openly readable. The fields below should be filled from those versions and labelled as preprint evidence, not as workshop-PDF evidence.

2) INPUT RECONSTRUCTION = ZOH. This is explicit, not just 'presumed'.
- v1, SSM Encoder: "Abar = e^{A Delta}, Bbar = A^{-1}(Abar - 1) B". This is the ZOH discretization formula, though v1 does not name it.
- v3 App. B.1 Eq. 19 names it: "the continuous input is replaced by the piecewise-constant reconstruction u~(Delta)(t)=u(t_Delta(t))".
- The grid is uniform with one global Delta per series. There is no first-order-hold, interpolation or spline reconstruction.

3) WHERE NONLINEARITY IS EVALUATED: at every input token.
- v1: "One S5 layer l consists of an S5 block, followed by an MLP."
- v3 Eq. 3 adds a per-step sigmoid output gate, h_t = c_t * gate(c_t) + D x_t.
- v3 App. B.1: "These operations act independently at each time step and therefore do not introduce additional temporal discretization error."
- So the number of nonlinear evaluations scales with the number of samples (L_eff = L/s_Delta). There is no fixed physical-time clock anywhere, so fixed_time_nonlinearity = none is confirmed.
- The only grid-free part is the linear functional basis decoder, which samples a continuous Legendre expansion at spacing Delta_F (v1 Eqs. 3-5; v3 Eqs. 4-6). That resembles an output-query rule but is not a fixed-time nonlinearity.

4) TIME HANDLING: global step-size rescaling.
- v1 Eq. 6: "Delta_bar = f(Delta, s_Delta) = s_Delta * Delta". v3 Eq. 7 uses separate factors s_Delta_E and s_Delta_F.
- The factor s_Delta comes from a seasonality heuristic, s_Delta = 24/Seasonality (v1 Temporal Scaling; v3 6.1.2 and D.2.1), with L_eff = L/s_Delta.
- There is no per-sample dt, no time channel, and no support for irregular sampling.

5) INVARIANCE CLAIM.
- v1 is approximate and empirical ('similar representations').
- v3 adds a formal but still approximate O(max{Delta, Delta'}) bound. It rests on Lipschitz input (Assumption B.1, constant M) and exponential stability (B.2). Prop. B.3, Eq. 23: ||s(T) - s'(T)|| <= (||B|| M / alpha)(1 - e^{-alpha T}) max{Delta, Delta'}.
- Per-step pointwise operations enter only through a Lipschitz constant (Eqs. 33-35). The end-to-end bound is Eq. 46, and the multi-layer recursion is E_l <= L_l E_{l-1} + C_l max{Delta, Delta'} (Eqs. 53-54).
- v3 itself notes that each later layer incurs a 'fresh ZOH mismatch' on inputs that earlier per-step layers produced. This is essentially the mechanism N2 targets, so N2 must cite it and must not claim to have discovered that per-token nonlinearities break rate consistency. Per the user's item 6, N2 must also label this exact-ZOH plus Lipschitz/Gronwall-type bound as existing work.
- None of these claims is exact, and none is specific to lossless refinement. refinement_invariance_claim = partial is confirmed.

6) GRID CHANGES TESTED: real downsampling only.
- v1: Loop Seattle, 5-minute data subsampled to 5-65 minutes in 5-minute steps.
- v3: ETT1m subsampled from 15 to 135 minutes; Fig. 2 forecasts ETT1m from an ETT1h context; App. B.2 compares cosine similarity of ETT1m and ETT1h encodings.
- Not tested: knot refinement on the same path, upsampling or interpolation, random drop, irregular sampling. 'Missing' appears only in the multi-patch inference scheme (MPI), which treats intermediate patches as missing, and in preprocessing, which splits series at NaN runs (v3 C.2).

7) knot_vs_measurement_distinction = none is confirmed. v3 App. B.2 treats subsampled data as "from the same underlying process, but just sampled with different rates", and there is no discussion of aliasing.

8) exact_input_integration: raise from none to partial, taking the hostile reviewer's position.
- FlowState's first layer is the exact solution for its own piecewise-constant reconstruction. v3 App. B.1: "The discretized SSM is by definition exactly equivalent to the sampled solution of the continuous-time system driven by u~(Delta)".
- So repeating samples is exactly lossless for layer 1 under right-hold ZOH.
- The rating does not go higher because there is no first-order-hold integration, exactness is lost after layer 1, and the paper frames ZOH as an approximation.

9) OVERALL = partial is confirmed. FlowState is the canonical dt-rescaling baseline that N2 must include, but it does not contain N2's central fixed-clock mechanism.

10) REPORTED NUMBERS. There are no HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM numbers in any version; FlowState reports forecasting only. The only nearby figures are ablations, and they are not useful for calibration: v1 Table 4, FlowState(G)-2.6M: MASE 0.733 / CRPS 0.502, and without time-scale adjustment 0.808 / 0.544. v3 Table 2, FlowState-3M (2k): 0.725 / 0.502, and without equivariance 0.799 / 0.553.

In /home/user/Sampling-Consistent-State-Space-Models-with-Fixed-Time-Nonlinearities/results/flowstate_probe.json, first window, v1.0:

- 2x ZOH sample repetition: relative forecast change 0.029.

verifications.corrections:
Four corrections to the record, plus four details worth adding.

Corrections:
1. Raise exact_input_integration from partial to substantial (hostile reading). S5 already integrates a continuous-time diagonal linear SSM in closed form (Eq. 6) over a held input, with a physical per-interval step in the pendulum branch. In pendulum-branch ssm.py the step is 'step * _timestep', with integration_timesteps = np.diff(timesteps) (train_helpers.py L328); the first token uses timestep 1. The hold is right-endpoint: u_k is held on (t_{k-1}, t_k]. By the semigroup property, this linear stem is already exactly invariant to virtual knots inserted consistently with its own piecewise-constant path. S5 never states or tests this. So the only difference from the N2 stem is hold order (ZOH vs first-order hold), and exact first-order-hold discretization is textbook control theory. Strictly, it is only 'partial', because S5 has no first-order-hold or piecewise-linear reconstruction. Also, 'implicit ZOH' in the record is wrong: the ZOH is explicit (Eq. 6), and the code also offers bilinear discretization (run_train.py: default 'zoh', choices zoh/bilinear).
2. Keep fixed_time_nonlinearity at none. Every nonlinearity runs per token:
   - the GELU/GLU after each SSM layer (App G.1; Listing 1 uses plain jax.nn.gelu; code default is half_glu1);
   - BatchNorm or LayerNorm between layers;
   - the per-image CNN encoder and per-step MLP decoder for pendulum;
   - mean pooling over the token axis (G.1), so the readout itself depends on the grid.
3. Residual connections are not stated in the paper text (grep finds no 'residual'). They exist only in code: s5/layers.py, 'x = skip + x'. Cite the code for this, not the paper.
4. Keep refinement_invariance_claim at partial. The only claim is empirical zero-shot rate transfer by rescaling Δ. It is tested only for downsampling by naive decimation with no anti-aliasing. Per G.4, only the validation and test sets are subsampled; training stays at 16 kHz, with no padding. There is no formal invariance claim and no test of refinement or upsampling. The code exposes step_rescale: 'allows for uniformly changing the timescale parameter, e.g. after training'.

Also worth adding:
5. The pendulum task is not a grid-change test. Train and test both draw 50 of 100 frames at random, i.e. real missing measurements. No trajectory is re-evaluated on a different grid at test time.
6. knot_vs_measurement_distinction stays none.
7. Numbers to add for calibration. For 'dt-only vs time-as-channel' baselines, from Table 9 (pendulum MSE x1e-3):
   - S5-drop (Δt set to 1.0): 6.68 (0.38)
   - S5-append (Δt appended as an input channel): 4.13 (0.43)

   - S4D-Lin: 96.25 / 91.58
   - S4-FouT: 95.27 / 91.59

8. The statement that FlowState builds on S5 is not evidence from S5 itself. Verify it against FlowState.

verifications.corrections:
1) RAISE refinement_invariance_claim from none to partial. The record says "The code makes none", and that is inaccurate. The code header names the paper "FlowState: Sampling Rate Invariant Time Series Forecasting" (L3). The model card says FlowState can "seamlessly adjust to all possible sampling rates" and has a "timescale invariant coefficient space". The notebook says scale_factor "allows to adjust these components to the sampling rate of the input data". A hostile reviewer will say this sampling-rate-invariance claim, by name, already covers a higher-rate (refined) version of the same signal. The claim is still only approximate and empirical: no exactness, no knot/measurement distinction, and only decimation is demonstrated. So it is partial, not substantial.

2) The other ratings stand.
- exact_input_integration = partial. FlowState uses exact closed-form ZOH with a rescaled Delta, which is an existing result. It does not integrate a first-order-hold reconstruction, so it is not refinement-invariant (see 4).
- fixed_time_nonlinearity = none. All nonlinearities act at every input index: causal RevIN, sigmoid output gate, SwiGLU/selu-sigmoid, LayerNorm. The closest analog is the FBD, a linear continuous-time readout queried at physical-time-consistent points t_k = -1 + k*s*1.95/patch. That is an output query rule, not a nonlinear update on a fixed clock. It should still be cited as prior art for N2's output query rule. get_fixed_factor maps all frequencies to a base seasonality of 24, but by Delta rescaling, not by moving computation to a clock.
- knot_vs_measurement_distinction = none. There are no timestamps, missing values are NaN mask tokens on the same grid, and decimation is handled only via scale_factor.
- overall = partial.

3) FACTUAL ERROR: the gift-flowstate branch does not "differ only in formatting". An AST/diff comparison (916 vs 963 lines) shows the encoder/decoder math is identical: S5Block, MLP, S5Layer, RevIN, FBD get_t/get_kernel. FlowStateForPrediction differs:
- main adds pad_mask handling, a quantile_outputs field and _transform_quantiles_to.
- gift computes mean/median directly from the 9 raw decoder heads and supports prediction_type='quantile'.
- main first applies torch.quantile across the heads (re-sorting and interpolating) before mean/median, so point forecasts can differ numerically.
- gift's _init_weights prints a warning, and main adds post_init calls.
Minor: the file has 963 lines by wc -l, not 964.

4) IMPORTANT ATTRIBUTION CAVEAT that the record does not flag. FlowState's refinement dependence is not caused only by per-observation nonlinearities. I took layer-0 S5Block of r1.1 with the gate off and D=0, fed it the same random affine 2->512 lift, and compared the original grid (s=1) with the np.interp-refined grid (s=1/r). The purely linear ZOH output at the last step differs by 11.8% at r=2 and 17.9% at r=4. With the gate it is 13.9% / 21.8%, and the full layer-0 output is 5.1% / 7.8%. The reason is that ZOH with u_k held over the step is not exact for a piecewise-linear input. Causal RevIN also uses cumulative sample counts (a discrete sample mean/std, not a time integral), which is grid-dependent by itself. Implication for N2: FlowState is not a clean minimal counterexample for "nonlinearity causes grid dependence". The N2 counterexample must hold the linear stem FOH-exact to isolate the nonlinear effect. N2 must also credit exact ZOH and Delta rescaling to S5/FlowState.

App B.3 gives the closed-form ZOH update, "calculated in closed-form assuming constant input f between t and t+Delta t". In the code, LTICell defaults to discretization='zoh' (scipy cont2discrete), and LSICell's zoh option uses expm(A*(log(t+1)-log t)). This is exact integration only for a piecewise-constant hold (the standard ZOH result N2 already cites as prior work). 2. The record's input_reconstruction 'None explicit' is imprecise. Sec 2.4 says the discrete case "implicitly defines a function f(t) where f(k*Delta t)=f_k". 3. The linear memory is not an input stem. By Eq.31 its input is f_t = L_f(h_t). In the code, u = W_uxh(cat(x, h)), so the memory is fed each step by the nonlinear gated hidden state, tau(h,x) = (1-g)h + g*tanh(L(h,x)). No part of the model is a pure linear function of the reconstructed path. This supports fixed_time_nonlinearity = none: there is no fixed clock at all, and every nonlinear update happens once per observation.

'Invariant to step size' (B.3) means the recurrence in the index k does not depend on the Delta-t label, so a denser sampling is treated as a dilated sequence and only approximately matches (discretization error). There is no exact claim for the nonlinear model, and no virtual-knot test.

That makes the whole nonlinear model exactly invariant, by construction, to a global rescaling of timestamps (the 'Missing values upsample/downsample' rows). A close runner-up is the Abstract: "its continuous-time parametrization allows it to produce a consistent representation of the input audio signal, regardless of the modulation strategy and sampling rate". Either one lets a reviewer argue that the pattern 'continuous-time linear SSM stem at the native physical step, then a fixed-rate clock, then nonlinear layers, giving a sampling-rate-invariant representation' is already published.
verifications.corrections:
1. RAISE exact_input_integration from none to partial. The paper already has a continuous-time linear SSM stem. It integrates the raw high-rate input with the physical step Delta=1/f_s (inside B-bar) before any nonlinearity, and only Delta changes between rates (Sec. III-A). What is missing is closed-form exactness and an explicit ZOH or FOH reconstruction. The paper uses bilinear discretization (Eq. 2) with x[n]=A-bar x[n-1]+B-bar u[n] (Eq. 3), which is only approximate. A hostile reviewer would say N2 'just swaps bilinear for the classical exact FOH discretization'.

2. RAISE refinement_invariance_claim from partial to substantial. The paper states the same qualitative claim N2 makes: a 'sampling-rate-invariant' representation that 'encode[s] the same continuous-time history' for integer K, with downstream layers 'agnostic to ... sampling rate'. Its PDM test pipeline also begins with cubic-spline upsampling of PCM by OSR, which is virtual-knot refinement of a spline path, before Sigma-Delta quantization. So a reviewer can say refinement was, in effect, tested, even though it is confounded with quantization. The claim is still only approximate and empirical ('nearly identical, up to the quantization noise'). There is no theorem or bound, and no test isolates refinement: spline-upsampled PCM is never evaluated without Sigma-Delta.

3. The residual differentiator is concrete and testable. Even on noise-free, lossless upsampled input, bilinear with a changed Delta is not refinement-exact (the discretization error depends on Delta). N2 should run this paper's encoder (bilinear LegT/FouT plus integer x[nK] decimation) and N2's exact FOH stem on linearly interpolated knot-refined input. It should show nonzero latent drift for the former and float64-level drift for the latter.

4. fixed_time_nonlinearity stays substantial, but a hostile reviewer could argue full for uniform integer-ratio grids. The clock is defined by sample-index counting (x[nK_PDM], with K_PDM = K_PCM x OSR). It is a fixed physical clock only for integer OSR and K, and its points always coincide with observation instants (with K_PCM=1 it is every PCM sample). The paper has no mechanism for clock points between samples, non-integer ratios, irregular grids or missing samples. That gap is N2's room.

5. knot_vs_measurement_distinction stays none. The paper does separate an input-rate change (the OSR sweep) from latent decimation (the K sweep). It also discusses shared baseband content, in-band quantization noise at low OSR, and aliasing of LegT high-frequency content at synthesis (V-B1). It never distinguishes virtual from real samples and never treats missing observations.

6. Code: the record said the repo could not be checked. It can: git clone works, although the web page returns 403 through the proxy. It contains only README.md ('# SSM-SPEECH-PROCESSING'), with no code and no license. It therefore cannot settle whether the encoder is trained or how it is discretized in practice.

7. Encoder trainability remains unconfirmed. IV-C2's 'All the parameters from Equation 1 were fine-tuned' refers to the downstream KWS blocks, but Eq. 1 is also the encoder equation, so the sentence is ambiguous. SE synthesis projects onto fixed basis functions P, and 112k total parameters at H=512 is less than the 262,144 entries of a dense 512x512 A. Both suggest the encoder is frozen or not counted.

8. Minor source issues:
- The Fig. 3 caption says 'Delta of 0.001 (16 kHz sampling rate)', which is inconsistent.
- The IV-C1 split counts (8,843 train) are likely a typo for Speech Commands v2's 84,843.
- '2 MHz' is actually 2.048 MHz (128 x 16 kHz).

9. Consequence for N2:
- N2 cannot claim the stem + fixed-clock + downstream-nonlinearity architecture, an 'SSM-based sampling-rate-invariant front end', or 'downstream layers agnostic to sampling rate'.
- This architecture must be a baseline in any N2 speech or PDM experiment. It also serves as the natural 'dt-rescaling + fixed-rate decimation' comparator.
- Novelty must rest only on four points: (a) exact closed-form FOH integration, with a proof of exact knot-refinement invariance; (b) clock queries independent of observation positions, including non-integer and irregular grids; (c) the explicit three-way separation of refinement, downsampling and missing data; (d) a learned diagonal stem.
- If N2's gains on real tasks do not exceed this baseline, the verdict should be NO_GO.

Every nonlinearity (conv, Block-SA/Grid-SA, GELU, GEGLU FF) runs once per frame at the deployment frequency, so there is no fixed-time clock. The only invariance claimed is empirical robustness, and the numbers show real non-invariance (S5 Gen1 falls from 47.71 to 39.84 at 200 Hz).

So "partial" is the defensible hostile ceiling.

On knot_vs_measurement_distinction ("none"): the aliasing discussion treats kernel bandwidth against the step Nyquist rate, which is a property of the model. The paper never separates virtual knots, real downsampling and missing data, and runs no missing-data or irregular-sampling tests.

This paper supports N2's motivation. It is a direct example of per-observation nonlinear updates plus dt-only rescaling giving grid-dependent outputs.

RATING CHANGES
1. exact_input_integration: raise partial -> substantial (hostile reading). The paper states a continuous-time input model, Eq. (12), and integrates the diagonal LTI SSM in closed form over it (Eq. 13 -> Eq. 14). It uses physical Delta_k and a parallel associative scan with Lambda-bar(Delta_k)Lambda-bar(Delta_l) = Lambda-bar(Delta_k + Delta_l) (Eqs 18-19). That is the same kind of mechanism as the N2 stem. What differs is the reconstruction: impulses rather than an FOH/piecewise-linear path. Closed-form FOH discretization itself is textbook, so N2 must not present "exact integration of the reconstruction" as new. Only the FOH-path version, and its composition with a fixed clock, can be N2's own.
2. fixed_time_nonlinearity: raise none -> partial. EventSSM already separates the rate at which inputs are integrated (every event) from the rate at which C x and the GLU are evaluated (every p-th event). The separating rule is an event count, not a physical-time clock, so virtual knots shift where the readouts fall. N2's novelty must rest specifically on the observation-independent physical-time clock.
3. refinement_invariance_claim: none (confirmed). The closest statement is Sec. 2, "our method integrates every single event asynchronously with arbitrary resolution without sacrificing simulation scalability". That concerns timing resolution, not invariance.
4. knot_vs_measurement_distinction: none (confirmed).
5. overall: partial (confirmed).

MECHANISM CORRECTIONS FROM THE CODE
(a) Pooling is applied only in the first layer of each stage. layers.py SequenceStage has the comments "first layer with pooling" and "further layers without pooling". The paper instead says pooling is applied "after each state-space layer". Configs: SSC/SHD/DVS medium use num_stages=2 with 3 layers per stage; SSC small uses 1 stage with 6 layers.
(b) In a pooled layer, ssm.py apply_ssm runs the full-resolution scan and then keeps xs[:remaining_timesteps:stride]. This is plain subsampling of the state; the state is never averaged. The avgpool and timepool modes (the timepool weights are Delta_k + eps) average only the skip path and the D u feedthrough. The paper's "equivalent to averaging" is therefore loose.
(c) The pooled integration timesteps are the sum of Delta over each group. Deeper layers treat the pooled nonlinear outputs as new impulses at the pooled times, so exactness holds only relative to each layer's own discrete input.
(d) Where nonlinearities act, per event: a learned embedding lookup (the input is a channel/token id), then a prenorm before the first SSM. SHD and DVS use LayerNorm, which is nonlinear. SSC uses BatchNorm, which is affine at eval and adds a bias per event. The layer-1 GLU, and every later GLU, runs at the stride-p event-count rate. The classifier head is an index-based masked mean pool in the medium configs, or a Delta-weighted "timepool" (a Riemann-sum time average) in SSC small.
(e) So the record's note that "inserting zero-valued virtual events would leave the linear state unchanged" holds only for the abstract Eq. (14). In the actual architecture a "null event" does not exist, because every event is an embedding of a channel id. Prenorm biases per event and the index-based pooling and readout would also break invariance.

- Code license: MIT ("Copyright (c) 2024 Mark Schoene").

  - The authors admit selecting models on the test set "for a fair comparison".
  - Spiking Speech Commands is a spike-encoded dataset. It is not the raw-audio Speech Commands resolution-change benchmark. There are no HAR, EigenWorms, SC-resolution or PDM numbers.
- Grid changes tested: none as evaluations. Drop-event and time-jitter appear only as training augmentations.

verifications.corrections:
1. RAISE fixed_time_nonlinearity from partial to substantial. The record overlooked B.3 and B.4. In B.3, DeepONet is written as T_{T_K} o N o T*_{Psi_N}: a linear analysis operator, then an arbitrary nonlinear branch net on a coefficient vector of fixed size. The paper says "Written in this manner, DeepONet satisfies Definition 3.4". In B.4, a discretized SNO "simply corresponds to an ordinary feedforward neural network mapping Fourier coefficients to Fourier coefficients". C.2 then describes how SNO runs at resolution M: "it takes in 2M+1 point samples, synthesizes these to a function in H which is then sampled on the training grid. Then, u(Psi_K,Psi_K) is applied". Fig. 4 shows that SNO is representation-equivalent. This is N2's abstract structure: an exact linear stage onto a fixed representation, with all nonlinearity applied only there. What ReNO lacks is time, causality and recurrence.

2. The most important consequence for GO/NO_GO. ReNO's own generic recipe is Eq. 3.3, u(Psi',Phi') = T_Phi'^dagger T_Phi u(Psi,Phi) T_Psi^dagger T_Psi'. Its SNO procedure in C.2 is exactly fixed-grid resampling followed by a fixed network, and that combination is representation-equivalent. In N2's setting, sampling the same piecewise-linear interpolant at fixed clock times is also exactly invariant to inserting virtual knots. Exact refinement invariance therefore does NOT separate N2 from the mandatory resampling baseline. Any N2 gain has to come from what the integrating stem keeps between clock ticks (it acts as a path-integral prefilter, where resampling keeps only point samples). That gain has to show up under real downsampling or missing data, not in the invariance property itself. N2 should state its invariance theorem as an instance of Remark 3.5, Prop 3.6 and Prop 3.7 for piecewise-linear frames.

3. Qualify the CNO claim. CNO's ReNO status in B.2 depends on assumption (B.3), sigma(f) in B_wbar. The paper admits that [23] assumes this only "up to negligible frequencies". Sec. 4 says ReLU gives sigma(f) outside B_omega for every omega. So CNO is at best an eps-ReNO, and Sec. 5.1 says only that CNO "is more likely to be a ReNO". This is a real point for N2 to exploit: exact equivalence with a pointwise nonlinearity on a grid that depends on the input needs a band-limit assumption, and N2 avoids that by never evaluating a nonlinearity on the input grid. But the same avoidance is already in the DeepONet/SNO pattern (point 1).

4. Keep exact_input_integration at partial. Eq. 3.2 (u = T_Phi^dagger U T_Psi) is the abstract principle for discretizing a linear layer exactly, and it is applied to the Fourier layer (B.1) and to band-limited convolution (B.2). The paper has no ODE, no closed-form exponential or ZOH/FOH integration, no causal kernel and no piecewise-linear frames. Remark 3.5 ("u must depend on Psi and Phi, and hence, must be discretization dependent") supports a stem that depends on the knots and dt. It is also prior art for the idea that the exact linear part must be discretization-aware.

5. The note "ReNO does not treat non-uniform knots" is slightly too strong. B.3 says: "if the sensors are randomly distributed rather than located on a uniform grid, then it can induce aliasing errors for DeepONets". The paper also cites Benedetto, "Irregular sampling and frames" [2], for its aliasing definition. This is a passing remark with no theory or experiments. Missing observations are never treated.

6. knot_vs_measurement_distinction stays substantial. ReNO separates a lossless change of frame (above Nyquist, where a frame exists) from information loss (below Nyquist). Its "above Nyquist" test grids are fresh point samples of a band-limited function, that is, real measurements that add no information. They are not virtual knots computed from an interpolant, and the frame formalism treats the two cases identically. Missingness is not covered. N2's contribution here is a three-way operational split (virtual knots vs real downsampling vs missing observations), not the lossless-vs-lossy principle.

7. Minor. The sections_read list should add B.3, B.4, D, D.1 and E. Keep the time_handling entry (none; spatial/PDE setting) and the reported_numbers entry as they are.

8. Overall stays substantial, not full. ReNO has no time series, no causal or recurrent SSM, no closed-form exponential integration over first-order-hold input, no fixed physical-time clock semantics, no missing-data handling, and no real-signal tasks. A hostile reviewer would still say that N2's invariance principle and its "linear exact stage, then nonlinearity on a fixed representation" design are both already in ReNO (Eq. 3.2, 3.3, Prop 3.6, 3.7, B.3, B.4, C.2).

Eq. 2 (f_conv(z) = K∗z: "the convolution operates by continuously sliding the discretized kernel over the continuous representation") shows linear layers acting exactly on the reconstructed continuous signal. Config B's Fourier-feature input can be evaluated exactly at any coordinate. verifications.corrections:
1) Input reconstruction. 'Kaiser-windowed' is not in the paper; it is confirmed only in the code (CNO2d_classic/training/filtered_networks.py). The paper says windowed-sinc via scipy.signal.firwin, with N_tap=12, c_h=0.8, N_sigma=2 and w_c=s/2.0001 (C.1.4). The repo's CNO1d_simplified does not use sinc at all: it uses F.interpolate(mode='bicubic', antialias=True).

2) The invariance claim needs a stronger qualifier. The record says Prop 2.1 is 'in theory exact for band-limited inputs', but that exactness depends on assumption (A.9), sigma(B_w) subset of B_wbar. The authors themselves weaken it: App A.5 says '(A.9) is satisfied up to negligible frequencies', and Remark C.1 says the condition may 'hold only approximately'. Exact equivariance needs polynomial or rational activations with enough upsampling (Remark B.4). The implemented activation is a filtered LeakyReLU (code), so exactness fails even in theory, not only because of the windowed sinc.

3) Where the invariance comes from. In C.4, invariance to the input's resolution comes from resampling the input to the fixed computational grid (A.7), not from the anti-aliased activation. Any network behind the same resampling would inherit it for band-limited inputs sampled at or above Nyquist. The paper never runs that control: FNO and UNet get the unresized input, and 'CNO w/o Filters' (C.5) is only said to be resolution-dependent 'similar to the UNet model' and is not re-tested with resampling. So CNO does not isolate the effect of resampling alone, which is N2's mandatory baseline. This gap is also a warning for N2: its gain over resample+backbone must come from something resampling cannot give. Candidates are exact PL integration of irregular knots, causality, and information between clock ticks.

4) Grid changes tested. Test resolutions lie both below and above the 64x64 training resolution (Sec 4 reports FNO errors at lower and at higher resolutions). NS thin-shear-layer data is multiscale, not band-limited. So below 64 the test inputs are genuinely lossy downsampled versions, and above 64 CNO low-pass filters away content. The experiment therefore mixes lossless refinement with lossy downsampling. There is no irregular sampling, no missing-observation test and no same-path knot-refinement test. Inputs are 2D spatial with no time or causality.

5) knot_vs_measurement_distinction should go up from partial to substantial. The record justifies its rating by s' < s vs s' > s, but that is the wrong axis. App A.2 formally separates lossless sampling at or above Nyquist, where 'sampling a function f in B_w on a finer grid ... amounts to representing the function f with respect to the system Psi_wbar' (change of frame, Eq. A.7), from sampling below Nyquist, which produces an 'aliasing error'. That is the lossless-refinement vs aliasing distinction. What is still missing: a virtual vs real distinction (every sample above Nyquist is equally lossless under the band-limit assumption), any treatment of missing or irregular observations, and an experiment that separates the cases.

6) exact_input_integration stays partial. The ideal downsampling operator D (Sec. 2) is an integral of the continuous input against a sinc kernel, sampled on a coarser grid. That is a linear anti-aliasing prefilter followed by sampling on a fixed grid, which a reviewer could present as N2's stem with a sinc kernel. But the kernel is fixed and non-causal, only uniform band-limited grids are covered, the filter is implemented approximately as an FIR, and there is no SSM, no closed form on PL paths and no irregular knots.

7) fixed_time_nonlinearity (substantial) and refinement_invariance_claim (substantial) are unchanged. A hostile reviewer could push fixed_time toward full, because the principle is identical and differs only in being spatial rather than temporal.

8) Reported numbers are not only in the figure. All ratings are kept (partial / substantial / substantial / substantial; overall substantial). Items 1-3 add missing bibliographic information. Items 4-8 add mechanism detail and hostile-reviewer points. Item 9 flags an inference.

1. Venue. Published in Doklady Mathematics (issued Dec 2023), DOI 10.1134/S1064562423701107 (checked through Crossref). The volume and pages were not checked. The arXiv v2 is dated 01 Apr 2024.

2. Code and license. The code is at https://github.com/VLSF/SNO, cited in App C.1 ('Code is available in ...'). The raw LICENSE file is CC0 1.0 Universal. The record wrongly says 'Not recorded'.

3. Where the nonlinearity is evaluated, made more precise with App C.1.3.
   - SNO(Ch) and SNO(F) apply sigma, a softplus on the real and imaginary parts, directly to coefficient matrices: Eq. 21 is U^{n+1} = sigma(U^n A + b) and Eq. 22 is sigma(B U^n A + b). In these variants the nonlinearity never touches a time grid; it acts on a fixed-length coefficient vector.
   - xSNO(Ch) and xSNO(F) apply the network to values on a fixed grid, either the Chebyshev grid or a uniform grid.
   - xcSNO alternates between grid values and coefficients (Eq. 23).
   - Everything is trained at a fixed resolution of 100 grid points or 100 coefficients (C.3).
   - So the record's phrase 'fixed coefficient vector (or the corresponding fixed grid)' is right. This is the spectral analog of N2's fixed clock.

4. SNO's grid consistency is never tested on SNO. It holds only by construction. Fig. 1b and Fig. 2a test grid refinement on FNO only. The tests that include SNO (Fig. 2b, Table 1, Table 3) change frequency content, i.e. harmonic shifts Δk, sometimes together with a 100-to-300-point grid change. They do not test lossless refinement of SNO itself. The grid changes the record lists are right, but the record should say 'FNO only' for the refinement test.

5. How the input is reconstructed, and the limits of 'exact'.
   - Coefficients come from DCT-I on Chebyshev nodes or FFT on uniform grids (Sec 2).
   - Inputs that do not fit the architecture are chopped (projected) (Sec 4).
   - Nothing handles arbitrary or irregular knot positions, piecewise-linear (first-order-hold) paths, or closed-form integration of a linear ODE.
   - The 'exact/lossless' claim covers only inputs that are truncated Chebyshev or Fourier series. This supports 'partial', not higher, for exact_input_integration.

6. Hostile-reviewer point that should go in the notes. SNO's 'detach interpolation, fix the resolution' is essentially 'project or resample onto a fixed representation, then run any network'. That is a spectral form of N2's mandatory fixed-grid resampling baseline. A reviewer can argue that N2's fixed-clock component is this principle moved into a causal SSM. N2 must therefore show a gain over fixed-grid resampling plus the same backbone. Beating per-observation models alone is not enough.

7. Knot-versus-measurement distinction.
   - Sec 1 also covers the measurement side: sampling on a 2N+1 point grid resolves frequencies only up to N, and higher frequencies are 'indistinguishable' (input aliasing under real undersampling).
   - Sec 3.2 covers the lossless-refinement side: refining a fully resolved function adds 'no ... novel information'.
   - Missing or dropped observations are not discussed.
   - Keep 'substantial'.

8. Time handling and causality. There is no dt, causality or streaming. Time is a global Chebyshev domain: SNO(F) uses a Chebyshev basis 'along temporal' axes (C.1.3), and the parametric ODE task f(t)->y(t) is Sec 5.1.2. The MambaNO paper never states its protocol, and its repo has no resolution-test script (the README 'Test' section is empty). So the protocol is inferred, but it is strongly implied.
