verifications.corrections:
1. ACCESS. Change ABSTRACT_ONLY to FULL_TEXT_SECTIONS. The paper is openly available at proceedings.iclr.cc (URL in access_self). "Paper body NOT read" and "should be checked before any claim relative to CROP is finalized" are resolved. Add the proceedings URL to arxiv_or_venue. No arXiv version was found.

2. INPUT RECONSTRUCTION (record said "exact filters not read"). The reconstruction is trigonometric (DFT) interpolation on a uniform periodic grid. Sec 4.1: "we will view it as a function reconstructed by the N Fourier coefficients".
- The lifting is v0(x)=∫C(x−y)a(y)dy with a band-limited kernel (Sec 4.3).
- The code computes it as rfft2 at the input resolution, keeping the lowest modes, zero-padding and applying irfft2 at a fixed latent size, rescaled by out_size/in_size. See Crop_to_latent_size in CROP_measure_errors.py and SpectralConv2d/LiftBlock in scr/CRNO.py.
- App D.6 says some tasks use "band-limited identity kernels (i.e. Fourier projection and interpolation operators)".
- Resolution independence of the lift is exact only if the samples come from a band-limited (trigonometric-polynomial) function above the coarser grid's Nyquist rate. Otherwise aliasing changes the retained coefficients.
- There is no first-order hold, no closed-form integration of a linear ODE/SSM over a piecewise-polynomial path, and no causality.
- One subtlety a reviewer could raise: refining the grid by sampling CROP's own trigonometric reconstruction leaves the lift output exactly unchanged. This is the Fourier analogue of N2's FOH-stem knot invariance, although the paper never states or tests it. Hence exact_input_integration = partial, not none.

3. WHERE NONLINEARITIES ARE EVALUATED (incomplete in the record). The intermediate nonlinearities act on the fixed latent grid. In scr/CRNO.py the lift also applies BatchNorm+GELU at the latent size. In addition, the CROP projection Q contains "a fully connected point-wise network" with nonlinear activations evaluated at the OUTPUT discretization (Sec 4.3, Remark 4.5, App C; ProjectBlock/MLP q applied after CROP_back in the code). Because this network is pointwise, it plays the role of N2's output-query rule: a nonlinear decode that commutes with sampling. Minor code detail: CRNO concatenates linspace(0,1,N) coordinate channels at the input resolution before the lift. Their truncated DFT depends weakly on N, so the implementation is not bit-exact invariant.

4. INVARIANCE CLAIM. The paper states the claim in words:
- Sec 1: "CROP is free of both DMEs and aliasing errors"; Table 1 marks CROP as "Free of DME".
- Sec 4.3: "does not suffer from the DME".
- The section titles, however, say "Minimizing the discretization mismatch error".

There is no theorem or exactness proof for CROP. The evidence is empirical and approximate:
- Table 6 (NS ν=1e-3, trained at 64): 0.54137/0.54140/0.54154/0.54142 % at 256/128/64/32. Nearly equal, not identical.
- Table 7 (nonlinear Darcy, trained at 85): CROP degrades at 43x43 (0.57 vs 0.51).
- Table 8 (linear Darcy): CROP gives 2.80 at 256 vs 1.10 at 64. The authors attribute this to the 256 data "contain[ing] more high-frequency information" (D.5).

So invariance is conditional on the refined data adding no new spectral content. refinement_invariance_claim stays substantial, not full: the claim is conditional and empirical, not an exact refinement theorem.

5. GRID CHANGES TESTED. Every test resolution is a decimation ([::sub, ::sub], sub in {1,2,4,8}) of the 256x256 solver output (D.1.1 and code), i.e. real measurements of one field on nested uniform grids. For Darcy: 421/141/85/43.
- 32x32 is real downsampling, where aliasing is possible.
- There are no virtual knots, no irregular sampling and no missing observations. Sec 6 names uniform grids and rectangular domains as a limitation.
- Time is autoregressive with a fixed step of 1; there is no dt-based handling.

6. KNOT vs MEASUREMENT. Keep partial, with an explicit flag. App D.5 already separates grid refinement that carries no new high-frequency content (NS, where CROP stays invariant) from refinement that carries new content (linear Darcy, where CROP degrades). A hostile reviewer could cite this as the conceptual core of N2's lossless-refinement vs real-measurement split. However, this is a post-hoc observation, not a protocol: there is no virtual-knot insertion on a fixed reconstruction and no missing-observation case.

7. FIXED-GRID NONLINEARITY. Confirmed substantial. Also note that the CROP paper already runs, in spatial form, what N2 plans as ablations and baselines:
- "Alias-free FNO (Fixed)": activations on a fixed 128x128 grid via bicubic interpolation, with the linear layers at native resolution. This is a "fixed clock only" analogue and it fails: 6.95/7.40/0.61/42.08 % at 256/128/64/32.
- "CNO (with interpolation)": bicubic resampling of the input to a fixed grid plus a backbone, i.e. a "fixed-grid resampling + backbone" baseline: 4.17/2.95/1.98/7.69 %.
- CROP, the analogue of stem + fixed grid, stays at 0.54 at all resolutions.

A reviewer can argue that "both components are needed and resampling is not enough" was already shown for spatial operators. N2 must cite this and its gains must go beyond it.

8. OVERALL. Confirmed substantial, not full. What CROP lacks relative to N2:
- It works on spatial periodic uniform-grid operator learning, not causal time series.
- It has no SSM or physical-time clock and no streaming.
- Its reconstruction is Fourier/band-limited rather than FOH, with no closed-form integral over the reconstructed path.
- It has no irregular or missing observations and no exactness theorem.

The architectural principle is nonetheless already published: a resolution-agnostic linear lift, all nonlinear processing on a fixed discretization, and a pointwise nonlinear decode at the query resolution. So is the aliasing explanation for why per-sample nonlinearities break cross-resolution consistency (Remark 4.5 / App C: an analytic σ creates frequencies beyond the band-limit; README: instability "largely arises from non-linear activation functions"). N2's per-observation-nonlinearity counterexample is therefore conceptually anticipated in space. N2 should also cite CNO (Raonic et al. 2023) and ReNO / continuous-discrete equivalence (Bartolucci et al. 2023), which CROP builds on. verifications.corrections:
RATINGS
- fixed_time_nonlinearity: raise from partial to substantial (hostile reading). In the spatial setting, the paper describes and tests several models that run all nonlinear computation on a fixed resolution that does not depend on the input grid:
  - CNO: "fixed-resolution models", with interpolation in and out (Sec. 4.2).
  - CROP: lifts inputs to and from a "fixed-dimensional representation" for any backbone (Sec. 4.2 and Sec. 6: "lifts arbitrarily discretization data to a fixed-resolution band-limited space").
  - DeepONet: "operates at a fixed resolution on the input" (App. J; the record missed this).
  This is the fixed-grid resampling + backbone pattern, which is N2's mandatory baseline. It is not a time clock, and it is prior work (Raonic 2023; Gao 2025) that this paper only evaluates.
  The record also omits a detail about the anti-alias activation in App. K. It upsamples "by a scalar factor" of the current resolution before applying the nonlinearity. So its evaluation grid still scales with the input grid and is not fixed.
- Other ratings stand:
  - exact_input_integration: none. No closed-form integration of a reconstructed path appears anywhere.
  - refinement_invariance_claim: partial. There is no exact or guaranteed invariance claim. The paper tests a lossless-type resampling ("resolution interpolation") and gets a negative empirical result for FNO, FNO with anti-alias activations (App. K, Fig. 40) and DeepONet (App. J, Fig. 35). "CNO does not alias" is qualitative. In the sections read, the CNO/CROP tests (Fig. 7, App. F) use the joint multi-resolution setting, not the pure resolution-interpolation protocol.
  - knot_vs_measurement_distinction: substantial. Resolution interpolation vs information extrapolation, plus strided downsampling framed as real sensors (App. M), is a clear analogue of refinement vs real downsampling. It is not full: missing, irregular or random-drop observations are never treated, all grids are uniform and spatial, and the "lossless" change is only lossless in the band-limited Shannon sense, not as a piecewise-linear (PL) knot refinement.
  - overall: partial.

CAVEATS FOR N2
- The "lossless-type" label is only approximately right at the lowest resolutions. The filters keep |k| up to Darcy 8f at N=16, Burgers 64f at 128, and Navier-Stokes 32f at 64. Each sits exactly at the Nyquist bin, even though the paper says "The sampling rates of all data are large enough to resolve all remaining frequencies."
- App. K / Fig. 42 conclude "activation functions alone are not the source of FNO aliasing" and blame out-of-distribution, "data-driven" aliasing. A reviewer can use this against N2's causal story. N2's minimal counterexample must isolate the per-observation nonlinearity, for example with fixed or untrained weights and exact arithmetic, instead of relying on accuracy drops after training.
- Fixed-grid resampling of the same PL interpolant is also exactly invariant to inserting virtual knots. So refinement invariance by itself does not distinguish N2 from the CROP/CNO-style baseline. N2's distinct claim has to rest on the exact integration stem (information between clock ticks) and on its specific conditions.

OTHER FIELD FIXES
- input_reconstruction:
  - FNO has no input reconstruction; it works directly on grid samples.
  - The data pipeline zeroes FFT components outside radius N (C.1), then keeps every Nth element by strided downsampling (C.1, App. M).
  - CNO/CROP interpolate to a fixed resolution, but this paper does not name the interpolation method.
  - Average pooling and bilinear interpolation (App. M) are alternative ways to build the downsampled datasets, not model input reconstruction.
- time_handling: "autoregressive" is not verified. The text says only that artifacts "compound across time steps (Fig. 15)". Temporal resolution is never varied; all resolution changes are spatial.
- invariance_claim: add that the proposed remedy is empirical multi-resolution training (Sec. 5).
- grid_changes_tested: add the average-pooling and bilinear downsampling variants (App. M). There are no missing, irregular or random-drop tests.

NUMBERS
- The "1x, 2x, 10x" figure is verified (Sec. 3.2, Fig. 16).
- Additional numbers from Table 5 (App. L, Darcy FNO, MSE, mean ± std over 3 seeds; the row/column orientation is unlabeled in the HTML, and the lowest value in each row lies on the diagonal):
  - (16,16): 3.6e-4 ± 9e-6
  - (16,128): 2.0e-3 ± 3e-4
  - (128,128): 2.7e-4 ± 8e-6
  - (128,16): 1.8e-3 ± 8e-5
- Confirmed: no HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM numbers.

CODE / LICENSE
- The repo github.com/msakarvadia/operator_aliasing is linked in the author footnote and in App. N.
- The LICENSE file does contain the standard MIT permission text. It has no "MIT License" header, and its copyright line is the placeholder "Copyright (c) 2023-Present FooBar Author". So the license is identifiable as MIT text with a placeholder copyright holder; the record's "type could not be identified" is wrong.

FOLLOW-UP
- The paper cites Gao et al. 2025 (ICLR, CROP), "Discretization-invariance? On the discretization mismatch errors in neural operators". It probably overlaps more strongly on fixed-grid lifting and discretization-mismatch claims and needs its own adversarial record.

(2) Sec. 3, paragraph "Direct fine-grid execution can be worse than Low+pad": "Because the linear parts of FNO (spectral convolution and residual linear map) are mode-wise, these resolution-dependent spectral corruption points to the nonlinearities (and their discretization) as the primary source of the mismatch." The factual details also check out: Eq. (1) is y_hat_{s->S} = U_{s->S}(M(T_{S->s}(x_S))); training is at s=85, with Fig. 1 at S=211; GeLU follows each block; there is a lifting MLP and a two-layer MLP projection; padding is none or 10; the training-set normalizer is reused. No code of the authors' own was found. The footnote link is printed as https://github.com/ixScience/fourier_neural_operator and is described as the official FNO implementation (Li et al., 2021). Additional verbatim evidence a reviewer would use:
- Sec. 4: "when high-frequency modes are absent from low-resolution observations, they are not identifiable in general, so zero-shot recovery of the correct fine-scale content cannot be expected without additional assumptions".
- Sec. 3: "executing the network on an unseen grid can still induce nonlinear aliasing that folds unresolved frequencies back into the learned band."
- Sec. 4: "Future work could combine limited multi-resolution supervision with anti-aliased and nonlinearity-aware designs to reduce grid-dependent spectral folding at inference time."
verifications.strongest_non_novelty_sentence: Sec. 3: "Because the linear parts of FNO (spectral convolution and residual linear map) are mode-wise, these resolution-dependent spectral corruption points to the nonlinearities (and their discretization) as the primary source of the mismatch." The paper says this in its band-limited, no-new-information setting (the Fourier-padding analogue of virtual-knot refinement). It pairs this with a remedy that runs the whole nonlinear network on the fixed training grid after an exact linear projection. The Sec. 2 sentence after Eq. 1 states the remedy: it "avoids executing the network at an unseen discretization and provides a strong reference for cross-resolution evaluation."
verifications.corrections:
RATING CHANGES (hostile-reviewer default):

(a) exact_input_integration: raise from none to partial. Eq. (1)'s T_{S->s} is an exact linear map on the band-limited reconstruction. In the paper's best-case setting the S-grid input is Fourier-padded, and s=85 is odd, so T_{S->s}(U_{s->S}(x_s)) = x_s exactly. Low+pad is therefore "exact linear projection of the reconstructed field, then a nonlinear net on a fixed grid, then a linear output query (zero-padding)". That is structurally the N2 pipeline. It is not a closed-form continuous-time SSM or ODE integration, there is no FOH, and it is spatial only, so the rating is partial, not substantial.

(b) fixed_time_nonlinearity: raise from partial to substantial. Low+pad evaluates every nonlinearity (lifting MLP, GeLUs, decoder MLP) on the fixed training grid, whatever the test discretization. The paper motivates this explicitly as avoiding execution at an unseen discretization. This is the spatial analogue of N2's fixed physical clock. It is presented as a baseline, not as an architecture.

(c) overall: raise from partial to substantial. This is borderline between partial and substantial. The conceptual core is already published for FNO:
- lossless (band-limited) refinement plus nonlinearities evaluated per grid point gives grid-dependent output;
- linear parts are not the cause;
- running the network on a fixed grid after exact projection avoids it and is a "strong baseline".
What N2 can still claim: the time-series/SSM instantiation with a closed-form FOH integration stem, a formal exact-invariance statement, and the three-way separation of refinement, downsampling and missing observations. refinement_invariance_claim stays substantial and knot_vs_measurement_distinction stays partial.

MECHANISM NUANCES THE RECORD MISSES:
1. The paper never states that Low+pad is exactly invariant, although it is by construction. Its claims are empirical (Fig. 1 spectra) plus inference.
2. The attribution to nonlinearities is inferential, not ablated. There is no identity-activation control.
3. padding=10 counts grid cells, so it covers a different physical width at 85 vs 211. That is a non-nonlinear, grid-dependent confound, which they report as a separate setting.
4. The training-set normalizer is reused at every resolution.

GRID CHANGES: only upsampling (S>s) is tested at test time. Training data are real downsampling of the 421x421 reference (A.1: "lower resolutions are obtained by downsampling this reference"). The input a(x) is piecewise-constant, so the raw data are not band-limited. No missing or irregular observations are tested, and there is no time axis.

KEY IMPLICATION FOR N2: the fixed-grid resampling baseline is itself exactly invariant to virtual-knot insertion on a piecewise-linear path, because the interpolant is unchanged. This paper shows that the analogous resample baseline is strong. Invariance alone therefore cannot be N2's contribution; N2 must beat fixed-grid resampling plus the same backbone on accuracy or cost. Otherwise the user's own rule makes it NO_GO.

MORE FORMAL PRIOR ART TO ADD (same phenomenon):
- ReNO, Representation Equivalent Neural Operators, arXiv 2305.19913 (verified): formal aliasing error from pointwise nonlinearities.
- CNO, Convolutional Neural Operators, arXiv 2302.01178 (verified): activations applied on an upsampled grid to be alias-free.
- Alias-Free GAN, arXiv 2106.12423 (verified).
- Gao et al., ICLR 2025, "Discretization-invariance? On the discretization mismatch errors in neural operators" (arXiv id unknown).
- Sakarvadia et al., ICLR 2026, "The false promise of zero-shot super-resolution in machine-learned operators" (arXiv id unknown). This is likely stronger on separating interpolation from extrapolation.

N2 must cite these papers. It must not claim as new either the diagnosis that nonlinearities evaluated on the grid break lossless-refinement consistency, or the fixed-grid remedy.

verifications.corrections:
1) Raise fixed_time_nonlinearity from substantial to full. The paper states the exact generic mechanism: put all nonlinear computation on a fixed latent discretization of the domain, independent of the input points (Sec. 3.7). It frames this as an encoder-decoder neural operator (Sec. 3.6, Eq. 14) and tests it experimentally (Sec. 5.2; C.2 'U-Net with input & output interpolation', a fixed 128x128 grid). The domain is a generic D_f in R^d (App. A.3), so a time axis is covered, and N2's component explicitly allows 'any network' on the clock. The only difference is causality and time series, which a hostile reviewer would call instantiation, not mechanism.

2) Raise overall from partial to substantial. The paper supplies the parts of N2's architecture in generic form:
- Sec. 3.3, Eq. (8): a convolutional integral operator with a fixed receptive field, where 'the output function g can be queried at arbitrary points y_i'. N2's stem is a causal instance of Eq. (8) with kernel C e^{At} B 1[t>=0], queried at y_j = tau_j.
- Sec. 3.6-3.7: a fixed latent discretization plus a network.
- Sec. 5.2: states the weakness of plain interpolation (it discards high-resolution information) and suggests the fix (combine with other neural-operator layers).
What the paper does NOT contain, and what N2 can still claim:
(a) exact closed-form integration against the first-order-hold path. The paper only uses quadrature: Riemann, Delaunay, Monte Carlo (App. A.5, Eq. 30-31). A.5 mentions 'analytically integrating simpler interpolating functions, such as polynomials, e.g., Newton-Cotes formulas', but that interpolates the integrand; it is not product integration of a fixed kernel against a piecewise-linear input.
(b) a causal, recurrent SSM or any time-series instantiation.
(c) an exact, finite-resolution invariance statement. Footnote 2: 'strictly speaking, neural operators still incur a (controllable) discretization error'.
(d) a virtual-knot vs real-measurement vs missing-observation distinction.

3) Keep exact_input_integration at partial: the encoder in Eq. (15) and the operator in Eq. (4)/(8) are approximated with quadrature and converge only asymptotically (A.4, Eq. 29).

4) Keep refinement_invariance_claim at partial, but add an omitted pointer. App. A.4 already formalizes nested refinements X_1 ⊆ X_2 ⊆ ... (Eq. 27-29). The claim is only asymptotic convergence, but that is the same refinement setting as N2. App. A.3 cites Bartolucci et al. (2023) for the conditions under which Eq. (26) holds with equality, i.e. exact discretization invariance. That paper is arXiv 2305.19913 (ReNO, 'Representation Equivalent Neural Operators: a Framework for Alias-free Operator Learning'; id verified). Sec. 3.3 and 3.7 also cite Raonic et al. (CNO, arXiv 2302.01178; id verified), which interpolates to a fixed resolution. Both need their own adversarial check because they address exact or alias-free invariance.

5) knot_vs_measurement_distinction: partial is generous. The paper separates discretization error from information loss under downsampling (Sec. 3.7: 'downsampling the input function leads to a loss of information (e.g., high frequencies for Fourier interpolation)'). It also mentions aliasing error (footnote 13) and a minimum resolution (App. B; Sec. 4.2). But it has no virtual-knot concept and no handling of missing observations. I keep partial under the hostile default; 'none' is also defensible.

6) Framing risk for N2 (my inference, not a claim in the paper). The paper's own fixed-grid interpolation baseline, with linear or bilinear interpolation (C.2), is exactly invariant to lossless knot refinement of the same piecewise-linear path. Inserting virtual knots does not change the interpolant, so it does not change the samples on the fixed grid either. So 'exact refinement invariance' cannot be what separates N2 from its mandatory resampling baseline. N2 is separated only by exactly integrating the information between clock ticks, which is the weakness named in Sec. 5.2. If the resampling baseline matches N2 on the tasks, the gain is explained by prior work, so the verdict would be NO_GO.

7) Sec. 3.2 asserts that pointwise operators are 'naturally agnostic to the resolution'. N2's per-observation counterexample must therefore target the composition: a pointwise nonlinearity followed by quadrature or recurrence over the grid. A reviewer can call this the known 'discretization error' (footnote 2; A.4), so N2 should present it as exact non-invariance at finite resolution under virtual knots. That is a case the paper's asymptotic framework does not separate out.

8) code_url_and_license: github.com/neuraloperator/NNs-to-NOs (footnote 1; C.2), MIT License (checked in the raw LICENSE file). The experiments also use the NeuralOperator library, github.com/neuraloperator/neuraloperator; I did not check its license.

9) sections_read: add App. A.3-A.5, A.8, B and Sec. 4.2. They contain the equality pointer, the nested-refinement definition, the quadrature schemes, and multi-resolution training by subsampling.

verifications.strongest_non_novelty_sentence: Sec. 1: "The error arising from this difference is called aliasing error, and during a forward pass of the FNO, the aliasing error propagates through the subsequent model layers and may be amplified by nonlinearities." Together with Thm 3.2 (error <= C N^{-s}) and the Sec. 4.1 ReLU result, a reviewer can argue that this paper already establishes, and bounds, the claim that nonlinearities evaluated pointwise on the sampling grid make an implemented model depend on the discretization. verifications.corrections:
1. sections_read is incomplete. The record lists only Abstract, 1, 1.1, 1.2 and 3. The experiments (Sec. 4), conclusions (Sec. 5) and App. A carry most of the evidence on grid changes and reconstruction; I read those and list them in access_self.

2. Mechanism needs precise conditions. Thm 3.2 bounds sup over a compact A_c in H^s of N^{-d/2} ||v_t - v_t^N|| in the discrete l2 norm, <= C N^{-s}. It assumes A1: C^s activations with derivatives bounded by B; A3: 1 <= K < N/2; A4: s > d/2; A5: bounded parameters. Thm 3.3 gives the same rate in continuous L2 using the trigonometric interpolant p_t^N. Remark 3.4 extends the rate to the output Psi. The domain is the periodic torus T^d (space, d=2 in experiments). There is no time, causality or recurrence. The experimental ground truth is a discrete FNO on a 2048 grid, not the continuum.

3. input_reconstruction should be sharper. The FNO takes grid-point values, and the first operation is the pointwise nonlinear lifting v_0 = P(a) (a shallow NN, Sec. 2.1). So there is no linear stem before a nonlinearity. By eq. (3.1) and (A.7), the grid spectral kernel K_t^N applies the continuum kernel exactly to the trigonometric interpolant of the grid values (the DFT coefficients are that interpolant's Fourier coefficients). The paper also uses trigonometric interpolation to query states at off-grid points (Sec. 4, justified by Thm 3.3). That is an output-query rule analogous to N2's item 4.

4. exact_input_integration: raised from none to partial (weak and implicit). A hostile reviewer can argue that spectral layers already integrate exactly over a band-limited (trigonometric) reconstruction, and that this integral is unchanged under band-limited refinement. On that view N2's exact stem is only a first-order-hold / causal-SSM version of a known property. Caveats: the paper never states this as a claim. It treats the DFT as an approximation (the aliasing term E^(1), App. B). The pointwise lifting P comes before any kernel.

5. fixed_time_nonlinearity: none is correct for this paper. sigma_t, P and Q act on the input grid X(N). The Sec. 4.3 adaptive subsampling changes the evaluation grid during training (32 -> 64 -> 128) rather than fixing it. The only link is the cited prior work [1] Bartolucci et al. (arXiv 2305.19913, alias-free ReNO) and [22] Raonic et al. (CNO, NeurIPS 36; no arXiv id is given in this paper). Those evaluate nonlinearities on an upsampled grid or map inputs to a fixed internal grid, which is the spatial analogue of N2's fixed clock and of the fixed-grid resampling baseline. They need their own records and are likely rated higher than this paper.

6. refinement_invariance_claim: partial is confirmed. There is no exact invariance at finite N. The claim is an asymptotic rate, plus the definitional "discretization-invariant operator" statement in Sec. 1.2. The paper directly addresses N2's core question in the spatial setting: grid-evaluated nonlinearities cause dependence on the grid. N2 must cite it for the diagnosis.

7. grid_changes_tested: the record's "varying N" is imprecise. The tests use Gaussian random field inputs of regularity H^{s-}, s in {0.5, 1, 1.5, 2}, discretized at N in {32, ..., 2048}. These fields are not band-limited, so every change of grid is a real change in the measurements, with aliasing present. There is no lossless (information-preserving) refinement test, and no irregular or missing-sample test. Also tested: ReLU vs GeLU (ReLU limits the decay rate); non-periodic positional encoding (a regularity-0.5 channel that caps the decay below N^{-1}), which is relevant to N2 baselines that feed time as a channel; trained FNOs on an elliptic homogenization PDE and on a gradient map. knot_vs_measurement_distinction stays at none. App. A's decomposition into truncation and aliasing error (A.8, Remark A.5) is textbook, as the authors say. It supports labeling the aliasing and discretization-error inequalities as existing results (N2 item 6), but the paper never separates refinement that adds no information from real downsampling.

8. The notes should add that N2 must treat the N^{-s} discretization-error bound and the claim that pointwise nonlinearities amplify aliasing as prior results.

9. reported_numbers: none for HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM. This is confirmed.

10. code_url: https://github.com/mtrautner/BoundFNO; license not verified. Venue: arXiv only, no journal-ref.

verifications.corrections:
1. Title/venue. The version on arXiv HTML and in JMLR is titled "Neural Operator: Learning Maps Between Function Spaces With Applications to PDEs", JMLR 24 (2023), paper 21-1524.

2. The ratings should be raised under the hostile-reviewer default.
- exact_input_integration: none -> partial. The paper's whole template is a linear integral operator, or a set of linear functionals <w_j, a> of the continuum input, applied before or between pointwise nonlinearities (Eqs. 6, 10, 33 and the Sec. 5.1 paragraph). A reviewer would call N2's exact FOH quadrature an implementation choice within this template. However, the paper itself only uses Monte Carlo / Riemann sums (Eq. 14), Nystrom subsampling, or FFT on uniform grids. It never uses closed-form integration of an interpolant, and it never claims exactness. So partial, not substantial.
- fixed_time_nonlinearity: none -> partial. Table 1's "Interpolation" baseline (interpolate, then a fixed-grid NN) is explicitly listed as discretization-invariant. Sec. 5.1 proposes evaluating the input "independently of its discretization" and feeding linear functionals to a finite-dimensional network. The hidden-layer domains D_t are free hyperparameters (Eq. 6). The output can be queried at any point (requirement 2). In the App. E proof, sigma_1 acts on a function queried anywhere on D, not only at input nodes. That said, there is no physical-time clock, and in every implementation the nonlinearity is evaluated at the input grid points (Sec. 4, O(J) sigma cost; GNO/MGNO nodes are subsampled from the input grid).
- refinement_invariance_claim: stays partial. The claim is asymptotic convergence under nested refinement (Def. 1, Def. 4, Thm 8, proved via Riemann sums for a single layer in App. E). The empirical claim is approximately constant error "once enough resolution is used, but is not zero". There is no exact finite-grid invariance.
- knot_vs_measurement_distinction: stays none.
- overall: stays partial. The reviewer risk is high: the conceptual pattern (linear functionals of the input function -> fixed finite-dimensional network; interpolation -> fixed-grid NN) is explicitly stated.

3. time_handling "None" is incomplete. The index t in Eq. (6) is a layer index, not physical time (Sec. 3 footnote). In the Navier-Stokes experiments, FNO-3D treats time as an extra coordinate on a uniform grid ("convolution in space-time"). FNO-2D/U-Net/TF-Net/ResNet run autoregressively with a fixed Delta t (Sec. 7.3). There is no dt-as-step-size or dt rescaling.

4. input_reconstruction should be expanded: point evaluations plus Monte Carlo / Riemann quadrature (Eq. 14); Nystrom subsampling with interpolation matrices that "linearly extend" from the nodes (Sec. 4.1); DFT on a uniform periodic grid for FNO (Sec. 4.4); optional (x, a(x)) and Gaussian-smoothed input features (Sec. 3 Preprocessing). NN+Interpolation appears as a baseline column in Table 1. There is no exact integration against a PL/FOH reconstruction.

5. where_nonlinearity_evaluated is correct but should add: the lifting P is itself a pointwise (possibly nonlinear) map applied at the input points before any integral (Sec. 3; "for the theory ... it suffices that P is the identity map").

verifications.quotes_verified:
All 4 quotes are verbatim and attributed correctly, with small refinements. (1) Abstract, "The existing architectural solutions to prevent aliasing are partial since they do not solve these effects, that originate in non-linearities.": exact. (2) "For example, the outputs of non-differentiable operations such as ReLU can have infinite support in the frequency domain, thus aliasing will be induced for every finite upsampling factor.": exact. It sits in Sec. 2.1 (Methods, "Shift invariance and equivariance"), in the paragraph just before Algorithm 1; "Sec. 2" is acceptable. (3) Sec. 1 Contributions, "Specifically, the robustness of AFCs is certified for circular shifts and the ideal (Sinc) interpolation kernel.": exact. (4) Sec. 3, "Activation function" paragraph, "We replace the original GeLU activation with a polynomial function of degree 2, whose coefficients are trainable parameters, per channel": exact. The paper then gives Eq. (4), Poly_2(x)=a0+a1x+a2x^2.

Mechanism statements that need small fixes:
(a) Algorithm 1 uses Upsample_{(d+1)/2}, which is 1.5 for d=2. The implementation (Fig. 1 caption) uses "Up x2", "LPF: ideal LPF with cutoff 0.5" and "Down x2". So "2x upsampled grid" matches the implementation, but the theoretical requirement is (d+1)/2.
(b) The paper says the polynomial "expands the frequency response support by as factor d" (Fig. 2/12 caption). This is an upper bound on support, not "exactly".
(c) The first downsampling stage uses LPFPoly_2(x)=a0+a1x+a2x·LPF_{3/4}(x) (Eq. 5; App B.2, Eqs. 35-37) with no upsampling.
(d) The invariance also needs circular convolutions (circular padding), a periodic-signal assumption (Sec. 3; App C), alias-free LayerNorm that scales per layer rather than per pixel, and BlurPool built as an ideal DFT-domain LPF (Eqs. 2-3, 40-42).

Additional evidence I verified:
- Sec. 2.1: "Applying a pointwise non-linearity in the discrete domain is equivalent to sampling a continuous signal after applying the pointwise non-linearity — which may break the Nyquist condition and cause aliasing."
- Sec. 2.1: "This implies that pointwise nonlinearities applied in the discrete domain are generally not shift-invariant w.r.t. the continuous domain."
- Sec. 1 (describing Karras 2021): "Their method wraps the component-wise non-linear operations by upsampling and downsampling layers in an attempt to mimic the effect of applying the non-linear operations in the continuous domain".
- App B.1, Eq. 15: Recon(x[n])(t)=Σ x[n] sinc((t−nT)/T).
- Sec. 4.1: the internal representation is "shift-equivariant w.r.t. the continuous domain (up to numerical error)".
- Sec. 6.3.1: "information-loss makes guaranteed robustness impossible".
- Sec. 4.5.2: crop-shift "is not cyclic, includes data loss, and is even integer-valued".
verifications.strongest_non_novelty_sentence: Sec. 2.1: "Applying a pointwise non-linearity in the discrete domain is equivalent to sampling a continuous signal after applying the pointwise non-linearity — which may break the Nyquist condition and cause aliasing." A reviewer could combine this with the next sentence, "This implies that pointwise nonlinearities applied in the discrete domain are generally not shift-invariant w.r.t. the continuous domain." Together they say that N2's diagnosis is already established: nonlinearities evaluated per sample make the representation depend on the grid, even when every linear operator is exact on the continuous reconstruction. That diagnosis is N2's core question and the step-3 counterexample. Karras et al. 2021 (StyleGAN3) is the earlier source of the same principle, and the reviewer would cite both.
verifications.corrections:
Field-by-field corrections to the record:

1. input_reconstruction. The record says "Ideal sinc interpolation." More precisely, the model has no explicit input reconstruction step. The theory treats the input as samples of a band-limited, periodic continuous signal (Def. 1; App B.1 Eqs. 12, 15-16, sinc Recon). Inside each activation, sinc/DFT-domain "ideal upsampling" is used (App C, Eqs. 43-45). The guarantee assumes a perfect anti-aliasing filter before sampling (Sec. 6.3.2).

2. where_nonlinearity_evaluated. The nonlinearity is a pointwise polynomial evaluated on an upsampled copy of each layer's own sample grid: 2x in the implementation per Fig. 1, (d+1)/2 in theory. The first stage (LPFPoly_2) runs on the native grid. The evaluation grid is tied to the sample positions and moves with them under a fractional shift. It is not a clock fixed in physical coordinates. Invariance comes from polynomials preserving band-limits, not from separating the nonlinearity grid from the observation grid. This is the opposite design choice to N2 and is the main thing that sets N2 apart. It also means AFC does not work with ReLU/GELU, while N2 claims any network on its clock.

3. time_handling. None. The work is on 2D images; the 1D exposition is in spatial index.

4. invariance_claim. Exact, proved invariance of the output and equivariance of internal features to integer and fractional circular shifts (Props 1-2, App B). This holds under a sinc (band-limited) interpretation plus periodic boundaries. It is confirmed numerically: near-zero layerwise difference in Fig. 3 and 100% consistency in Table 1. Results are only empirical for zero-pad + bilinear-interpolation shifts and for crop-shift (Sec. 4.5).

5. grid_changes_tested. Circular integer, half-pixel and fractional shifts: T_integer, T_half, T_frac,k with k up to 7 (Eqs. 7-9). Fractional shifts are implemented as ideal upsample-by-n, shift by m, downsample (Sec. 4). Also tested: zero-pad + bilinear shifts (4.5.1), crop-shift with new content and information loss (4.5.2), and ImageNet-C with 1/7-pixel shifts (4.4). Nothing tests a resolution change, knot/density refinement, real downsampling of the input, or missing samples.

6. Overlap ratings. The record gave exact_input_integration none, refinement_invariance_claim none and knot_vs_measurement_distinction none; I raise all three to partial, as a hostile reviewer would. fixed_time_nonlinearity stays partial and overall stays partial.
- exact_input_integration: there is no time integration or SSM. However, the linear layers (circular conv, ideal LPF/BlurPool) are exact continuous-domain operators on the declared sinc reconstruction (App B.1 item 2, citing Karras 2021). That is the same "linear part is exact on the reconstruction" principle, applied to spatial filters rather than a closed-form FOH-integrated SSM.
- refinement_invariance_claim: AFC proves exact invariance when the same reconstructed continuous signal is resampled on a shifted grid. That is the same logical form as N2's claim, "a grid change that preserves the reconstruction gives an identical representation, even with nonlinearities". It differs only in the kind of grid change (shift, not density refinement) and the reconstruction class (band-limited sinc, not PL knots).
- knot_vs_measurement_distinction: AFC explicitly separates grid changes that satisfy the guarantee (circular shifts, ideal sinc) from those that change the information or break the reconstruction assumption. The latter are bilinear kernels and crop-shift with "data loss", where "information-loss makes guaranteed robustness impossible" (Sec. 6.3.1). The paper reports only empirical robustness for them. This is not N2's split into refinement, downsampling and missing samples, but the principle is the same.
- overall: stays partial. AFC has no temporal SSM, no fixed physical-time clock, no resolution or refinement test and no irregular sampling. It does anticipate N2's diagnosis and the general "exact on the declared reconstruction implies exact grid-invariance" framing.

7. Implications for N2. N2 must cite AFC and Karras et al. 2021 for the claim that per-sample pointwise nonlinearities break consistency with the continuous signal. N2 should present its minimal counterexample as a temporal, density-refinement instance of that known effect, not as a new discovery. N2's novelty has to rest on three points: (i) the grid for nonlinear updates is fixed in physical time and independent of the observations, rather than band-limit-preserving activations; (ii) the reconstruction is PL/FOH with exact knot-refinement invariance for arbitrary nonlinearities; (iii) the SSM stem integrates exactly over irregular observation times.

8. Minor fixes. The polynomial support expansion is "by a factor d" as an upper bound, not "exactly". Degree-4 polynomials were also tried (DeiT-tiny, Table 3).

9. code_url_and_license. https://github.com/hmichaeli/alias_free_convnets. I found no top-level LICENSE (raw LICENSE returns 404). The README only links a ConvNeXt license file, which also returns 404 on the main branch. The license is still unverified. Checkpoints are at https://huggingface.co/hmichaeli/convnext-afc.

10. reported_numbers. None relevant to HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM speech. ImageNet only: ConvNeXt-AFC is about 81.0% (81.03% adversarial, constant) vs 82.1% baseline. Cost: training 418 h vs 84 h and evaluation 9.16 vs 1.39 ms/sample on A6000 (Table 4). This is useful context that alias-free nonlinearities are expensive, relevant to N2's cost measurement.

verifications.corrections:
I keep all ratings from the original record: exact_input_integration partial, fixed_time_nonlinearity substantial, refinement_invariance_claim partial, knot_vs_measurement_distinction none, overall substantial. The factual corrections follow.

(1) VENUE. The arXiv abs page comment says "accepted for European Signal Processing Conference 2021 (EUSIPCO 2021)". I did not check page numbers in the proceedings.

(2) SECTIONS. The record leaves out Sec. II, but Sec. II-A is the source for the claim that the encoder ReLU runs on the frame clock. I read all of Sec. II.

(3) INVARIANCE CLAIM needs more detail:
- "Proposed" gives similar SDR from 12 to 48 kHz.
- "Proposed+" (with aliasing reduction) gives consistent SDR at every tested rate, 8 to 48 kHz. Sec. IV-B: "Proposed+ showed a consistent performance at all sampling frequencies".
- The evidence is empirical and measured at the level of task performance. The only representation-level check is Fig. 3, where the filter frequency responses at 16 and 32 kHz are "consistent". The paper states no exactness claim and no bound.
- The paper does frame SFI as a structural property: "we explicitly define an SFI structure to handle any sampling frequency without retraining" (Sec. II-C).

(4) GRID CHANGES:
- Training uses 16 kHz. The test tracks are produced by "down- and up-sampling" to 8, 12, ..., 48 kHz (Sec. IV-A). The resampling method is not stated.
- MUSDB18-HQ is natively 44.1 kHz (this comes from knowledge of the dataset; the paper does not say it). So the 20-44 kHz test sets hold real denser measurements with extra bandwidth compared with training, and only 48 kHz is an upsampling of the source. None of this is refinement of the same path.
- The paper does not test irregular grids or missing observations.
- Both the train and test signals are resampled beforehand, so resampling is part of the data protocol, not a baseline.

(5) INPUT RECONSTRUCTION. My reading, which the paper does not state: h[l]=T g(lT) followed by FIR filtering is a rectangle-rule (Riemann-sum) approximation of the continuous-time convolution, with the input implicitly treated as an impulse train. There is no ZOH, FOH or spline reconstruction. The encoder output would change under piecewise-linear knot refinement, because the quadrature error is O(T). The exact_input_integration rating stays partial: the concept of a continuous-time latent linear filter discretized per rate is present, but exactness is not. A hostile reviewer will say that exact FOH integration is a standard alternative discretization.

(6) FIXED-TIME NONLINEARITY:
- Every nonlinearity (encoder ReLU, the TCN masking module, and the mask product) runs on the 2.5 ms frame clock. The decoder is a linear transposed conv at the input rate, so no nonlinearity is applied per input sample. This makes the substantial rating strong, and a hostile reviewer could argue full.
- I keep substantial because the clock ticks must coincide with uniform sample instants aligned at t=0, and W = 2.5 ms × fs must be an integer. The paper does not state the integer condition; I inferred it. Every tested rate gives an integer W from 20 to 120.
- So the clock is not independent of where the observations are in general, and irregular grids are unsupported.

(7) KNOT VS MEASUREMENT. The paper treats low sampling rates specially (Nyquist-aware zeroing of channels, Sec. III-B). That zeroing targets aliasing of the discretized filter, which is an artifact on the model side. The paper never separates virtual from real samples, or refinement from decimation or missing data. I keep the rating at none; a weak partial is arguable.

(8) FOLLOW-UPS, which should get their own records because they are closer to N2:
- (a) The TASLP 2022 journal version, doi 10.1109/TASLP.2022.3203907, which the repo implements. Its README abstract says the SFI method "outperforms a conventional method based on signal resampling when the sampling frequencies of input signals are significantly lower than the trained sampling frequency". A resampling baseline therefore already exists in this line of work.
- (b) arXiv 2306.10718, Imamura et al., EUSIPCO 2023, "Algorithms of Sampling-Frequency-Independent Layers for Non-integer Strides". According to the search snippet only, it uses windowed-sinc interpolation to build continuous-time feature representations and to sample them at the desired stride. That separates the frame clock from the sample grid, but by approximate sinc interpolation. This is the closest precedent to N2's fixed clock.
- (c) A 2025 Signal Processing paper, "Stride conversion algorithms for convolutional layers and its application to SFI DNNs" (ScienceDirect S0165168425005365). Search result only; arXiv id unknown.
- The record's phrase "integer strides required (fixed by the 2023 follow-up)" is correct at snippet level.

(9) NUMBERS. The paper gives SDR in Fig. 2 only, as the mean of median SDR over 4 seeds, with no numeric tables. Settings: N=440, B=H=Sc=160, P=3, X=6, R=2; L=5 ms, W=2.5 ms. There are no HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM numbers.

(10) CODE. The repo is MIT licensed ("Copyright (c) 2022 TomohikoNakamura", verified) and implements the TASLP 2022 version, not the EUSIPCO 2021 paper.

What remains open for N2 against this line of work:
- closed-form exact FOH integration of a diagonal SSM, which gives exact representation invariance to virtual-knot insertion at arbitrary, non-uniform positions;
- a clock fully decoupled from irregular observation times;
- an explicit three-way separation of refinement, downsampling and missing data;
- an SSM backbone, and classification tasks.
N2 must cite this line of work and must not claim that fixed-physical-time nonlinear processing after a per-rate continuous-time linear front end is new.

All nonlinear computation runs on the frame clock m*S'*T', and S'*T' = S*T = 2.5 ms is independent of the input sampling frequency. That includes the encoder ReLU (Sec. II-B) and the whole mask predictor. The encoder conv and the decoder are linear. A hostile reviewer would say N2's fixed clock is exactly SFI Conv-TasNet's design, which this paper completes for non-integer strides. What N2 could still claim on this component: uniform grids only (the sinc interpolation of Eqs. 2 and 5 assumes a uniform period T'), no irregular or missing observation times, no SSM backbone, and the clock is tied to the signal start and padding P.

2. exact_input_integration stays partial; do not raise it. The principle is present: a continuous-time linear operator (latent analog filters, a modulated Gaussian, Eq. 13) whose output is evaluated at arbitrary physical instants. But every step is approximate and the paper says so:
- weights come from frequency-domain filter design approximating the analog response (Sec. II-A);
- K' is rounded (Sec. III-A);
- a finite windowed sinc is used (L=16, Kaiser, torchaudio defaults);
- anti-aliasing before sampling at m*S'*T' is deliberately omitted (footnote 1).
The implicit input reconstruction is bandlimited or sinc, not first-order hold. Nothing is integrated in closed form, and nothing makes the state provably unchanged under refinement. verifications.quotes_verified:

Additional verified evidence the record should carry:
(a) Sec. 3.4: "the resulting implementation of convolution is equivariant with respect to (real-valued) trigonometric interpolation." Corollary 1 states K(θ̂)(v^{N→L}) = (K(θ̂)(v))^{N→L} for any L ≥ M. This is a proved exact statement, but only for the linear convolution.
(b) Abstract: "propose an interpolation-equivariant adaptation of the architecture."
(c) Sec. 1: "In addition to interpolation of inputs to the training resolution, various other approaches have been proposed to address this issue". So resampling to the training grid is framed as the standard fix.
(d) Sec. 4.2: "the FNO performs worse for inputs with resolutions below 112×112, but only slightly diminishes for higher resolutions. We attribute this fact to the dimension reduction operations in the architecture."
(e) Repo README: "out_shape=[N,M]: resizng via trigonometric interpolation. Here, N,M can not depend on the input shape." This is a layer whose output grid is fixed whatever the input grid.
verifications.strongest_non_novelty_sentence: Sec. 4.2: "Applying trigonometric interpolation before a convolutional layer can be interpreted as an FNO-layer with predetermined output dimensions." Sec. 5 backs this up: "However, we have seen that the trigonometric interpolation of inputs outperforms all other considered approaches." Together these describe a model that resamples the input exactly, with a linear, interpolation-equivariant map onto a fixed grid, and then runs every nonlinearity on that grid. This is the spatial and spectral analogue of N2's exact stem plus fixed clock, and it beats the discretization-agnostic operator.
verifications.corrections:
1. VENUE. The record's "venue not verified" is resolvable. Crossref: SSVM 2023 (Scale Space and Variational Methods in Computer Vision), LNCS, pp. 236-249, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-31975-4_18. arXiv has only v1.

2. CODE AND LICENSE. The record's "Not recorded" is wrong. Paper footnote 2 says: "Our code is available online: github.com/samirak98/FourierImaging". On license: setup.py declares "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License". No LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, COPYING or LICENCE file exists on branch main (all return 404). So the license is MIT by classifier only, with no license file. The README describes a SpectralConv2d option (out_shape) that resizes by trigonometric interpolation to a fixed shape "can not depend on the input shape".

3. MECHANISM. The record's wording is imprecise.
- Converting a CNN into an FNO is done with the DFT of the zero-padded spatial kernel, not by interpolating it: Lemma 3, T(θ)=λF(θ).
- Adapting to other resolutions is done by spectral zero-padding of the parameters (Sec. 3.1), plus Nyquist splitting for even sizes (Sec. 3.3, Eq. 8). That amounts to real-valued trigonometric interpolation.
- FNOs are also trained directly (Sec. 4.1).
- Networks: FMNIST uses 2 conv layers, adaptive average pooling and a linear classifier. Birds500 uses a ResNet18 trained at 112x112 with striding replaced by trigonometric downsampling.

4. INPUT RECONSTRUCTION. The record conflates two uses.
- Trigonometric or bilinear resizing (a) generates the resized test data and (b) is the "rescaled to the training resolution" baseline.
- The FNO layer itself implicitly uses a periodic, band-limited trigonometric interpolant through the DFT on the torus, truncated to the N lowest modes (Eqs. 6-7).

5. INVARIANCE CLAIM. "Empirical; notes that..." understates it.
- Corollary 1 is a proved, exact equivariance of the linear convolution K under trigonometric interpolation (L ≥ M).
- The abstract says "interpolation-equivariant adaptation of the architecture".
- For the full network there is no exactness claim. The pointwise σ (Sec. 2.1, Eq. 1) is evaluated on the input grid, which breaks equivariance, and the paper never discusses this (the word aliasing does not appear).
- Consequence for N2: the FNO network is itself a small instance of N2's counterexample (exact linear part, per-grid-point nonlinearity).

6. GRID CHANGES TESTED. More precise version:
- Test sets are resized with trigonometric or bilinear interpolation to sizes both below and above the training size.
- FMNIST (native and training 28): about 3 to 59. Birds500 (native 224, training 112): about 5 to 215.
- FMNIST sizes above 28 are pure interpolation, i.e. information-free refinement. Sizes below are lossy downsampling.
- For Birds500, 112 < N ≤ 224 carries real extra information relative to training.
- The paper never separates these cases. The "none" rating for knot_vs_measurement_distinction stays; the asymmetry is only observed, never framed.
- No irregular sampling, random drop, or time axis appears anywhere.

7. RATINGS RAISED.
- exact_input_integration, none to partial: the DFT-based linear layer is exact on the trigonometric reconstruction and provably equivariant to lossless (band-limited) refinement. It is a spectral, periodic, uniform-grid analogue, with no FOH, no SSM and no causal integration.
- fixed_time_nonlinearity, partial to substantial: in the rescale-to-training-resolution pipeline, which the authors explicitly interpret as an FNO layer with predetermined output dimensions and which the code supports, every nonlinearity sits on a fixed grid independent of the input discretization. It is spatial, not physical time, and it appears as a baseline, not as the proposed method.
- refinement_invariance_claim stays partial: exact for linear layers, empirical (Fig. 4) for full networks.
- Overall stays partial: different domain, no FOH or SSM, no irregular or causal setting, no formal whole-model invariance theorem, no knot/measurement distinction. The architectural principle, however, is present.

8. NO_GO-RELEVANT OBSERVATION. The record's note should be sharpened. In the FMNIST "Data sizing: TRIGO" panel, the resample-to-28 curve is flat for every N > 28. That is exact invariance to lossless refinement obtained by plain resampling of the same reconstruction. By the same logic, point-sampling the FOH interpolant on a fixed clock is exactly invariant to inserting virtual knots, because the interpolant does not change. So refinement invariance alone cannot separate N2's exact stem from the mandatory fixed-grid resampling baseline. N2 has to show gains from integration between clock points (anti-aliasing, information between samples), or on real downsampling and missing data. Otherwise this paper's result supports a NO_GO.

9. REPORTED NUMBERS. The record's "Figure only" is correct: there are no tables. Approximate readings from Fig. 4:
- FMNIST, trained at 28: about 0.91 at 28. The rescale-to-28 curves stay about 0.91 for N > 28. The CNN falls to about 0.68 (TRIGO sizing) or 0.74 (bilinear) near N=59.
- Birds500, ResNet18 trained at 112: about 0.93 at 112. The CNN falls to about 0.22 (TRIGO) or 0.16 (bilinear) near N≈215. The FNO sits at about 0.87-0.88 there.
- Nothing on HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM speech.

1. MAJOR, solver: the record says "adaptive dopri5 in the experiments" and "adaptive by default". This is wrong.
   - App D.1 says every NCDE, GRU-ODE and ODE-RNN run used fixed-step RK4 (3/8 rule) through odeint_adjoint, with the step equal to the minimum adjacent time difference.

   - "Variable step size solvers" in Sec 6.3 describes torchdiffeq's default, not the settings used in the experiments.
   - Fix the mechanism field to: fixed-step RK4, h = minimum observation gap, f_theta evaluated at the RK4 stage times.

2. Upgrade fixed_time_nonlinearity from partial to substantial.
   - In uea.py, times = torch.linspace(0, L-1, L) is shared by every series, and dropped points are set to NaN (lines 97-102). The spline is then fitted per channel through the remaining points.
   - So in the 30/50/70% drop runs, f_theta was evaluated on a fixed index-time clock (h=1, stages at k, k+1/2, k+1). That clock does not depend on which observations survive.
   - Sec 6.3 also says solver steps "can be made across observations".
   - Caveats that keep this below full: the paper never states a fixed clock as a design principle, and the step rule h = minimum gap means inserting finer virtual knots would shrink h and change the clock. The discretised NCDE as implemented is therefore NOT invariant to refinement.

3. Consequence for N2: NCDE as run is effectively "point-sample dX/dt of a spline on a fixed grid, then an RK4-structured recurrent net". That places it in the class of the mandatory fixed-grid resampling + network baseline.
   - With h fixed independently of the knots, it would be exactly invariant to knots inserted on the spline (spline-consistent knots). This is an inference, not a claim in the paper.
   - What N2 has beyond NCDE must therefore come from (a) exact closed-form integration of the input between clock ticks, rather than RK4 point samples of dX/dt, and (b) a causal, local piecewise-linear reconstruction, rather than a global, non-causal natural cubic spline.
   - N2 should include a fixed-step NCDE as a close-work baseline.

4. Scope of the refinement invariance (refinement_invariance_claim stays partial). Remark B.13 covers only knots inserted on the spline itself. I checked this numerically with scipy's natural CubicSpline on 8 knots:
   - Knot inserted at the spline's own value: max difference 1.8e-15.
   - Knot inserted at the linear-interpolant (chord) value, i.e. N2's virtual knot: max difference 0.070, and still 1.8e-3 on the interval [5,7], which contains neither the new knot nor its neighbours. Natural splines are global.
   - So NCDE is not invariant to N2's piecewise-linear lossless refinement, even at the continuous level.
   - The paper's example uses collinear points, where both definitions agree. A reviewer may cite it anyway; the reply is that it covers only data that is locally linear.

NCDE already has the recipe: continuous reconstruction, integration against the path, nonlinear evaluation on a solver grid that is not tied to observations, deliberate identification of refined series, and intensity to mark real observations. What remains for N2 is narrow:
   - exact closed-form linear-stem integration over a piecewise-linear reconstruction;
   - an invariance guarantee for the discretised model, with tests;
   - refinement defined on the piecewise-linear interpolant, kept separate from downsampling/aliasing and from missingness;
   - the application to per-token nonlinearities in dt-rescaled SSMs.

This is not the raw-audio SC35 of S4/S5, and there is no resolution-change evaluation, so it is not a calibration point for N2's SC resolution task. The paper has no HAR, EigenWorms or PDM results.

2. MISSED App B.2.1. It is exactly the lossless-knot-refinement case: an extra observation (t_*, x_0) lying on a constant path gives the identical control under all four schemes. The authors frame this as a defect (non-injectivity) and restore distinguishability with c_i (B.2.2; Sec 1.1 "frequency of observations may carry information").
- refinement_invariance_claim goes partial -> substantial (hostile reading). Morrill et al. state that the control is identical after an on-path knot insertion. Combined with A.2, this gives exact invariance of the continuous-time solution. Caveats: it is shown only for constant data, framed as a flaw, never tested, and does not hold for the discretised model.
- knot_vs_measurement_distinction goes partial -> substantial. The paper explicitly separates "same path, extra point" (invisible without c_i) from informative observation frequency and from missing data (forward fill, Table 1 asterisk). It does NOT treat downsampling or aliasing at all.

3. exact_input_integration: none -> partial. The linear control is exactly the FOH reconstruction N2 uses. N2's stem, dz = Az dt + B dx, is itself a linear-vector-field Neural CDE driven by the linear control with a time channel. A reviewer can call N2's stem "a linear NCDE solved in closed form". Morrill integrate numerically only (dopri5 tol 1e-5/1e-3, or rk4), with no closed form and no SSM.

4. fixed_time_nonlinearity: keep partial. The vector field is evaluated continuously in path time, so it is grid-agnostic only in exact arithmetic. That means one RK4 step, and 4 vector-field evaluations, per observation interval. This is a per-observation nonlinear update, and inserting a virtual knot adds a step. dopri5 uses min_step=0.5. Sec 2.2 recommends jump_t, but the released code never passes it; the record's claim that jump_t is used should be framed as a recommendation, not as what the experiments did.

5. Record inference on Hermite: correct. For non-constant data, natural cubic, cubic Hermite with backward differences, and rectilinear (forward-fill staircase in index parameterisation) are all NOT invariant to inserting knots on the linear interpolant. Only the linear control preserves the path in general. B.2.1's "all schemes identical" holds only for its constant example.

The N2 mechanism (closed-form linear stem plus nonlinearity on an observation-independent physical clock, giving exact invariance of the COMPUTED model) and the downsampling/aliasing separation are absent. N2 must not claim either of the following as new: (a) continuous-time invariance of CDE-type models to on-path knot insertion, or (b) the idea that an extra on-path point is indistinguishable unless observation counts are encoded. Both must be credited to Kidger et al. 2020 / Morrill et al. 2021-22. N2's claim must be restricted to exact invariance of the discretised network and to the fixed-clock design.

7. Venue: TMLR 2022 ('On the Choice of Interpolation Scheme for Neural CDEs', OpenReview caRBFhxXIG) is confirmed via ML Anthology and ORA. I did not read the TMLR text, and it may differ from arXiv v1.

8. Code: the paper repo (jambo6/online-neural-cdes) has no top-level license. It vendors torchcde, which is Apache-2.0.

(b) fixed_time_nonlinearity: raise from partial to substantial. verifications.corrections:
1. RAISE fixed_time_nonlinearity from substantial to full, at the level of mechanism.
- If you pass physical t, the window boundaries sit at t0 + j*W. They are independent of where the observations are, and the neural vector field is evaluated only on the window-index clock.
- NRDE Section 3 states this design: points r_i, 'typically space[d] ... equally far apart', and eq. (9), which holds LogSig_{r_i,r_{i+1}}(X)/(r_{i+1}-r_i) fixed on each [r_i, r_{i+1}).
- Caveats: the default t=None is the sample index, and example/logsignature_example.py uses that default. The clock is anchored at the first observation t0, not at 0. The last window is cut off at t_n.

2. RAISE refinement_invariance_claim from none to partial.
- The code comment (lines 47-48) states the key fact: signatures treat the linear infill as information-free, including infill at virtual points the code inserts itself.
- The README states the classical reparameterisation-invariance result for CDEs in continuous time.
- Nobody claims or tests invariance of the whole discretised pipeline to knot refinement. NRDE's experiments use regular sampling ('Every problem is regularly sampled, so we take t_i = i', Section 4).

3. The record's inference is CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY, with two caveats.
- Result: with physical t and time as a channel, inserting 600 random collinear virtual knots into a 400-point path changed the logsig_windows output by at most 3.6e-17 relative (depth 1) and 4.0e-16 relative (depth 2), in float64.
- Caveat (a): 'exact up to floating point' is slightly overstated. Line 31 uses torch.allclose with its defaults (rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-8). A virtual knot within about 1e-5*|t| of a window boundary replaces that boundary. With t around 36.5, a knot at boundary+1e-4 gave an absolute difference of 9.7e-4, while a knot at boundary+5e-4 gave 7e-15.
- Caveat (b): with the default index clock (t=None), refinement changes the number of windows (41 became 101). There is no invariance in that case.
- Real 2x downsampling changed the output by 8.7e-2 relative, as expected.

4. The notes' last sentence is WRONG for the logsig pipeline and right only for a plain NCDE on raw data.
- After logsig_windows, LinearInterpolation(coeffs) uses the default t, so grid_points are 0..m-1.
- That makes the README's recommended step_size = min gap = 1, and jump_t = grid_points = the window indices. Both are independent of the original knots.
- With a fixed solver, or any deterministic solver, the downstream computation depends only on the logsig path, which is invariant as shown in item 3.

- Virtual window-boundary knots and genuinely missing observations both become NaN and go through the same linear fill.
- Leading and trailing missing values are filled with a constant.
- Nothing separates refinement from downsampling or dropped observations.
- The companion NRDE paper does contrast its windows with 'naive subsampling of the data' for NCDE (Section 4). That distinction belongs to that paper's record, not to torchcde.

6. exact_input_integration stays at substantial rather than full.
- What matches: an exact closed-form functional of the piecewise-linear reconstruction on each window. It is invariant to collinear knots by Chen's identity and reparametrisation invariance.

- NRDE depth 2, step 4: 83.8 ± 3.0% (best overall)
- NRDE depth 3, step 4: 76.9 ± 9.2%
- NCDE step 1: 62.4 ± 12.1%, 22.0 h
- NCDE step 4: 66.7 ± 11.8%
- NCDE step 128: 48.7 ± 2.6%
- ODE-RNN (folded) step 4: 35.0 ± 1.5%

RATINGS: I raised two ratings and the overall.
(a) fixed_time_nonlinearity goes from partial to substantial. The general Log-ODE formulation takes the intervals as an arbitrary time partition. Sec 1.3: "Given a set of intervals {[r_i,r_{i+1}]} satisfying t_0=r_0<...<r_m=t_n, the Log-ODE method replaces a CDE with an ODE on each interval". Sec 1.2 says outright that network forward passes are decoupled from the observations: "By decoupling the number of forward passes through their neural network from the number of observations...". Figure 2 draws roughly evenly spaced r_i on a time axis, with irregular, channel-asynchronous observations in between. Its caption says the observations "represent irregular samples", and each interval covers a different number of samples. A hostile reviewer would say N2's "nonlinear updates on a fixed physical-time clock" is just the Log-ODE method with r_i=j·Δ_c. It stays below full because the paper never fixes r_i in physical time: C.2 fixes the interval to a number of observations.
(b) refinement_invariance_claim goes from none to partial. The paper claims qualitatively, without testing, that the model depends on the data only through X ("unaware of when the time series was observed"). Sec 3.1 adds that "(22) and (3) are equivalent when X is a linear interpolation", i.e. depth-1 Log-NCDE is the same as an NCDE on a piecewise-linear X. For a CDE with piecewise-linear control on a fixed physical-time solver grid, exact invariance to collinear virtual knots follows immediately. Likewise, the log-signature of a piecewise-linear path over an interval does not change when collinear points are inserted, which is a standard rough-path fact (Chen / reparametrisation invariance). N2 must present both as existing results. The paper itself never states, proves or tests this invariance.
(c) overall goes from partial to substantial. Taken together, the paper already describes N2's pattern: an exact closed-form integral summary of the piecewise-linear input (the log-signature) over time windows, followed by nonlinear dynamics on a window grid decoupled from the observations. What N2 can still claim as its own: a diagonal LTI SSM stem with memory across windows instead of per-window truncated log-signatures; a stated and tested exact-invariance result; the three-way split into refinement, downsampling and missing data; and the resampling baselines.
exact_input_integration stays at substantial. calc_paths computes the signax signature of point sequences, which is the exact signature of the piecewise-linear path. It first prepends a zero basepoint, and each window starts at the previous window's last point. knot_vs_measurement_distinction stays at none.

- time_handling: time is index-based whether or not the time channel is used. With include_time=True, the time channel is itself created as (T/L)·arange(L) in create_uea_dataset, with T=1. The solver runs from t0=ts[0] to t1=ts[-1]. The intervals are ts_train[0, 0:L:stepsize] with T appended.

For EthanolConcentration it is step 1 with dt0 = 1/1752, and for the NCDE on EigenWorms dt0 = 1/17985. In those two cases there is about one Heun step per observation, which is exactly the per-observation nonlinear update N2 argues against. The vector field reads a piecewise-constant log-signature driver found with searchsorted on the intervals. y0 = linear(x0).

1. Where the nonlinearity sits is misstated for the time-series (UEA) setting. The UEA code runs a single LogLinearCDE layer (generate_model.py, "_linear_ncde"). It has a linear init layer and linear flows. The states at the interval boundaries are averaged by index (`ys = jnp.mean(ys, axis=0)`) and then passed through a linear layer and softmax. The only nonlinearity is that final readout, and there are no tanh/LayerNorm blocks between layers. The A.3 block (linear, tanh, LayerNorm, skip; the code also has optional GLU and dropout) is the stacked PyTorch model used for A5 and formal languages. There the nonlinearity is applied at every token.

2. Input reconstruction differs by setting.
- UEA: omega^X = X. The log-signature (depth 1 or 2) is computed with signax on the piecewise-linear path over chunks of `stepsize` samples. It is exact for the piecewise-linear path up to the truncation depth.
- A5 and formal languages: Eq. 22 sets the increments to (1, X_{t_j}) * dt. The token is treated as a piecewise-constant rate, which is ZOH-like. The code uses a constant dt = 1/40.

3. Time handling.

- The time channel is (T/n)*index with T=1, and only EW, EC and HB include it. MI, SCP1 and SCP2 have no time channel at all.

4. Every implementation uses first-order flows, including the Log-ODE steps. The code sets `flows = log_flows + I` (JAX) and `y + A(inp*dt)y` (PyTorch, Algorithm 1 lines 6 and 12). The affine term is also approximated (Eq. 48).

5. Rating changes.
- exact_input_integration goes from partial to substantial. Eq. 2 is the exact closed-form flow over the piecewise-linear interpolant. For D-SLiCE with diagonal A^i, that is exactly a diagonal linear system integrated in closed form, and the interval log-signatures are exact path functionals. Only the implementation is approximate. N2 cannot claim exact piecewise-linear integration as new. What is not covered is N2's additive-input diagonal LTI stem, whose exact integration SLiCE only approximates (Eq. 48).
- fixed_time_nonlinearity goes from none to partial. Sec 5.3 explicitly claims "decoupling the number of recurrent steps from the number of observations". The Log-ODE interval boundaries act as a coarser update/output clock, but it is counted in samples, not physical time.

For S4 (ξ=∫X dt) this reduces to piecewise-constant X, which is ZOH. But the paper's own chained and experimental Linear CDEs are driven by dX (eq. 11, eqs. 76-77, and ω=ξ=(t,X_t) in Sec 6), so a linearly interpolated X is integrated exactly by the same formula. By integration by parts, a dX-driven linear state is an affine function of N2's X·dt-driven state and X_t, so a reviewer can argue that N2's exact first-order-hold (FOH) stem is already covered. What is not in the paper: an explicit FOH formula for ω=t, ξ=∫X, and any exact solve in the experiments.

In the code, the A5 block applies ReLU(linear_mix) per token after the LCDE, followed by residual and LayerNorm, and the toy models put a GeLU between stacked layers per token. fixed_time_nonlinearity therefore stays partial.

2. input_reconstruction is wrong. The piecewise-linear and piecewise-constant extensions in Def. B.5 (App. B.1.2) extend the discrete KERNEL κ_{D_M} from D_M to [0,1]. The input path is not reconstructed there. The Remark after Def. B.5 says the linear extension is "used to prove uniform convergence" and the constant one handles "positive semidefinitess". In the theory the input is a given continuous path x ∈ 𝕏, i.e. W^{1,2} with x(0)=0 (Sec. 1.2 / App. A.1), evaluated at the partition points. No rule for rebuilding a path from observations is given. The polynomial interpolant x̄ in the proof of Prop. B.16 is only a proof device. The code works on the raw samples: it takes torch.diff of the samples, divides by dt from linspace(0,1,T), and raises "Different Grid case not yet implemented. Use torchcde package to interpolate the data" when X and Y have different lengths. In practice, then, the input is taken on the observation grid, and resampling or interpolation is the suggested fix.

Hostile reading: for a fixed D_M and a piecewise-linear x, the finite controlled ResNet depends only on x(t_i) for t_i in D_M. Inserting virtual knots therefore leaves it exactly unchanged. This is N2's fixed-clock property with a trivial pure-increment stem, the A=0 special case of an exact linear SSM stem. The paper never states this, never fixes D_M independently of the data, and keeps only the increment at each cell end, so it throws away the shape of the path inside a cell. This paper names that scheme only as future work.

It sits in Section 3.2 (Properties of the log-signature, paragraph "Invariance under time parameterization"), not in Section 2, which is "Related Works on Signature Feature" in both v1 and v2. The record's sections_read entry "2 (log-signature properties ...)" should also read 3.2. This quote is also not evidence of exactness. The exactness sentence is 3.2: "Then it is proved that the log-signatures of X and X~ are equal Lyons (1998)", with the same result in App A.3 Lemma A.3, Eq. (10). That invariance is under time re-parameterization of the same interval (a non-decreasing surjection lambda: J->J), which is a speed change. It is not a statement about knot refinement or sampling.

Two further passages support it. Model 4.1 defines the Logsig-RNN as a map "from an input path x∈BV(J,E)", with the RNN run only on the N cells of a partition D of J. Sec 4.2 says D need not coincide with the observation timestamps ("When D coincides with timestamps of the input data ..."). A hostile reviewer would argue from these that the architecture is already there: exact closed-form integration of the linear interpolant over fixed windows, with nonlinear recurrence only on those windows. Refinement invariance would then be a one-line corollary of the definition.
verifications.corrections:
(a) Section attribution. The frame-rate quote and the "log-signature properties" reading are in Sec 3.2, not Sec 2 (see quotes_verified).

(b) time_handling. Math and code differ. On paper, D=(u_k) is "a time partition of J", i.e. physical time. In the released code (model/logsignature.py), the partition is by sample index: `t_vec = np.linspace(1, nT, n_segments+1)` rounded to integers, where nT is the padded buffer length and not the true sequence length. No timestamps are ever passed. Segment boundaries snap to observation indices instead of being interpolated at u_k. The time channel, `add_time`, is `torch.linspace(0,1,length)`, i.e. normalised index time. So the nonlinear clock is a fixed NUMBER of segments per sequence, relative and index-based, not tau_j = j*Delta_c. The code uses N1=50 and N2=30 in two stacked layers; the paper's Chalearn optimum is N=4.

(c) where_nonlinearity_evaluated. This needs sharpening. In the released GCN-Logsig-LSTM, GraphConv is an MLP of Conv2d 1x1 + BatchNorm2d + ReLU, followed by `F.relu` at EVERY FRAME before the first log-signature layer. That is exactly N2's per-observation nonlinear update. The paper calls EL "linear". The Accumulative Layer, however, is a cumulative sum over frame index (App E), not a time integral, and it scales with the number of samples. The log-signature itself is a degree-M polynomial functional of each segment's path, computed exactly: Chen/BCH, App A Lemma A.2, Eq. (9).

(d) grid_changes_tested. The record undersells this. The paper text says test-time "discarding/repeating", and the Fig 4 caption says "drop/insert rates". But the released feeder implements "add" as `cv2.resize(..., cv2.INTER_LINEAR)` to (1+r)x length, applied only at TEST time. config/ntu_sub/test_joint.yaml sets robust_add: True, add_rate: 0.5, with trained weights. So there is a test-time linear-interpolation upsampling robustness check, which is closer to a virtual-knot test than stated. It is still not an equal-path refinement, for three reasons: cv2's half-pixel resampling drops the original knots and cuts corners at the kinks; the edges are clamped; and the padding tiles the sequence into a longer buffer. The test config also references `model.gcn_logsig_var`, which is missing from the repo. "Repeating frames is a ZOH-type virtual knot" is also imprecise. With index time, which is all the code has, a repeated frame inserts a stationary segment. That is a time re-parameterisation, not a knot on the same physical-time path. Without a time channel the log-signature is exactly invariant to it, but index boundaries shift, and TL and AL are not invariant.

(e) My numeric check (depth-2 log-signature, L=37, midpoint knots inserted on the same piecewise-linear path):
- Whole-path log-signature difference: 7e-15, i.e. exactly invariant.
- The released index-partition layer: invariant for N=4 and N=6, but a difference of 2.39 for N=5, because rounded boundaries move.
- ReLU(linear) before the log-signature: difference 0.27.
- Accumulative Layer: difference about 4e3.
So the paper's actual pipelines are NOT refinement-invariant, even though the Def 4.1 path-level log-signature layer is.

(f) Rating justification.
- exact_input_integration: substantial. There is exact closed-form integration of the first-order-hold (linear-interpolation) path over fixed windows, and the signature is the solution of a universal linear controlled differential equation (App A, Thm A.1). But the functional is a truncated log-signature, not a diagonal LTI SSM.
- fixed_time_nonlinearity: substantial. The RNN runs only on D, independent of the observations, in the definition. But the per-frame ReLU/GCN, the index-based D, and the absence of any rule that all nonlinearities must live on the clock keep this below full.
- refinement_invariance_claim: partial. There is exact re-parameterisation invariance (a different transformation), plus "A higher frequency of input data ... makes the computation of l_k more accurate" (4.1), plus empirical robustness. There is no explicit exact statement about knot refinement and no equal-path test. A hostile reviewer could push this to substantial, because invariance is immediate from Model 4.1 being defined on paths.
- knot_vs_measurement_distinction: partial. The paper lumps "missing data and varying frame rate" together (5.3) and treats drop and insert symmetrically. Only the separate 5.4 interpolation experiment hints at the difference.
- overall: substantial.

(g) reported_numbers. These are skeleton data only. Chalearn2013: EL-Logsig-LSTM+aug 92.94±0.21; best D_el=30 gives 93.38. NTU120 (GCN-Logsig-LSTM)2: X-Sub 75.8±0.35, X-Set 78.0±0.46. "HAR" in this paper means human action recognition, not UCI HAR. None of it calibrates UCI HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM.

(h) code_url_and_license: github.com/steveliao93/GCN_LogsigRNN (PyTorch, depends on signatory). The clone has no LICENSE file, and the Chalearn TF/EL code is not included.
