verifications.corrections:
1) Version and year. All cited items (Example 13, Corollary 1, the "Time augmentation" subsection, "Paths with jumps") come from v2 (arXiv 1603.03788v2, 17 Jan 2025). They are not in the 2016 v1. Record the version, or cite v2 as 2025.

2) time_handling should not be "Not applicable". v2 §2.1 "Time augmentation" adds t_i as a channel, and also t̂_i = t_i − t_0 and Δt_i (Table 1(b)). Without a time channel the signature discards speed: §1.5 says "one can never recover from the signature the exact speed at which the path is traversed". v1 §2.2.2 adds an "auxiliary time parametrisation vector". Correct entry: time is either a channel (time augmentation) or absent, in which case the signature is reparametrisation-invariant. There is no dt step size and no fixed grid.

3) where_nonlinearity_evaluated should not be "Not applicable". The pipeline is data → path → signature → features → learning algorithm (§2.2). The learner (v1: logistic regression with LASSO) is applied once per sample to the whole-path signature, so no nonlinearity is evaluated at each observation. The only nonlinearity sits at one terminal time. In the theory (§1.2), CDEs with nonlinear vector fields are also determined by the signature, i.e. the nonlinearity acts continuously in time.

4) input_reconstruction is incomplete. The paper uses PL interpolation (eq. (31)) and also rectilinear (axis) paths built with auxiliary points. v2 §1.5 "Paths with jumps" adds: "if X is piecewise constant with finitely many jumps, the signature of X^δ is the same as that of the piecewise linear path connecting the jumps". So for the signature without a time channel, ZOH with Marcus-type straight jumps gives the same result as PL.

5) Ratings.
- fixed_time_nonlinearity: raise from none to partial. This is a degenerate single-tick case: the nonlinearity acts only on a path functional at the fixed time T, never per observation. A multi-tick fixed physical clock inside a deep model is NOT in this paper.
- refinement_invariance_claim: raise from partial to substantial. The paper states exact reparametrisation invariance, states that CDE solutions at time t are determined by S(X)_{a,t}, and includes time augmentation. Its remark on auxiliary points (v2 §2.1b: "it is not important how the rectilinear path is precisely parametrized over [t_i,t_{i+1}] due to the parametrization invariance") shows that the placement of non-data knots does not matter. Everything needed to derive stem invariance under lossless knot insertion is there. It is not stated as "knot insertion" and not tested, and it says nothing about models with intermediate nonlinearities.
- knot_vs_measurement_distinction: raise from none to partial (weak). Auxiliary points (the "empty red circles") are explicitly distinguished from data points. v1 §2.2.2 encodes missing values with an indicator channel plus forward fill, separate from observed points. The paper does not discuss downsampling, aliasing, or refinement versus loss of real measurements.
- exact_input_integration: keep partial. The paper gives a closed-form signature of a PL path, and notes that the signature itself solves a linear CDE. It gives no SSM or matrix-exponential FOH formula; exact FOH discretisation is classical control theory and must be cited elsewhere.
- overall: keep partial. The math behind the N2 invariance lemma is textbook here. The architecture (SSM stem plus a multi-tick fixed-clock deep network), the refinement/downsampling/missing taxonomy and the experiments are not in this paper.

6) reported_numbers should not be "None". v1 §2.2.1 Table 1 reports a synthetic ARMA(1,1) two-class task using a level-2 signature and logistic regression with LASSO: accuracy 0.92 on the training split (70%) and 0.90 on the test split (30%). v1 §2.4.1 also cites Field et al. finance results (KS/ROC). Nothing is reported on HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM.

7) Notes refinements.
- The one-line identity e^{aΔ}⊗e^{(1−a)Δ}=e^{Δ} holds because both factors are exponentials of the same vector, so they commute.
- Without a time channel, invariance holds for ANY knot placed on the segment (arbitrary time).
- With a time channel, or for the N2 stem, the inserted knot must lie on the segment in (t,u) space, i.e. at the interpolated value at its own time. The N2 stem is NOT invariant under reparametrisation (it has dt drift). It is invariant only under lossless refinement.
- N2 must label its stem-invariance lemma as a corollary of Chen's identity, the reparametrisation invariance and §1.2 of this primer. Novelty can then be claimed only for: the fixed physical-clock placement of nonlinearities in a deep SSM; the explicit separation of refinement, downsampling and missing observations; and the tests.

Fixed-window log-signature models are a closer threat on the fixed-time nonlinearity component: Neural RDEs (Morrill et al. 2021, arXiv id believed to be 2009.08295, not verified in this task), Log-NCDE (Walker et al. 2024) and the generalised signature method's windows. In these, exact path functionals are computed over fixed windows and a nonlinear vector field is evaluated at the window points. This primer does not cover them. Their records must be checked separately.

verifications.corrections:
1) Raise fixed_time_nonlinearity from substantial to full. The Log-NCDE's nonlinear vector field (Eq. 7), or the Log-SLiCE decoder at h_{r_i}, sees the input only through Φ over a physical-time partition π that does not depend on observation times. C.1 draws π "independently of the observation times". In the UEA runs, π is a uniform grid: Table 4 gives the Log-ODE step (e.g. EigenWorms depth 2, step 12) on regularly sampled series, and C.3.2 holds that grid fixed when observations are dropped. So N2's 'fixed physical clock' is already a special case. N2 differs only in using a uniform clock with a deep-SSM backbone.

2) Input reconstruction needs a caveat. The record's 'rectilinear/ZOH-like' holds when time is a continuously observed channel (Sec. 2.4, and the synthetic C.1, which also drops count coordinates). In the UEA experiments, C.3 says "time is treated as a discretely observed variable when included in the driving path, and there are no continuously observed variables." Each event is then one straight-line increment in (time, values[, counts]). The realised path is therefore the piecewise-linear interpolation of (t_i, x_i) up to reparametrisation, with each segment assigned to the query interval that contains its right endpoint. C.3.1 also says observation-aligned depth-1 updates are "equivalent to solving the CDE exactly with a linearly interpolated observation path."

My own derivation, not stated in the paper: with time as a discrete channel and no counts, inserting a collinear (FOH) virtual knot leaves G unchanged, since exp(λa)⊗exp((1−λ)a)=exp(a). This holds whenever the knot falls in the same query interval as the next real observation. It fails only when the knot crosses a partition point, because segments are not cut at the r_i. The record's statement that FOH knots break the invariance is therefore too strong. The real gap to N2 shrinks to cutting FOH segments exactly at the clock boundaries, plus using an LTI-SSM stem instead of a truncated log-signature. The paper does not say whether the UEA runs use count coordinates.

3) exact_input_integration stays substantial. The interval summaries are exact depth-N truncated log-signatures computed via Chen's identity. For the nonlinear Log-NCDE, however, the hidden-state update is an approximation (Eq. 7, "h_{r_{i+1}} ≈ h̄"). It is closed-form only for the SLiCE variants. There is no learnable linear-SSM stem and no FOH exponential-kernel integral.

The same section continues: "This separation is what allows a model to be simultaneously expressive (through its input-dependent components) and extrapolative across sampling regimes (through the analytic time-handling of the discretization)." verifications.corrections:
1) Authorship: on arXiv the paper is not anonymous. The authors are Taylan Soydan, Miguel A. Bessa, Dirk Mohr and Rui Barreira (ETH Zurich AIMM; Brown). Only the acknowledgments are hidden, and the README says 'NeurIPS 2026 submission'. The LICENSE does read 'Copyright (c) 2026 Anonymous' (MIT). The arXiv id and date are confirmed; v1 is the only version.

2) input_reconstruction is incomplete. Bilinear (Tustin) discretization is also offered: Fig 3 caption, 'both ZOH and bilinear are possible'; disc ∈ {zoh, bilinear} in the Table 4/5 search spaces; discretize_bilinear in the code. Bilinear is not exact integration of any reconstruction. All best UEA configs use zoh (Table 3). There is no FOH or linear-interpolant integration anywhere.

3) The code's ZOH index convention differs from the paper. The scan operator (A_j*A_i, b_j + A_j*b_i) gives x_k = Λ̄_k x_{k-1} + B̄_k u_k, with step_k = t_k - t_{k-1} (step_scale_from_indices; tides_collate step_s = [t_0, diff(t)]). The code therefore holds u_k on (t_{k-1}, t_k], using the right-endpoint value, and y_k = Re(C_k x_k) + D u_k already includes u_k. The paper's App B instead holds u_k on [t_k, t_{k+1}). The step is also scaled per mode: Δ̃_p = exp(log_step_p)·Δ_k, with log_step initialized in [0.001, 0.1]. This scaling preserves the semigroup property.

4) The 'My analysis' claim needs qualification. The first SSM layer's state at the original timestamps is unchanged by an inserted knot only under all of these conditions: (a) forward scan only; (b) BatchNorm in eval mode, since train-mode statistics over batch×time change when tokens are added; (c) the knot carries the held value, which in the code is the right-endpoint sample; (d) we look only at states, not at the new outputs.
- The bidirectional scan (used in the random-drop runs and several UEA configs) reuses Λ̄_k, built from the gap t_k - t_{k-1}, for the backward transition k+1→k. That is an off-by-one gap under irregular sampling, so the backward direction is neither exact ZOH nor knot-invariant.
- The classifier readout is TIDESClassifier: head(h.mean(dim=1)). This mean is over token count, not time-weighted, so the pooled feature changes under knot insertion even if every state were invariant. This matters for N2's output/query rule.

5) where_nonlinearity_evaluated, additions: Re(Λ_k) passes through a per-token nonlinear reparameterization (-exp, stable or softplus), with RMSNorm, so it is not literally the affine form of Eq. 5. There is an optional deep GLU encoder g^(d_enc) per token. There is also an optional causal conv1d+SiLU in the code (conv_kernel_size, default 0). All of these are per observation.

6) Physiome-ODE (tides_collate.py) is more damaging for knot_vs_measurement than the record says. Missing channel values are zero-filled with no mask channel; the code comment reads 'zeros propagate naturally'. Forecast query timestamps are merged into the timeline as zero-valued input tokens, with step = Δt normalized to [0,1]. Queries and missing entries therefore enter as observed zeros that change the ZOH path. This is the opposite of N2's separation. Compare Broader impact: 'without engineering an explicit time-encoding pipeline or maintaining separate logic for missing observations'. The rating of none is confirmed.

7) The random-drop protocol in the paper does not match the released code. uea/main.py samples keep_indices once per run. The same indices are used for every sequence and for train, val and test, at a single random_percentage (all released search grids set 1.0). There is no per-step resampling and no r_train≠r_test sweep. App F's protocol ('a different random 50% ... at each training step', 'fixed dropped indices per sequence', the r_test sweep) cannot be reproduced from the release. Steps are integer index gaps. The Fading Flash core (App C.2) is a real-diagonal SSM with no BN, GLU or dropout. It uses the same 40-token sequence under a global Δ, so it tests a rescaled continuous signal and target, not path refinement. The Mamba_S-with-Δ-as-a-channel setup applies only to Fading Flash and random drop; the Mamba/S6 numbers in Table 1 are copied from Walker et al. on uniform grids.

8) reported_numbers: all verified. The timing setting in Table 8 is batch 8, 1 channel, about 100k params, 4 layers, 24 GB Quadro RTX 6000, generic PyTorch scan. At L=1k, TIDES takes 59.9 ms / 1,223 MB versus RFormer 22.3 ms / 531 MB. At L=5k, TIDES takes 173.3 ms / 5,924 MB versus 380.1 ms / 11,508 MB. The paper has no numbers for HAR, Speech Commands resolution change or PDM.

9) Ratings: I keep all of them. Hostile direction: exact closed-form ZOH is a special case of exact input integration, and Sec 2.1 plus the 'by construction' extrapolation claim and the drop-rate robustness are what a reviewer would cite. Both justify partial rather than none for those two components. Lenient direction: there is no FOH, no fixed physical-time clock, and no claim of exact representation invariance. Invariance is only empirical robustness, tested on random index drop and on global Δ rescaling. So neither of those components reaches substantial.

verifications.corrections:
1. exact_input_integration should go from partial to SUBSTANTIAL, taking the hostile reviewer's view.
- S5 Eq 6, with a per-step Δ_t (Sec 6.3), integrates a diagonal continuous-time LTI SSM in closed form over a piecewise-constant hold at physical intervals.
- In the code, both A_bar_k and B_bar_k are rebuilt per step from exp(log_step)·step_rescale·Δt_k (pendulum branch, ssm.py line 290).
- Because exp(ΛΔ) composes over split intervals, inserting a virtual knot that repeats the held value leaves the layer-1 state at the original knots exactly unchanged.
- N2's first-order-hold (piecewise-linear) stem differs only in hold order.
- N2 must therefore present closed-form ZOH/FOH integration and the linear-part split invariance as prior or textbook results, as the user request requires. The novel part has to be the fixed-clock nonlinearity and readout. S5 never states the reconstruction or claims exactness, so the rating is not FULL.

2. Mechanism details:
- The per-step interval multiplies the learned per-state Δ vector (P entries); it does not replace it.
- The first step uses Δt=1: fwd_timesteps prepends 1, which is not physical time.
- In the pendulum branch, integration_timesteps goes to EVERY layer (seq_model.py line 88), so every layer is dt-aware at observation tokens and applies a per-token nonlinearity.
- On the main branch, StackedEncoderModel accepts integration_timesteps but ignores it. Variable-interval code exists only on the 'pendulum' branch (README lines 82-83). Reuse that branch for the dt-only baseline.

- Not tested: lossless refinement, upsampling, and drop-rate sweeps.

- BatchNorm (the default for most tasks, G.2) also computes training statistics over tokens.

verifications.access_self: FULL_TEXT_SECTIONS. I read arXiv HTML 1909.07782 end to end: Abstract; Sec 1; Sec 2 Related Work; 3.1; 3.2; 3.2.1 (Eqs 1-5); 3.2.2; 3.2.3 (Eq 6); 4; 4.1.1-4.1.2; 4.2 (Table 1, Fig 2 caption); 5; App A.1.1 (Table 2); A.1.2; A.2.1; A.2.2; A.3 (Table 3); A.4 (Table 4). I also read the official code and README in mlds-lab/interp-net: src/interpolation_layer.py (both layers) and a grep of src/multivariate_example.py. The LICENSE file is MIT; I read it directly. To check the calibration numbers, I also read the mTAN paper (arXiv 2101.10318): Table 2, Table 4, and the dataset paragraphs in Sec 4.
verifications.quotes_verified: All 4 quotes appear verbatim in the paper and are attributed to the right sections. (1) "The $T$ reference time points $r_{t}$ are chosen to be evenly spaced within that interval." is in Sec 3.2. (2) "...the intensity functions $\lambda_d$ to capture information about where observations occur in time." is the last sentence of Sec 3.2.1, after Eq 5. (3) "In this work, we conduct experiments leveraging a GRU network as the prediction network." is in Sec 3.2.2. (4) "we randomly sample 10% of the observations points from each time series to create a sparse and irregularly sampled data." is in App A.1.2. The code confirms the fixed physical-time grid: interpolation_layer.py sets `ref_t = np.linspace(0, self.hours_look_ahead, self.ref_points)` when not in reconstruction mode. It also fixes kappa=10 (comment "# kappa = 10"), uses alpha = softplus(learned) per channel, and computes intensity as exp(logsumexp(...)), which equals the unnormalized sum of kernel weights. The mTAN numbers check out. mTAN Table 2 gives IP-Nets PhysioNet AUC 0.819±0.006, MIMIC-III 0.8390±0.0011, and Human Activity accuracy 0.869±0.007, and Table 4 repeats them.
verifications.strongest_non_novelty_sentence: "Also similar to Li & Marlin (2016) and Futoma et al. (2017), the interpolation layers in our architecture produce regularly sampled interpolants that can serve as inputs for arbitrary, unmodified, deep classification and regression networks." (Sec 2). Pair it with Sec 3.2: "The $T$ reference time points $r_{t}$ are chosen to be evenly spaced within that interval." Together these let a reviewer say: "Mapping irregular observations onto a fixed, evenly spaced physical-time grid with a closed-form continuous-time layer, then running any standard network only on that grid, is IP-Nets (and GP adapters before it). N2 only swaps the interpolator."
verifications.corrections:
RATING CHANGES.
(a) fixed_time_nonlinearity: raise from substantial to FULL. Every learned nonlinear computation (the GRU/LSTM, and even the lambda-ratio normalisations of Eqs 3 and 5) is evaluated only at the reference points r_k. These points are evenly spaced over a fixed physical interval (0 to 48 h) and do not depend on where the observations fall. Evidence: Sec 3.2, Sec 5 ("prediction network that operates over the regularly spaced and fully observed, multi-channel output"), and the code's np.linspace. The grid is specified by a count T over a fixed-length window rather than by a spacing Delta_c. For fixed-length windows these are the same thing. N2 therefore must not claim "nonlinear updates on a fixed physical-time clock, independent of the observation grid" as novel.
(b) exact_input_integration: raise from none to PARTIAL on hostile grounds. The interpolation layer plays the same role as N2's stem. It is closed-form, works in continuous time, is linear in the observed values for fixed times, and runs before any network, with no per-observation recurrent nonlinear update. It is NOT exact integration of a reconstructed path. There is no ZOH, FOH or spline path and no SSM. Eqs 1-4 are sums over observation points, not integrals. So the exactness, which is N2's actual contribution, is absent.
(c) refinement_invariance_claim stays NONE. The paper claims no invariance or equivariance to sampling rate and runs no resolution-shift test. It is non-invariant by construction (my analysis, not claimed in the paper). lambda = sum_j exp(-alpha (r - t_j)^2), so every inserted knot, virtual or real, strictly increases it. sigma and gamma are density-weighted averages, so inserting knots on the linear interpolant re-weights them unless x(t') happens to equal sigma(r). Under dense uniform refinement, sigma only approximately converges to a kernel-weighted path average, and lambda grows roughly with point count.
(d) knot_vs_measurement_distinction stays PARTIAL, and that is generous. On the related side, Sec 2 separates irregular sampling from missing data ("A closely related (but distinct) problem is performing supervised learning in the presence of missing data"). The paper also models observation times as an informative point process, and App A.2.1 excludes unavailable data "not taken into account at all". But it has no concept of a virtual knot, and it does not separate refinement from downsampling. Its intensity channel deliberately treats every point as information, which is the opposite of N2's premise.
(e) overall stays PARTIAL. N2's central claim is exact invariance to lossless knot refinement, obtained from an exact stem plus a fixed clock, with a three-way grid separation. IP-Nets has none of that claim. It does fully cover the two-stage template: continuous-time stem, then a fixed reference grid, then any network.

FACTUAL CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD.
(1) The notes call IP-Nets "the oldest clear instance" of a network on a fixed reference grid. The paper itself credits Li & Marlin 2016 (GP adapter, NeurIPS) and Futoma et al. 2017 (MGP-RNN) with producing regularly sampled interpolants for unmodified networks (Sec 2 quote above). Those should be cited as earlier instances.
(2) Mechanism detail. The first layer outputs sigma, gamma and lambda (Eqs 2-4). The network input is chi (the cross-channel smooth interpolant, Eq 5, weighted by rho and lambda), tau = gamma - chi, and lambda. kappa is fixed at 10 in the code, not learned; alpha_d and rho are learned. The code's cross-channel layer departs slightly from Eq 5: it subtracts a per-channel mean before applying the rho map. This does not affect the ratings.
(3) Grid changes tested. MIMIC-III's own cohort is naturally irregular (53,211 admissions, 12 vitals, first 48 h, 5-fold CV). The Harutyunyan MIMIC benchmark is in A.4. UWave uses a fixed random 10% subsample from Li & Marlin, applied as dataset construction, not as a train/test shift. Training also holds out 20% of observed points at random for the interpolation loss (A.2.1), which is a random-drop augmentation. No knot-refinement, upsampling or cross-resolution test is reported.
(4) Reported numbers. Own MIMIC-III: AUC 0.853±0.007, AUPRC 0.418±0.022, length-of-stay MedAE 2.862, EV 0.245 (Table 1). Harutyunyan benchmark with an LSTM prediction net: AUC 0.8610, AUPRC 0.5370 (Table 4). UWave appears only as a plot in Fig 2 (accuracy vs training time, with the GP adapter similar and about 50x slower), so no values can be extracted; the README runs it with ref_points=128. The mTAN "Human Activity" 0.869±0.007 is per-time-point 11-class accuracy on UCI "Localization Data for Person Activity" (12 channels, 50 time points, Rubanova et al. 2019 preprocessing). It is NOT UCI HAR smartphones and must not be used to calibrate HAR. The paper has no numbers for UCI-HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands resolution change, or PDM.
(5) Code license confirmed MIT (LICENSE: "Copyright (c) 2019 Machine Learning for Data Science").
(6) Venue: OpenReview r1efr3C9Ym (ICLR 2019); the arXiv posting is 1909.07782. The record is correct here.

IMPLICATION FOR N2. IP-Nets is effectively a learned instance of the mandatory fixed-grid-resampling baseline. N2 should add a variant with an RBF/IP-Net-style stem on the same fixed clock and show that its representation moves under virtual-knot insertion, driven by lambda and the density re-weighting, while the exact FOH-SSM stem does not. N2's novelty must rest only on the stem's exactness, the refinement-invariance theorem and test, and the refinement/downsampling/missing separation.

verifications.corrections:
1) Year and version: arXiv v2 is from 2016 and Sci Rep from 2018; the section and equation numbers in the record are arXiv v2's (mapping above).

2) fixed_time_nonlinearity should go from none to partial. On PhysioNet and MIMIC-III, the RNN steps are the observation time stamps s_t. v2 Table A.3 gives a mean of 68.91 and 35.89 steps and a max of 155 and 150 over 48 h, more than an hourly or 2-hourly grid would give. On the synthetic Gesture data, however, the time series is regularly sampled. Missing entries are injected at random per entry: supplementary Sec 3.3 gives a 50% average missing rate, with correlation to the label of 0, 0.2, 0.5 or 0.8. GRU-D runs on that fixed grid with masks, so its nonlinear updates happen at fixed times that do not move when observations are dropped. Latent ODE Sec 5 also describes Che et al. as 'discretize the timeline into equal intervals, impute missing data, and then run an RNN'. A hostile reviewer can call this a fixed clock plus masked missing values. It is really the fixed-grid resampling+mask baseline that N2 already has to include, not an architectural split between input integration and the clock. The paper also resamples to a fixed grid for its non-RNN baselines: hourly on PhysioNet, 2-hourly on MIMIC-III, with forward/backward fill. Sci Rep adds GRU on CubicSpline, SoftImpute, KNN, MICE, MF, PCA and MissForest imputed data. So resampling/imputation followed by an RNN is already a baseline inside this paper.

3) Input reconstruction: there is no continuous path. Each missing entry gets a per-variable decayed forward-fill toward the training mean (v2 Eq5 / Sci Rep Eq11), and only at the time steps that exist. W_gamma_x is diagonal and W_gamma_h is full.

4) Time handling: the record is right that decay depends on delta. More precisely, delta_t^d is the per-variable time since variable d was last observed, and it accumulates across steps where d is missing (v2 Sec 2 definition / Sci Rep Eq2). It is not the step size.

My own derivation (not in the paper): suppose a virtual step with m=0 is inserted between two real observations. It adds one GRU sigmoid/tanh update and an extra V*m input. It also adds one extra hidden decay, and because delta accumulates, the combined decay exponent becomes roughly W(2*delta_a + delta_b) instead of W(delta_a + delta_b), before the max and bias. So elapsed time is counted twice. This makes GRU-D a clean per-observation counterexample for N2 step 3, not a threat to it.

5) Invariance claim: it is not just 'None'. GRU-D is built to be sensitive to the sampling pattern ('informative missingness'), and its Limitations section says the gains depend on the missingness being informative. A reviewer can turn this against N2: refinement invariance could throw away label-relevant sampling information. N2 must argue that virtual knots carry no information by construction, while real missingness may.

6) Grid changes tested: add the Gesture random drop on a regular grid, early prediction by truncation (Sec 3.4 / Sci Rep Discussions), and training-set subsampling (not a grid change). The paper has no knot refinement, no downsampling, no rate change and no upsampling.

7) Reported numbers: the record's list of other papers' numbers is mostly not about GRU-D and partly mislabeled.
- 'Latent ODE Human Activity 0.806' is actually GRU-D's number: Latent ODE Table 7, per-time-point accuracy 0.806±0.007. Human Activity is UCI 'Localization Data for Person Activity', not UCI HAR smartphones. The record's S7 'HAR (person activity)' is the same dataset, not UCI HAR.

  - Caveat: NCDE App D.3 says its GRU-D baseline filled missing values with natural cubic splines, not with the GRU-D decay imputation.
- Latent ODE Table 6, PhysioNet mortality AUC: 0.818±0.008.
- Own numbers, v2 Table 2 (mortality AUC): MIMIC-III 0.8527±0.003, PhysioNet 0.8424±0.012. Table 1 (multi-task AUC): 0.7123 and 0.8370.
- The GRU-D paper itself has no numbers for UCI HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands at changed resolution, or PDM.

verifications.corrections:
RATINGS
(a) fixed_time_nonlinearity: raise from substantial to FULL. As written, the method feeds every learned nonlinearity (attention, MLP) with tokens indexed by 'a fixed set of time points' (Sec 3.1). The workshop Eq 2 says explicitly 'Fixing a set of times T={t_1,...,t_Lbar}'. N2 allows 'any network' on the clock. For fixed-length data, a fixed window count on [0,T] is the same thing as a fixed Delta_c. The code deviates (see below), but reviewers judge novelty against what the paper describes.
(b) refinement_invariance_claim: raise from partial to SUBSTANTIAL. The record quoted only the hedged Prop 3.1. The paper also makes unqualified claims:
- Sec 3: the local component is 'a type of convolutional filter that is invariant to the sampling rate of the signal'.
- App B: '(ii) being invariant to the sampling rate of the signal'.
- Contributions: the mechanism 'is provably robust to irregularly sampled data'.
- Abstract: 'robust to changes in the sequence length and sampling frequency'.
Exact invariance to virtual knots is never stated or tested. But it follows in one line from Eq 8, because M(X) depends only on X-tilde at fixed t_k and virtual knots leave X-tilde unchanged. A hostile reviewer would call N2's theorem a trivial corollary.
(c) exact_input_integration: keep SUBSTANTIAL. RFormer computes exact truncated PL signatures (App A.1, Eq 16 and 22), which are fixed features, not learned kernels. Hostile argument: the state of a linear CDE/SSM driven by the time-augmented path is a linear functional of its untruncated signature, so N2's stem is a learned linear readout of the object RFormer computes truncated. N2 is still genuinely new in learned exponential decay without truncation.
(d) knot_vs_measurement_distinction: keep PARTIAL. Workshop footnote 1 acknowledges that aliasing is below Nyquist. App F.2 notes that a level-1 signature on the PL path 'corresponds to naive downsampling'. But the paper merges reparameterization, irregular sampling and random drop into one 'robustness' claim. It has no virtual-knot test, and in the public UEA code the drop mask is the same at train and test.
(e) overall: SUBSTANTIAL, and a hostile reviewer could argue near-full: 'N2 is RFormer with the signature replaced by a linear SSM and the Transformer replaced by a deep SSM.' N2's defensible deltas:
- a learned diagonal SSM stem;
- a causal deep SSM on the clock;
- stating exact refinement invariance and testing it;
- the three-way separation of refinement, downsampling and missing data.

CODE FACTS (fixes to the record)
- The record says windows are 'snapped to the last observed index before the boundary'. That is only partly right. Global features come from iisignature streamed format, where stream[k] is the signature of points 0..k+1 (I checked this). So a global window ends at observation idx+1, the first observation at or after the boundary.
- Local-tight windows are data[idx_i:idx_{i+1}) with an exclusive end. The segment from idx_{i+1}-1 to idx_{i+1} belongs to no window, so local windows do not tile the PL path. The last window is shortened by indices[-1]-=1.
- step=max(x)/num_windows uses the largest kept timestamp, so the window grid shifts when the last point is dropped.
- The local end is capped at int(max(x)), which is a time value used as an index.

MY TEST
Setup: public sig_utils.py, iisignature 0.24, L=200, d=3 random walk, 10 windows, level 2. I inserted collinear midpoints, which leave the PL path unchanged.

verifications.corrections:
1) Citation. The Appendix B quotes come from Remark B.13, which directly follows Def. B.12. The record's placement is right; cite it as 'Remark B.13'.

2) Solver grid. Replace the vague 'solver grids are often aligned with knots in practice' with what App D.1 and the code say.
- Every NCDE experiment used fixed-step RK4 (3/8 rule) through torchdiffeq odeint_adjoint.
- The step size equals the minimum time difference between adjacent observations. In code this is step_size = min(diff(times)) over the shared grid; for UEA data the grid is times=linspace(0,L-1,L).
- So in the 30/50/70% drop experiments, f_theta was evaluated on a fixed regular grid (step 1, the original sample index, with RK stages at 1/3 and 2/3). That grid is the same for every per-series drop pattern: the nonlinear evaluations were already decoupled from which observations were present.
- This is why I raise fixed_time_nonlinearity from partial to substantial under the hostile default. The continuous-time model has no per-observation nonlinear update (Fig. 1, Sec 3.4, Sec 6.3), and in practice it ran on a fixed clock that does not move with the drop pattern.
- What NCDE does not have: (a) its step rule depends on the minimum spacing of the time grid, so adding virtual knots at finer spacing shrinks the solver step and changes the numerical output; (b) between steps the input enters through RK samples of dX/dt at stage points, not through an exact closed-form linear integral; (c) it states no clock-based invariance claim.
- This is N2's best defence. Numerically, NCDE's invariance holds only in continuous time and up to solver error, and its default discretization is not refinement-invariant.

3) exact_input_integration stays partial. The model is a Riemann-Stieltjes integral over the reconstructed path (Eq. 3, Eq. 5), so it is exact in continuous time. But it is nonlinear (f_theta(z) dX), it is solved numerically, and it is not closed-form.

4) Refinement invariance. The paper's example uses collinear points only. By uniqueness of the natural cubic spline interpolant, though, any knot inserted at a point sampled from the spline itself leaves X unchanged; this is my own reasoning, not a claim in the paper. A reviewer can therefore extend Remark B.13 to general lossless refinement, which supports rating refinement_invariance_claim as substantial.
- The rating is not full: the paper does not claim numerical invariance and never tests knot refinement.
- The paper's other stated invariance (Sec 6.1, tree-like or reparametrisation invariance) is why time is added as a channel.
- With the intensity channel (Sec 3.5; cumulative count, code cumsum(~isnan)), invariance to refinement is deliberately broken if virtual knots are fed in as observations. That channel is exactly NCDE's switch between treating a point as a virtual knot or as a measurement, which supports rating knot_vs_measurement_distinction as substantial.
- NCDE does not separate real downsampling or aliasing from random missingness. Only random drop is tested.

5) Grid changes tested: random per-series drop of 30/50/70% (CharacterTrajectories); PhysioNet sepsis with vs without intensity; regular Speech Commands. verifications.corrections:
1. RAISE fixed_time_nonlinearity from none to partial. The original record did not read Sec.3.2. There, 'Impulse and mollified impulse method' (p.260; Grubmuller et al. 1991, Tuckerman et al. 1992) applies the nonlinear slow force only as kicks at the step points t_n and t_{n+1} ('kick p_n^+ = p_n + h/2 f_slow(q_n)'). Between kicks it propagates the linear part exactly: 'For linear fast forces (3.36), the "oscillate" step can be computed exactly'. Ex.2.12 also has the exponential Euler method evaluating g only on a constant grid ('we consider constant step sizes h_n = h only'). So the pattern 'exact linear flow plus nonlinear updates only on a fixed step grid' is established. What H&O lack is a nonlinear clock decoupled from an observation or knot grid: the forcing is a known function, and the grid belongs to the integrator. N2 must not present 'exact linear flow + nonlinearity at fixed physical times' as new. The only candidate novelty is that the clock is independent of where the input was observed.
2. Fix the exactness argument. The record says exactness 'follows from the Theorem 2.7 error bound, which vanishes when f^(p)=0'. Theorem 2.7 assumes f^(p) in L1(0,T). A piecewise-linear f with kinks has f'' made of Dirac masses, so the global hypothesis fails. Exactness instead follows directly from the construction (2.9)/(2.9b): the 2-node Lagrange interpolant at c=(0,1) reproduces f exactly on any step where f is affine. The per-step defect in the proof also involves f^(p) only inside each step. The condition is that every real kink must be a step endpoint. That is exactly N2's condition: stem steps must include all real observation knots, and virtual knots on an affine segment make no difference. N2 should state this condition and credit H&O (2.9), Ex.2.6 and (2.4).
3. refinement_invariance_claim stays partial. H&O make no invariance claim and test no grid changes. But stem-level refinement invariance is an immediate corollary of exactness plus the semigroup property (2.4) and the step-sequence independence in Theorem 2.7. N2 may claim at most the invariance of the full model: the stem, sampled at a fixed clock, followed by nonlinear layers and the output-query rule. Stem invariance alone is not new.
4. knot_vs_measurement_distinction stays none. H&O have no notion of observations, reconstruction, downsampling, aliasing or missing data.
5. overall stays partial. A hostile reviewer could argue substantial for the theory: FOH exactness, step-sequence independence and fixed-step nonlinear splitting all exist, so the invariance theorem is a short corollary. But H&O do not have the combination, the observation-grid decoupling or the invariance claim.
6. Add to where_nonlinearity_evaluated: exponential RK stages G_nj = g(t_n + c_j h_n, U_nj) (eq.2.20c); exponential Adams interpolates g at past step points (eq.2.69); impulse and MTS methods kick at fixed macro-steps (Sec.3.2).
7. Extra priority and cost points. Sec.6: Hersch (1958) 'proposed new schemes that are exact for linear problems with constant coefficients'. Sec.5 intro: with constant step sizes the matrix functions can be computed 'once and for all'. N2's saving from precomputing phi-weights on a fixed clock is therefore not new either.
8. Sign convention. H&O write u' + Au = f, so an SSM x' = Lambda x + B u maps to A = -Lambda with z = h Lambda. The stem is s_{n+1} = e^{h Lambda} s_n + h[(phi1-phi2)(h Lambda) B u_n + phi2(h Lambda) B u_{n+1}]. H&O do not discuss cancellation in the small-|z| recurrence (2.11), so N2's small-dt stability handling (series or Kassam-Trefethen style evaluation) needs a separate citation.
9. Naming note confirmed. Mamba-3 (arXiv 2603.15569) calls its non-exact rule 'exponential-trapezoidal' and claims it is 'novel for structured SSMs used in deep learning'. H&O's exponential trapezoidal rule is the exact FOH rule. N2 should cite H&O Ex.2.6 and explicitly distinguish the two rules.

(b) The FOH defect is bigger than "only the phi_2 part". The exact FOH step is h_{k+1}=e^{AΔ}h_k + A^{-1}(e^{AΔ}-I)B x_k + A^{-2}(e^{AΔ}-I-AΔ)B (x_{k+1}-x_k)/Δ. I keep all the ratings. The record is accurate, but it needs these additions and refinements.

(a) Exact input integration is 'partial', and a hostile reviewer would push it higher. S5's recurrence x_k = Ā_k x_{k-1} + B̄_k u_k with ZOH (eq. 6) is exact integration of a piecewise-constant path. In the code, the step for sample k uses the preceding interval, so u_k is held over (t_{k-1}, t_k]. By the semigroup property, S5's linear SSM state is therefore already exactly unchanged when virtual knots are inserted on that ZOH path. The paper never states or tests this, and it treats ZOH as a 'discretization method' (Sec. 2.1, with bilinear offered as an alternative), not as a reconstruction. N2 must not present exact linear refinement invariance itself as new. Only the FOH stem plus the fixed-clock separation of the nonlinearities can be claimed, and this invariance should be labelled as a known ZOH/semigroup result.

(b) The record misses other per-token, grid-dependent operations N2's counterexample can cite. These are the D u feedthrough at every step, batch/layer norm between layers (G.1), and above all the mean pooling 'across the sequence length dimension' before the decoder (G.1). An unweighted mean over tokens depends on sample density even when every layer is linear.

(c) The refinement-invariance claim is 'partial'. S5 only claims zero-shot usability at a new rate via Δ rescaling, shown empirically. All ratings are confirmed. The record needs these fixes:

1. invariance_claim understates the paper. The Abstract says outright that the kernels are "resolution invariant by construction". A hostile reviewer will cite that line, so the record should quote it. The claim covers only the linear kernel, and only approximately: it needs Δ rescaling plus a bandlimit. It is not a network-level claim. The paper itself says (Sec.1) that "performance suffers when moving between resolutions due to aliasing artifacts in the kernel". Table 4 shows the output is not invariant: CIFAR-10 S4ND scores 93.10 at base→base, 88.77 at mid→base and 73.71 at low→base. This is why refinement_invariance_claim stays at partial rather than substantial.

2. grid_changes_tested is incomplete.
   - Table 4 also has low→mid.
   - Every lower-resolution image comes from the base image by torchvision bilinear resize with antialiasing on (App. B.3). So a zero-shot test at higher resolution feeds more real samples. None of it is knot refinement of the same reconstructed path.
   - There is no random drop, no missing-observation test and no irregular sampling. Irregular and non-uniform sampling is only listed as future work (Sec.6). The ImageNet and HMDB-51 runs use one fixed resolution.
   - Progressive resizing uses low→base 80-20 on CIFAR-10 and low→mid 16-4 on CelebA.
   - Caveat: the checkpoint for each test resolution is picked at "the epoch where it performs best at the test resolution in question" (App. B.3.1). The zero-shot numbers are therefore optimistic.

3. input_reconstruction: the paper never states a reconstruction. It samples the kernel with "standard discretization rules ... to minimize the error" (Sec.3). In the current state-spaces/s4 main, the DPLR kernel (the legs/fourier inits) uses bilinear, and the diagonal kernel defaults to disc='zoh'. ZOH is exact only under a piecewise-constant hold, which N2 already counts as prior work. Nothing here does exact FOH/PL integration, so exact_input_integration = none. A hostile reviewer could say "partial via ZOH", but that belongs to S4D/S5, not S4ND.

4. mechanism: the printed rule in Sec.4.2, "for any n such that a_n·Δ < α/2, mask out C_n", has the inequality the wrong way round compared with the prose and the code. The code keeps a mode only when dt·|Im a_n|/(2π) < α/2 and zeroes C otherwise. The mask uses the training dt (dt/rate), so it does not depend on the test rate. The record's paraphrase, masking modes above the cutoff, matches the intended behaviour. Sweep values from App. B.3.1: α in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, ∞}. Progressive resizing uses α = 0.1/0.2 on CIFAR-10 and 0.1 on CelebA. The ablation reports drops of 20+ points without bandlimiting.

5. where_nonlinearity_evaluated is correct. The CIFAR backbone is the S4 isotropic backbone "identical to the one used by Gu et al. [21]" with S4ND swapped in (App. B.3), and the CelebA backbone is ConvNeXt. Both apply pointwise nonlinearities at every pixel of whatever grid they get, including after the S4ND stem downsampling. There is no fixed clock. fixed_time_nonlinearity = none.

6. knot_vs_measurement_distinction stays partial, but only just. The paper covers aliasing on two sides: data ("sampled images with more distant objects are more likely to contain power at frequencies above the Nyquist cutoff", Sec.1) and kernel ("aliasing artifacts in the kernel"). It never names lossless refinement or virtual knots, and it never keeps them apart from real downsampling or missing data.

     - base→base 93.10 / 91.9 / 92.2
     - mid→mid 88.80 / 87.2 / 86.5

verifications.quotes_verified: Both quotes are real and attributed to the right place. verifications.strongest_non_novelty_sentence: "in both 1D and 2D, RelErr_T(N) decays with the resolution N, improving with input smoothness at first ... but eventually saturating in the case of activation functions with finite Sobolev regularity (e.g., ReLU)." (Sec.5.1, Results; Figures 2(a)-(b).) With Theorem 4.1's recursion, a reviewer can say it is already known and bounded that SSM-kernel layers with a pointwise nonlinearity at every grid point give grid-dependent outputs, and that the activation's regularity limits resolution consistency. That covers N2's counterexample and motivation. It does not cover N2's exact-invariance construction. A runner-up is Sec.4.1: "Theorem 4.1 and above lemmas show that the discretized operator remains a faithful approximation of its continuous counterpart as the grid resolution N increases."
verifications.corrections:
Overall the record is accurate and its ratings hold. The corrections and additions are:

(a) Sections read. The record lists only Abstract / Sec.4 / Thm 4.1 / Sec.5.1. The paper also has App. J, K and L, which matter here. App. L deliberately under-resolves sinusoids u_k = sin(2πkx+φ), with k in {4,...,128} and L in {16,...,1024}. It marks a Nyquist threshold L≈2k and reports an error plateau below it. This is the paper's only explicit treatment of an under-resolved (aliasing) regime, and it is the best support for the "partial" rating on knot_vs_measurement_distinction.

(b) The rate "N^{d/2-s}" in the record is only the Fourier-cutoff case (beta = d/2 - s < 0). For kernels whose spectrum decays algebraically, beta = max{d/2 - s, d - alpha}. The paper states that raw SS-NO kernels decay only like ||xi||^{-1} ("finite Sobolev norm up to a constant s<..."), so the cutoff assumption does not hold for them as they stand. The full bound is N^beta * B * (A^T - 1)/(A - 1), which grows geometrically with depth T.

(c) Where the grid dependence comes from (Eq.63, App. E.1). The error enters through E^(1), the Riemann-sum or aliasing error of the linear convolution applied to the exact v_t, and through E^(2), the propagated error. Both then pass through the Lipschitz activation sigma. The paper says "we do not discretize the function space" (Sec.4): sigma acts pointwise on functions over the continuous domain. So the nonlinearity does not create error by itself. It lowers regularity, which is why ReLU saturates, and the next layer's grid sum then aliases the non-band-limited sigma(v). This is essentially the mechanism behind N2's counterexample (reconstructing sigma(h) from samples at the knots). N2 should therefore cite this paper for the grid-dependence phenomenon rather than claim it as new.

(d) The record's "time_handling: Uniform spatial grid of size N" needs more detail. There is no time axis and no dt. The domain is the periodic torus T^d, and the kernel is non-causal and two-sided (K_+ and K_-, Eq.4). The kernel is a closed-form damped oscillatory exponential that can be evaluated at any grid offset. That makes the parameterization resolution-agnostic, which is only analogous to dt rescaling. There is no sequence classification task.

(e) Grid changes tested, to add: App. J uses trained ReLU SS-NOs on Burgers. Inputs at resolution 1024 are subsampled to L in {16,...,1024}, and the log-log slopes are -1.9436, -1.9428, -2.0006 and -1.9976 for T = 1, 2, 4 and 8. Sec.5.2, App. K and Thm 4.5 cover additive input perturbations (noise delta), and Thm 4.5 separates the input-perturbation term from the discretization term. Every coarse grid is a real subsample of a fine field (GRF fine grid 8196 in 1D as printed, 2048 in 2D). The paper never tests virtual-knot or lossless refinement of the same reconstructed path, upsampling, random drops, missing observations or irregular grids. The method used to interpolate coarse states onto the fine grid is not specified in the text I read.

(f) Ratings. exact_input_integration = none: the convolution is a grid sum over samples, and no interpolant is integrated in closed form. fixed_time_nonlinearity = none: sigma is evaluated on the same grid as the input. The phrase "output resolution 1024/8192" in App. J/K/L is ambiguous, but the main text evaluates the model on the coarse grid and lifts the states afterwards, so there is no separate clock. refinement_invariance_claim = partial: the paper claims only approximate convergence as N grows, and never exact invariance. knot_vs_measurement_distinction = partial, and weak: it separates aliasing from error propagation, noise from discretization, and resolved from under-resolved (Nyquist) regimes, but never virtual knots from real measurements or missing data. overall = partial. Nothing here would justify raising any rating.

(g) Reported numbers: there are no HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM results. The only numbers are the App. J slopes (R^2 = 0.9793, 0.9698, 0.9829, 0.9821) and the parameter counts (20993, 33473, 58433, 108353 for T = 1, 2, 4, 8).

(h) Code: I found no repository link. CC BY 4.0 is the arXiv paper's license, not a code license.

(i) The SS-NO architecture itself comes from Koren & Lanthaler (2025). That paper should get its own record, since it may make its own resolution-invariance claims for spatiotemporal settings.

verifications.corrections:
1. Section attribution. The "tree-like invariance / blind to speed" quote and the discussion of time as a channel and the initial value network are in Sec. 6.1 (Discussion: Considerations), not Sec. 3. Sec. 3 only defines X_{t_i}=(x_i,t_i) (eq. 3) and z_{t0}=ζθ(x0,t0).

2. where_nonlinearity_evaluated is inaccurate.
- The paper does not use "adaptive or fixed" solvers decoupled from observations. All experiments use fixed-step RK4 (3/8 rule) through torchdiffeq odeint_adjoint, with step size equal to the minimum gap between adjacent observations (App. D.1).
- The released code sets this as the default: metamodel.py L116-118, step_size = time_diffs.min().
- dopri5 appears only as an aside about tanh activations.
- So the nonlinear vector field is evaluated on a uniform physical-time grid starting at t0, not interrupted at each observation (Sec. 6.3). But the clock is derived from the sampling: inserting a virtual knot that creates a smaller gap changes the step and therefore the numerical output. The implementation is not refinement-invariant.
- The sampling-independent clock (Delta_c fixed a priori) is a real point of difference for N2. A hostile reviewer will still call it a trivial hyperparameter choice (a user-set step_size), which is why I rate this component substantial.

3. The invariance claim is narrower and different from N2's.
- Remark B.13 sits inside the topology/seminorm used for universal approximation (Def. B.12, Thm B.14). It is not a theorem that the model is invariant, and it is never tested.
- My derivation, not stated in the paper: because the natural cubic interpolant is unique, inserting a knot whose value lies on the spline leaves the spline unchanged (scipy check: max diff 7.8e-15). So the continuous-time NCDE is exactly invariant to refinements that preserve the spline.
- Inserting virtual knots on the piecewise-linear interpolant (N2's protocol) does change the natural cubic spline unless the points are collinear (my check: max diff 0.21). NCDE as published is therefore not invariant to N2's refinement protocol even in exact arithmetic, apart from the collinear example the paper itself gives.
- N2 must define refinement relative to its reconstruction and cite Remark B.13 for the principle.

4. grid_changes_tested. Speech Commands is regular and fully observed (Sec. 4.3), not partially observed. The actual settings are:
- CharacterTrajectories: 30/50/70% random drop, removed across channels, so irregular but fully observed.
- PhysioNet 2019: natively irregular and partially observed (10.3% of values observed), run with and without observational intensity.
There is no knot-refinement, downsampling, upsampling or resolution-change test.

5. reported_numbers. Speech Commands here is 10-class, not 35-class: 34,975 series of ten words, 20 MFCC (Hann window 200, hop 100, 128 mel filterbanks), length 161, 70/15/15 split. Results, mean over 5 runs:

| Task | NCDE | ODE-RNN | GRU-D | GRU-Δt | GRU-ODE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Speech Commands, test accuracy | 89.8±2.5% | 65.9±35.6% | 32.4±34.8% | 43.3±33.9% | 47.9±2.9% |
| CharacterTrajectories 30% drop | 98.7±0.8% | 95.4% | 94.2% | 93.6% | 92.6% |
| CharacterTrajectories 50% drop | 98.8±0.2% | 96.0% | 90.2% | 91.3% | 86.7% |
| CharacterTrajectories 70% drop | 98.6±0.4% | 95.3% | 91.9% | 90.4% | 89.9% |

- PhysioNet AUC for NCDE: 0.880±0.006 with observational intensity, 0.776±0.009 without.
- This paper reports no HAR, EigenWorms or PDM numbers, and no sampling-rate-change results. Its SC-10 MFCC task is not comparable to the 35-class raw-audio Speech Commands used by S4/S5.

6. input_reconstruction.
- Linear interpolation is not discussed in this paper.
- App. A requires X to be continuous and piecewise differentiable, needs twice differentiability for gradients with respect to t0 under the adjoint, and discusses quadratic splines (A.2) and GP/kernel/curve-fitting alternatives (A.3).

7. Rating changes, all leaning toward the hostile reading:
- exact_input_integration: none -> partial. The state is a Riemann–Stieltjes integral against the reconstructed path (eq. 2-3), not a per-sample update. There is no closed-form linear stem, and dX/dt is only sampled at RK4 stage points.
- fixed_time_nonlinearity: partial -> substantial, for the reasons in item 2 (evidence: Fig. 1, Sec. 3.4, Sec. 6.3, App. D.1).
- refinement_invariance_claim: partial -> substantial. The principle is stated explicitly, but not for the discretised model, not for piecewise-linear refinement, and never tested.
- knot_vs_measurement_distinction: stays partial. Sec. 3.5/3.6 intensity channels are the explicit mechanism: the index i increments at every knot, which deliberately breaks equality. There is no separation of refinement, downsampling and missing data.
- overall: partial -> substantial.

8. What N2 can still claim over NCDE:
- a closed-form exact FOH linear stem with no solver error, whose input between clock ticks is integrated exactly rather than point-sampled through dX/dt;
- a clock independent of sampling, with a theorem and float64 tests showing exact invariance of the discretised representation;
- a protocol that separates refinement, downsampling and missing data.

NCDE run with a fixed, data-independent step (and linear interpolation) should be included as a close-work baseline.

1) fixed_time_nonlinearity should go up from partial to substantial. The method places no constraint tying the intervals r_i to observations (Sec.1.3). Sec.1.2 says outright that network evaluations are decoupled from observations. In code, f_theta runs only at the stage points of a constant-step Heun solver (diffrax ConstantStepSize, dt0). The per-window vector field is autonomous and uses only the window's log-signature (models/LogNeuralCDEs.py: searchsorted(intervals, t)). A hostile reviewer would argue: pick r_i = i*Delta and a fixed dt0, and you have N2's structure. That is an exact path summary per fixed physical-time window plus nonlinear updates on a fixed clock. Signature-type summaries of a piecewise-linear path do not change when collinear points are inserted, so refinement invariance follows from standard rough-path facts. The paper never says so and never uses such a clock. In practice both the clock and the windows are set by observation counts: EigenWorms uses Log-ODE step = 12 observations and dt0 = 6.67e-4 ≈ 1/(1+17984/12), i.e. dt0 is a function of n. So inserting virtual knots would move the windows and the solver grid. This is the concrete gap N2 can claim.

2) refinement_invariance_claim should go up from none to partial. There is no exact invariance statement and no test. Used together with Sec. 4.1, which says step-size (residual) rescaling (STN) 'converges to the incorrect response therefore represents a different system to the original', a reviewer can argue that this paper already shows two things: dt/step-size rescaling fails for per-sample nonlinear recurrences, and tying the nonlinear recurrence to a fixed physical-time lag restores rate independence (near machine precision for integer oversampling, Sec. 5.3).
verifications.corrections:
1. ACCESS: change from ABSTRACT_ONLY to FULL_TEXT_SECTIONS covering all sections (Abstract; 1; 2; 3.1-3.5; 4, 4.1-4.2; 5.1-5.3; 6). The arXiv HTML is available.

2. MECHANISM: the record is incomplete. The paper compares four inference-time modifications of a pretrained per-sample RNN h^n = f(h^{n-1}, x^n) (Eq. 1a):
- naive: run the model unchanged at the new rate.
- STN: residual/step-size rescaling by 1/M, which is forward Euler on dh/dt = F_s r(h, x) (Eqs. 2-4). This is the direct analogue of dt-rescaling.
- delay-line methods: they reinterpret the RNN as h(t) = f(h(t-T), x(t)) with a fixed physical delay T (Eq. 5). The update becomes h~^n = f(h~^{n-M}, x~^n) (Eq. 7). For non-integer M the fractional delay is estimated by linear interpolation (LIDL, Eq. 8, from Chowdhury 2022), an all-pass filter (APDL, Eqs. 9-11) or cubic Lagrange interpolation (CIDL, Eqs. 12-14).
Evaluation uses 18 pretrained LSTM models from GuitarML; the cost benchmark uses GRUs with hidden sizes 24-72 in RTNeural C++. Nothing is retrained.

3. INPUT_RECONSTRUCTION: the record is wrong. Lagrange/all-pass/linear interpolation is applied to the HIDDEN-STATE delay line, not to the input. The input is bandlimited-resampled to the target rate with the FFT-based method of Valimaki and Bilbao [22] (Sec. 5.1). This is effectively ideal periodic sinc interpolation; Sec. 4.1 assumes x is bandlimited to the original Nyquist. There is no piecewise-linear/first-order-hold reconstruction and no closed-form input integration, so exact_input_integration stays at none.

4. WHERE_NONLINEARITY_EVALUATED: correct that f (tanh/sigmoid gates) is evaluated at every sample of the new rate, so the number of nonlinear evaluations grows with M. Add that in the delay methods each evaluation's recurrent lag is a fixed physical time T. For integer M the model splits into M interleaved copies of the original RNN, each on one phase of the upsampled input. The chain aligned with the original instants reproduces the base-rate model exactly, because the FFT upsampler preserves the original samples.

5. TIME_HANDLING: add that STN is step-size rescaling (1/M on the residual, Eq. 4). The delay methods fix the recurrent delay in seconds (Eqs. 5-7). Time is not an input channel. There is no fixed clock that is independent of the input grid.

6. fixed_time_nonlinearity: raise from none to partial. Eqs. 5-7 and the Sec. 3.2 sentence explicitly tie the nonlinear recurrence to a fixed physical-time lag. This is not N2's structure: N2 evaluates nonlinearities only at tau_j = j*Delta_c, independent of where the observations are, with a separate linear stem. A hostile reviewer would still cite it as prior art for 'nonlinear update anchored to physical time rather than per sample'.

7. refinement_invariance_claim: keep partial, but record the strong integer-case evidence. Sec. 4.1 (linear one-pole analysis) says delay methods give a frequency response 'identical to the original', apart from spectral mirroring above the original Nyquist. Sec. 5.3 reports SNRH of about 100 dB, 'near machine precision (operating at single-precision)', for integer ratios on a nonlinear LSTM. Non-integer ratios are only approximate because of interpolation error. The headline claim remains 'approximately sample rate independent'. The tested setting is upsampling a bandlimited signal: the same underlying signal on a finer grid, which is conceptually close to N2's lossless refinement but uses sinc rather than piecewise-linear reconstruction. It is not arbitrary non-uniform knot insertion, and there is no exact-invariance theorem for the nonlinear model.

8. knot_vs_measurement_distinction: raise from none to partial. The paper treats oversampling of a signal bandlimited to the original Nyquist, so no new information is added (Sec. 4.1). It evaluates only within the original Nyquist band (Sec. 2), treats aliasing separately (Sec. 5.3, SNRA), and explicitly defers downsampling (Sec. 2). The follow-up 2409.15884 covers undersampling (abstract only). Missing or irregular observations are never considered, and there is no explicit 'virtual knot vs real measurement' concept.

9. GRID_CHANGES_TESTED: 44.1 kHz base upsampled to 48 kHz (M=1.0884), 88.2 kHz and 96 kHz (Fig. 7). The text says '88.1 kHz'; I take that to be a typo for 88.2. Fig. 9 also shows M=2 and M=4. Inputs were one minute of guitar/bass and sine tones from 27.5 to 4186 Hz. There is no downsampling, random drop or irregular sampling.

10. REPORTED_NUMBERS: none on HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM. The only numbers are audio:
- at M=2, delay methods beat STN by 18 dB (MesaMiniRec) to 50 dB (DumbleLowG) SNR;
- SNRH is about 100 dB at integer ratios;
- APDL fails catastrophically (about 0 dB SNRH) on some models at 48 kHz;
- real-time-factor overhead versus naive is -0.56% (delay), -0.57% (STN), -2.13% (LIDL), -3.24% (APDL), -3.17% (CIDL), on an M1 MacBook Pro.

11. CODE: https://github.com/a-carson/dafx24_sr_indie_rnn (linked from https://a-carson.github.io/dafx24_sr_indie_rnn/). License not verified.

12. NOTES for N2:
- Section 1 frames resampling to the model's training rate as the standard alternative the paper wants to avoid. This supports making fixed-grid resampling a mandatory baseline, and it weakens any novelty claim for 'run the nonlinear net on a fixed clock', which is close to resampling to a fixed rate.

- The follow-up claim 'instability artefacts explained by linearized stability analysis' is confirmed by the 2409.15884 abstract: 'We analyse these failure cases through linearised stability analysis, showing that they result from instability around a fixed point.'
- The mechanism N2 can still claim as distinct: an exact closed-form linear stem over the FOH reconstruction, giving exact state invariance under arbitrary (non-uniform, non-integer) virtual knot insertion, plus nonlinearities only on an input-independent clock, kept separate from downsampling and missing data. None of these appear here.

verifications.strongest_non_novelty_sentence: "The bounds of these integrals are a fixed set of time points, meaning that the sequence length of the multi-view attention mechanism is fixed and independent of the sequence length of input samples." (Sec.3.1, arXiv 2405.20799v3). The integrals here are exact signatures of the piecewise-linear interpolant, computed with Chen's relation (App. A.1). The only nonlinear stage, the Transformer and final MLP, sees only these fixed-time tokens. A reviewer can pair this with Sec.3, "the local component as a type of convolutional filter that is invariant to the sampling rate of the signal". Together these state N2's two-component structure plus a sampling-rate invariance claim.
verifications.corrections:
RATING CHANGES
- fixed_time_nonlinearity: substantial -> full. As written in the paper, the only nonlinear processing (attention, eqs. 9-10, plus the final MLP) runs on M(X)_k at a "fixed set of time points" (Sec.3.1). The preliminary version says explicitly "Fixing a set of times T={t_1..t_L̄}".
  - What remains different (weak, implementation-level): the code grid is linspace(0, x.max(), L̄+1). It is a fixed count over [0,T], not a fixed spacing Δ_c, so it moves if the last observation is dropped. The code also snaps each grid time to an observation index instead of querying at the clock time.
- refinement_invariance_claim: partial -> substantial. The paper does not just say "robust". It explicitly claims "invariant to the sampling rate" (Sec.3 local component; App. B (ii); App. B Efficient Attention). Prop. 3.1 is only approximate (≈), and there is no exact knot-refinement theorem or test.
  - A hostile reviewer will note that eq. 8, as written, is exactly invariant to virtual knots. My test: midpoint knots inserted on a random 3-channel path (L=200, 10 windows, level 2, time channel added), with eq. 8 evaluated at exact clock times, gave a relative difference of 1.9e-15. So N2's exact-invariance result is a direct corollary for RFormer eq. 8. It is not new for "exact PL integration + fixed-clock nonlinearity" in general.
- knot_vs_measurement_distinction: none -> partial. The NeurIPS v3 text has none. However, the cited preliminary version (2403.10288, footnote 1) attributes the performance drop under 50% random drop to aliasing below the Nyquist rate. That is the lossy-measurement half of N2's distinction. Virtual knots are never discussed.
- exact_input_integration: kept at substantial. Exact closed-form integration of the PL path is present (signature via Chen's relation). The learnable diagonal LTI SSM with FOH closed form and exponential memory is not; the signature is a fixed truncated feature map. A reviewer could argue "full" by calling the signature the canonical exactly integrable linear CDE.
- overall: kept at substantial.

CODE FINDINGS (repo commit 27d59ea; these support N2's query-rule differentiation)
- The UEA _compute_global_sigs reads the streamed signature at np.where(x < step*i)[0][-1]. That is the last observation strictly before each boundary, not the boundary time.
- _compute_local_sigs slices data[idx_i:idx_{i+1}]. This drops the linear piece that crosses each boundary, and indices[-1] -= 1 drops the end as well.
- `end = min(int(max(x)), ...)` mixes time units and index units. With added knots it crashes (iisignature RuntimeError "Path has no length").
- Midpoint-knot test on the repo functions, as relative differences:

| Function | Relative difference |
|---|---|
| UEA global | 1.36e-2 |
| UEA local, with the clip removed | 2.37e-1 |
| EEG Signature_overlapping_irreg | 1.19e-2 |
| EEG Signature_nonoverlapping_irreg | 1.20e-1 |

- So the implementation is not refinement-invariant, even though eq. 8 is.

PROTOCOL DETAILS
- Random drop: the Table 5 caption says "per epoch". In the UEA code, however, keep_indices are sampled once per seed and shared by train, val and test. The UEA results therefore reflect a fixed missingness mask, not a zero-shot rate change.
- The EEG code resamples 100 indices per batch. It also has an unreported --zero_shot_downsample flag.
- No experiment separates virtual knots from real downsampling from missing data. No upsampling or knot-refinement test exists.
- EigenWorms configuration (Table 6): 10 windows, local signature only [L], level 2, multivariate, 2 layers, 1 head, embedding dim 20.

ADDITIONAL CALIBRATION NUMBERS
- F.2 Table 14 is a direct resampling+Transformer baseline:

| Setting | Linear-Interpolation + vanilla Transformer | RFormer |
|---|---|---|
| EigenWorms (accuracy) | 64.10% | 90.24% (level 2) |
| HR (RMSE) | 10.56 | 2.66 (level 4) |

- G.1 Table 15, EigenWorms, RFormer: full data 90.24±2.15 (Table 2 reports 90.3±0.1 for the same setting, an inconsistency in the paper); 30% drop 87.86±3.28; 50% 87.69±4.97; 70% 83.35±2.86; 85% 82.74±2.13. The Transformer runs out of memory at every rate except 85%, where it scores 72.45±3.36.
- HR, RFormer (Table 16): 2.66 / 2.72 / 2.82 / 2.98 for 0 / 30 / 50 / 70% drop.
- TIDES (App., EigenWorms, trained at 50% drop): RFormer mean 0.720 across test drop rates, falling to 0.562 at r_test=0.9.
- No HAR, Speech Commands or PDM numbers appear in this paper.

WHAT N2 CAN STILL LEGITIMATELY CLAIM
- A learnable exponential-memory SSM stem with an FOH closed form, instead of truncated signatures.
- An SSM backbone.
- An explicit exact theorem, together with a minimal counterexample for per-observation nonlinear models.
- A query rule that evaluates at clock times inside intervals rather than at observations.
- The three-way separation of virtual knots, real downsampling and missing observations.

WHAT N2 MUST NOT CLAIM
- That "interpolate + exact path integration + nonlinearity only on a fixed time grid" is new.
- That sampling-rate invariance from this structure is new.
- N2 must cite RFormer and its preliminary version 2403.10288 as the structural precedent.
- RFormer should be included as a near-neighbour baseline on EigenWorms.

verifications.access_self: FULL_TEXT_SECTIONS. I read the arXiv HTML of v2 (arXiv:2409.15884v2 [eess.AS], 30 Jan 2025, CC BY 4.0) in full: Abstract; I Introduction; II Problem Statement (Eqs. 1a, 1b, 2); III Sample rate independent RNNs (Eqs. 3, 4); III-A Lagrange interpolation (Eq. 5); III-B Minimax design; IV Experiment details; V Results; VI Linearised analysis (Eqs. 6-9); VI-A Experiment; VI-B Case study; Table I; VII Conclusions. I also opened the project page (https://a-carson.github.io/icassp25_srirnns/), which says "ICASSP '25 submission". I read only the README of the code repository (https://github.com/a-carson/icassp25_srirnns, JAX). No LICENSE file was found at the repository root on main or master, so the code license is unknown. Figures are images and I did not inspect them beyond their captions.
verifications.quotes_verified:
Both quotes in the record are real, verbatim, and correctly attributed to the Abstract.
(Q1) "RNNs have a fixed sample rate encoded in their model weights, making the sample rate non-adjustable during inference." Verbatim, Abstract.
(Q2) "in some cases the sample rate adjustment leads to unwanted artefacts in the output signal. We analyse these failure cases through linearised stability analysis". This is a verbatim substring of the Abstract; the original is preceded by "however," and continues ", showing that they result from instability around a fixed point."
Additional verified quotes from the full text:
(Q3, Sec. III, before Eq. 3) "Adjusting the inference sample rate of an RNN can be achieved by maintaining the same delay duration (in seconds) seen by the RNN during training [13, 14]."
(Q4, Sec. III, Eq. 4) "For non-integer conversion ratios, the state at non-integer time step n-1-Delta can be approximated with a fractional delay FIR filter". Eq. 4 is h'_{n-1-Delta} ≈ sum_k l_k h'_{n-1-k}, and Eq. 3 uses Delta = F'_s/F_s - 1.
(Q5, Sec. II) "In this work we consider f to be a LSTM cell, and g an affine transformation (which is by definition sample rate independent)."
(Q6, Sec. I) "One possibility is to resample the input signal to the desired rate, and then back to its original rate after processing. For real-time applications, however, this may add excessive CPU expense and/or latency."
(Q7, Sec. I) "a detailed investigation into this is left to future work." This refers to the resampling alternative.
(Q8, Sec. V) "We can conclude that there is no single filter for undersampling that will give reasonable results across all models."
(Q9, Sec. VII) "this analysis may enable sample rate independence by adjusting the weights of the network, thus avoiding the need for interpolation or extrapolation entirely."
verifications.strongest_non_novelty_sentence:
"One possibility is to resample the input signal to the desired rate, and then back to its original rate after processing." (Sec. I).

A hostile reviewer would use this to say that running a nonlinear model on its native fixed clock through resampling is an obvious, known option. The paper never implements it and leaves it to future work, and it is exactly N2's mandatory fixed-grid resampling baseline, not N2's exact-integration stem.

The runner-up sentence, for the claim that physical-time step rescaling of per-sample nonlinear recurrences is already known and already known to be approximate, is Sec. III: "Adjusting the inference sample rate of an RNN can be achieved by maintaining the same delay duration (in seconds) seen by the RNN during training [13, 14]."
verifications.corrections:
1) ACCESS. The record says ABSTRACT_ONLY. The full text is open on arXiv HTML, so this should be FULL_TEXT_SECTIONS (all sections, listed above). Venue: arXiv 2409.15884, eess.AS; v2 dated 30 Jan 2025. The project page and README say "ICASSP '25 submission". I did not verify acceptance.

2) INPUT_RECONSTRUCTION is wrong. The record says "FIR fractional-delay/extrapolation filters", but those filters act on past HIDDEN STATES in the feedback loop (Eq. 4: h'_{n-1-Delta} ≈ sum_k l_k h'_{n-1-k}), not on the input. The input is not reconstructed at all: the LSTM takes the samples x'_n at the new rate directly (Eq. 3). The text does not say how x' was produced. A DFT-based sample rate conversion [20] appears only in building the evaluation target, which is y_n resampled to F'_s (Sec. II, Eq. 2).

3) MECHANISM, stated more precisely. The feedback delay is set to Delta = F'_s/F_s - 1 samples so that its duration in seconds stays fixed (Eq. 3). Non-integer delays use Lagrange interpolation (Eq. 5; K = 1..5; extrapolation, i.e. a fractional signal advance, when Delta < 0) or a minimax FIR filter with unity DC gain over a 0 to 0.25 F_s band. Baselines are the naive method (no interpolation) and the state-trajectory network (STN) [28, 14]. Linearised fixed-point pole analysis (Eqs. 6-9) predicts which filters fail.

4) WHERE_NONLINEARITY_EVALUATED. Confirmed: at every sample of the new rate (LSTM cell f, hidden size 40, H = 80 states). The output map g is affine.

5) TIME_HANDLING. This is only a global uniform rate change: the delay duration in seconds is preserved, which is the recurrent analogue of dt rescaling. There is no irregular or per-sample dt and no time channel.

6) INVARIANCE_CLAIM. There is no formal or exact invariance claim. The stated objective is to maximise SNR against a DFT-resampled target (Eq. 2), and the result is empirical, approximate, and model-dependent. Some filters do worse than the naive method, and Sec. V says no single undersampling filter works for all models.

7) GRID_CHANGES_TESTED. Only two uniform non-integer rate conversions of bandlimited audio were tested:
- 44.1 to 48 kHz (ratio 160/147, "oversampling")
- 44.1 to 40.5 kHz (ratio 147/160, "undersampling")

There is no knot refinement of the same reconstructed path, no random drop, no missing observations and no irregular sampling.

8) OVERLAP RATINGS:
- fixed_time_nonlinearity: raised from none to partial, taking the hostile-reviewer default. Sec. I names resample, process at the native rate, resample back as the obvious alternative and rejects it for CPU cost and latency. This is mention only, and it corresponds to N2's resampling baseline, not to an exact-integration stem. The proposed method itself does the opposite, with per-sample nonlinearity at the new rate.
- exact_input_integration = none: confirmed. There is no linear input stem and no closed-form integration.
- refinement_invariance_claim = partial: kept. Sample-rate independence of per-sample nonlinear recurrences is the stated goal, but only as an empirical approximation for uniform rate changes. Nothing is claimed about lossless refinement of the same path.
- knot_vs_measurement_distinction = none: confirmed. Over- and undersampling are separated, but both treat the signal as bandlimited with a DFT-resampled target. There is no notion of virtual knots versus real measurements, and no aliasing or missing-data separation.
- overall = partial: confirmed.

9) REPORTED_NUMBERS. None are on HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM, so nothing here calibrates N2's tasks. What the paper reports (160 GuitarML Tone Library LSTM models, F_s = 44.1 kHz, 60 s guitar/bass DI test signal, first 44100 samples discarded):
- 48 kHz: Lagrange-5 is best in 58.1% of models, reaching 80 dB SNR, but is worse than naive in 8.1%, going as low as -5 dB. Lagrange-3 ranges from 19 to 73 dB.
- 40.5 kHz: the minimum SNR is below 0 dB for every method, and naive is best in 3.1% of models. The conclusion reports up to 73 dB when undersampling.
- The linearised stability analysis predicts success or failure in 97.8% of cases ((2868+261)/3200, Table I).

10) CODE. https://github.com/a-carson/icassp25_srirnns (JAX; license unknown, no LICENSE file found). Audio examples are at https://a-carson.github.io/icassp25_srirnns/.

11) NOTES. The paper supports N2's premise that per-sample nonlinear recurrences are grid-dependent even when the delay duration in physical time is preserved, so the nonlinearity makes this style of rate adaptation approximate. Three works it cites should get their own records and be checked, because they may be closer to N2:
- [14] Carson, Wright, Chowdhury, Välimäki, Bilbao, "Sample rate independent recurrent neural networks for audio effects processing", DAFx24
- [13] Chowdhury 2022 blog, "Sample-rate agnostic recurrent neural networks"
- [15] Saito et al., "Sampling-frequency-independent convolutional layer", IEEE/ACM TASLP 2022. It uses continuous-time kernels sampled at the operating rate, which is closer to N2's exact linear input stem.
