verifications.quotes_verified:
The one quote in the record is real, verbatim and correctly placed: "In this paper, we propose a convolution layer capable of handling arbitrary sampling frequencies by a single DNN." (Abstract). It is not evidence for any mechanism, though. The record left out the load-bearing passages. Verified extra quotes, all verbatim:
(a) Sec III-A, Eq. (2): "The impulse invariant method generates a discrete-time impulse response h[l] from an analog filter g(t) so that the sampled instants coincide: h[l]=Tg(lT)."
(b) Sec III-C: "Hence, as the sampling frequency doubles, L and W should double to make the representation consistent for the masking module."
(c) Sec III-C: "we determine L and W for each target sampling frequency to keep the frame length and shift unchanged in the continuous time domain."
(d) Sec IV-A: "we determined L and W to be 5.0 and 2.5 ms at the sampling frequency of 16 kHz"
(e) Sec III-C: "The masking modules are the same as in [3]."
(f) Sec III-C: "By replacing all convolution layers in the masking modules with the SFI convolution layers, this issue might be resolved. However, we left it as a future work"
(g) Sec II-A: the encoder is "a one-dimensional (1D) convolution layer (with kernel size L and stride W) and the rectified linear unit (ReLU)."
(h) Sec III-B: "Since the impulse invariant method simply performs sampling to an analog filter, aliasing occurs in the obtained digital filters."
(i) Sec IV-A: "we created the test data by down- and up-sampling the test tracks to several target sampling frequencies, F_s=8,12,...,48 kHz."
(j) Sec IV-A: "We applied all models to the audio signals of the unseen sampling frequencies without resampling them at the trained sampling frequency"
(k) Sec V: "Since the analog filters do not depend on sampling frequency, the proposed layers can generate consistent weights for arbitrary sampling frequencies."
verifications.strongest_non_novelty_sentence: "For this reason, we determine L and W for each target sampling frequency to keep the frame length and shift unchanged in the continuous time domain." (Sec. III-C). It follows directly from "as the sampling frequency doubles, L and W should double to make the representation consistent for the masking module." A reviewer could read this as N2's recipe already in place: a continuous-time linear front end, rebuilt for each sampling rate, plus all downstream nonlinear processing on a fixed physical-time frame clock (2.5 ms shift). The net result is a representation that does not depend on the sampling rate.
verifications.corrections:
1. ACCESS: change from ABSTRACT_ONLY to FULL_TEXT_SECTIONS (all sections listed above).

2. WHERE_NONLINEARITY_EVALUATED is wrong. It is not "at every sample". The SFI encoder is a strided convolution followed by ReLU, so ReLU fires once per frame. Frame length is L = 5.0 ms and frame shift is W = 2.5 ms, both fixed in continuous time (quotes c, d, g). The ordinary non-SFI masking modules (dilated TCN blocks, group norm, mask multiplication) run on that frame sequence, which has a fixed physical rate of 400 frames/s. The SFI transposed-conv decoder, which is linear, maps back to the sample grid.
- For every tested rate (8, 12, ..., 48 kHz) W is a whole number of samples, so frame n sits exactly at t = n x 2.5 ms whatever the sampling rate.
- The authors say they chose this instead of making the masking modules SFI (quote f).
- Follow-up arXiv 2306.10718 (abstract only) adds windowed-sinc feature interpolation "to sample instants with the desired stride" when W is fractional (e.g. 44.1 kHz). That confirms the design intent is a physical-time frame clock.
- fixed_time_nonlinearity should be SUBSTANTIAL, not none. It is not full because the clock ticks only land on sample positions for uniform grids with integer strides, and the paper never frames it as a clock independent of irregular observation times.

3. INPUT_RECONSTRUCTION: none. The discrete samples are used directly. Impulse invariance samples the analog filter kernel, h[l] = T g(lT) (Eq. 2), which makes the layer a Riemann-sum approximation of continuous convolution with a length-L FIR truncation. Kernel aliasing is admitted in Sec III-B. It is not exact, and inserting virtual knots on a linear interpolant would change the output. Keep exact_input_integration at PARTIAL: the idea of a continuous-time linear layer rebuilt per sampling rate is there, but without exactness.

4. INVARIANCE_CLAIM: the paper names the goal "SFI" (sampling-frequency independent). The evidence is purely empirical (similar SDR at 12-48 kHz, Fig. 2), and the only formal argument is consistency of the generated weights (quote k). There is no exactness claim and no theorem. Keep refinement_invariance_claim at PARTIAL.

5. GRID_CHANGES_TESTED: training at 16 kHz only. Test sets are uniform rates of 8, 12, ..., 48 kHz, made by down- and up-sampling the 44.1 kHz MUSDB18-HQ test tracks (quote i).
- Test signals above 16 kHz contain real extra bandwidth up to about 22 kHz, so they are real measurement changes, not lossless refinement of the same path. Only 48 kHz is band-limited (sinc) upsampling, not first-order hold.
- No irregular sampling, missing observations or same-path knot refinement is tested.
- The EUSIPCO version has no resampling baseline (quote j). Per the repo README, the TASLP 2022 extension adds one and reports SFI beating signal resampling only when the input rate is far below the trained rate.

6. KNOT_VS_MEASUREMENT: raise from none to PARTIAL, taking the hostile reading.
- Sec III-B handles aliasing at low sampling rates with a separate technique: zeroing channels whose centre frequency is above Nyquist.
- Sec IV-B links consistency at high rates to the information content of the signal ("dominant frequency components ... below 8 kHz").
- There is still no concept of virtual knots versus real measurements, and nothing on missing observations.

7. OVERALL: raise from partial to SUBSTANTIAL. The record's note ("audio analogue of dt-rescaling") understates the overlap: it covers only the SFI conv layer and misses the fixed-physical-time frame clock for all nonlinear processing, which is the half of N2's structure most exposed to a novelty challenge.
- What N2 still adds beyond this paper: exact closed-form integration of a continuous-time diagonal SSM over a first-order-hold reconstruction, where the paper uses approximate impulse-invariant FIR on uniform samples; exact (provable) invariance to lossless knot insertion on irregular grids, where the paper's result is empirical and for uniform rates only; explicit separation of refinement, downsampling and missing observations; and an SSM backbone.
- N2 should cite this paper, the TASLP 2022 extension and 2306.10718 as prior work for "continuous-time linear front end plus fixed physical-rate downstream network".

8. REPORTED_NUMBERS: none for HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM. SDR results appear only in Fig. 2 (MUSDB18-HQ, trained at 16 kHz, tested at 8-48 kHz) and are not tabulated in the text.

9. CODE: github.com/TomohikoNakamura/sfi_convtasnet, MIT License, official code for the TASLP 2022 extended version; pretrained model at huggingface.co/tnkmr/sfi_convtasnet_fd_mgf_musdb18hq. The EUSIPCO text itself gives no code URL.

10. RELATED FOLLOW-UPS that should get their own records: arXiv 2306.10718 (non-integer strides via sinc interpolation of features, i.e. an explicit physical-time frame clock), arXiv 2309.12581 (SFI universal sound separation), arXiv 2206.02124 (SFI dialogue separation), arXiv 2601.14684 (degradation under sampling-frequency mismatch). I have not read the full text of any of them.

Mechanism evidence that I checked myself in the paper:
- Eq. 11 (Sect. 3.1): "Output = Skip(uk) + LeakyReLU(yk)".
- Sect. 2.2: "By adjusting Ts, the discrete SSM-Layers can operate at different effective sampling rates."
- Sect. 1: "we infer deeper layers with lower sampling rates (similar to a stride in the time domain)."
- Sect. 3.2: "When downsampling somewhere the sampling rate of all following layers has to be updated (see Fig. 2)."

Code evidence:
- sequence_layer.py forward: x = x[:, ::int(step_scale/previous_step_scale), :]. This is naive decimation before the SSM. Norm, ReLU/LeakyReLU and skip are then applied at every sample of the decimated grid.
- ssm.py: step = self.step_scale * torch.exp(self.log_step), fed into discretize_zoh, where Lambda_bar = exp(Lambda*Delta) and B_bar = (Lambda_bar-1)/Lambda * B.
- test_sc_add_params_macs_to_test.py: the 8k and 4k accuracies are the runs with step_scale == [2]*length and [4]*length. So "8 kHz" means naive x[::2] decimation of the 16 kHz input plus a Ts x2 update in every layer, not anti-aliased resampling; the torchaudio Resample call is commented out.

However, there is significant accuracy degradation, suggesting that either the networks behave differently at lower frequencies or that relevant information is lost by removing higher frequencies." A reviewer would say this already states N2's core question: is the drop from a sampling-rate change caused by the model depending on the grid, or by lost information? Runner-up, against the fixed-clock mechanism, Sect. 1: "Specifically, we infer deeper layers with lower sampling rates (similar to a stride in the time domain)." Together with Sect. 3.2 ("the sampling rate of all following layers has to be updated"), this shows that running nonlinear layers on a coarser clock with physical Ts was already done.
verifications.corrections:
1. ACCESS. The record's "ABSTRACT_ONLY / Springer paywall" is wrong. The paper is open access and I read the full text (list in access_self). Venue: Mach Learn 114(8):175, published online 19 June 2025, presented at ECML-PKDD'25. No arXiv version was found.

2. INPUT RECONSTRUCTION (confirmed, now with sources). S5-style exact ZOH discretization: Eq. 3, Ad = exp(A Ts), Bd = A^-1(Ad - I)B. The diagonal complex form is Eq. 6 / 14, with the time step equal to learnable Delta times a global Ts. The input bias is folded in as an extra constant input with its own ZOH term (Eqs. 7, 9). The input is held piecewise-constant on whatever grid it arrives on. There is no first-order-hold or spline reconstruction and no integration over a reconstructed path independent of that grid. Exactness for ZOH is standard prior art, which N2 already concedes. Rating: partial.

3. WHERE THE NONLINEARITY RUNS (sharpened). Every layer applies (batch/layer) norm, the SSM, pointwise LeakyReLU/ReLU and the skip at every sample of its own grid (Eq. 11; sequence_layer.py). That grid is the previous grid naively decimated by an integer factor, x[:, ::k]:
   - The layer clocks are strides of the observation index grid, anchored at index 0. They are not a clock independent of observation times.
   - Layer 1's nonlinearity always runs once per input sample.
   - Decimation is applied to post-nonlinearity feature maps, with no anti-aliasing filter.
   - Deeper layers can run at physically defined coarse rates (for example [1,1,1,2,2,38], so layer 6 runs at 421.05 Hz). A hostile reviewer could therefore argue "substantial" for the idea of a coarse internal clock. But the clock is not held fixed when the input rate changes: the Table 2 runs at 8 and 4 kHz run every layer at the input rate. If virtual knots were inserted, layer 1 would evaluate LeakyReLU at each knot.
   Rating: partial.

4. INVARIANCE CLAIM (tightened). The only claim is generic rate flexibility inherited from S4/S5. From the Abstract: "Their definition in continuous time allows for discretization and operation of the network at different sampling rates." Sect. 1 attributes to Smith 2023 and Gu 2024 that the discretization rules "theoretically allow ... inference on input data with different sampling rates without the need for retraining". The paper claims no exact invariance and itself documents that the model is not invariant: accuracy drops at 8 and 4 kHz. Its discretization-error metric e_{L,Tn} (Eq. A5) covers only the linear part and explicitly treats LeakyReLU as identity (A.3). So the effect of the nonlinearities on grid dependence is expressly left unanalyzed, which supports N2's niche. One implicit point matters: RZOH (A.1) decimates, then ZOH-upsamples feature maps by repeating samples, "we do not need to modify any following layer". That is a ZOH knot refinement of a decimated path, used only as training augmentation, with no equivalence claim. I keep partial rather than none only because of the generic claim and the RZOH mechanism; "none" is also defensible.

5. KNOT VS MEASUREMENT DISTINCTION. Raised from "none" to "partial". Sect. 3.2 explicitly separates two causes of the accuracy drop: the network behaving differently at lower rates, versus information being lost. Sect. 4.4 separates system (discretization) aliasing from input aliasing ("We argue that we introduce input aliasing errors during training ... this regularization does not inherently reduce system discretization errors"). However, it never separates virtual knots from real measurements, never tests lossless refinement or upsampling of the same path, and never tests missing or irregular observations.

6. GRID CHANGES TESTED (corrected).
   - Downsampling only, by naive decimation. At the input: x2 and x4 (the "8 kHz" and "4 kHz" columns).
   - Internally, layer by layer: a brute-force search with factors up to 64 per layer, 6686 combinations per 6-layer model.
   - RZOH training augmentation: power-of-two decimation followed by sample repetition, with factor up to 128.
   - No upsampling or knot refinement, no dropped samples, no irregular sampling.

7. REPORTED NUMBERS. Setting: Speech Commands, 35 classes, raw audio, causal/autoregressive models trained at 16 kHz; 8 and 4 kHz are naive input decimation plus Ts update, no retraining.
   - Table 2, accuracy at 16k / 8k / 4k:
     - S5† (208k params, causal, trained in the S5 repo): 95.83 / 93.53 / –
     - S5-Leaky-ReLU† (151k): 95.41 / 90.60 / –
     - S4-LegS (306k): 93.60 at 16k only
     - S-Edge-Full (141k, RZOH): 95.19 / 93.38 / 81.11
     - S-Edge-naive-XL: 94.56 / 92.30 / 78.87
     - S-Edge-L: 94.26 / 89.65 / 61.34
     - S-Edge-S: 93.37 / 87.77 / 69.40
     - S-Edge-Tiny (8k params): 90.50 / 85.82 / 67.32
   - Table 3, internal downsampling, best accuracy with at least n-fold FLOP reduction, columns n = 1 / 2 / 4 / 5 / 8 / 16:
     - S-Edge-Full, RZOH: 95.22 / 95.17 / 94.38 / 93.66 / 90.31 / 74.94
     - S-Edge-Full, no RZOH: 94.92 / 93.39 / 85.14 / 82.64 / 65.63 / 23.58
     - S-Edge-S, RZOH: 93.18 / 93.18 / 93.09 / 93.03 / 91.58 / 69.86
     - At n=4, internal downsampling (94.38) far outperforms naive 4 kHz input decimation (81.11).
   - Costs:
     - Training: 4-13 GPU-hours per model on an A40; 431 model/hyperparameter configurations.
     - Table 4, MCU STM32L4R5 (Cortex-M4F): S-Edge-Full RZOH without downsampling, 95.19% at 103.53 s; S-Edge-Tiny RZOH with factors [1,9,54], 88.01% at 0.2891 s.
   - No results on HAR, EigenWorms or PDM.

8. IMPLICATIONS FOR N2.
   - S-Edge is the closest precedent for running nonlinear layers on a coarser physical clock, and it is a natural cost and accuracy baseline on Speech Commands 8 kHz.
   - N2 must credit it for layer-wise dt-rescaled downsampling and for posing the question "does the model behave differently at another rate, or is information lost?"
   - N2 must not claim to be first to run deep SSM layers at lower internal sampling rates.
   - What remains open after reading this paper:
     - exact integration over a first-order-hold path;
     - a clock decoupled from observation positions for all nonlinear updates;
     - exact invariance to lossless refinement, tested with virtual knots;
     - explicit separation of refinement, downsampling and missing observations.

critic.angle_summary:
What the sweep missed, and what I read to fill the gaps. I read 8 missing items in full text: 7 on arXiv, plus the DAFx25 PDF read directly from the proceedings. They cover three categories the digest skipped or underweighted.

(A) Speech SFI models that run all nonlinear layers on a fixed physical-time frame clock:
- USES (Zhang et al., ASRU 2023, 2309.17384) uses a fixed-duration STFT (window 32 ms, hop 16 ms). The frame count stays the same across sampling rates and only the number of frequency bins changes. A dual-path Transformer then runs on that fixed clock. It is trained at 8 kHz only and tested at 16 and 48 kHz: SI-SNRi 20.3 at 8 kHz and 19.8 at 16 kHz. By contrast, the "resampling" route (down to 8 kHz, process, back up) gives 12.0.
- USEMamba (Interspeech 2025, 2505.21198) puts a deep Mamba SSM on the same SFI-STFT clock.
- Together with Saito/Imamura SFI and Boulanger & Wood PDM (already in the digest), this settles one point. "Linear front end, then nonlinear SSM/Transformer on a clock fixed in physical time" is standard practice in audio, and ms-defined mel/STFT hops make it ubiquitous. N2 cannot claim the fixed clock.
- N2 can still defend one distinction, and should test it rather than assume it. An STFT of point samples is NOT invariant to virtual-knot refinement: denser samples of a piecewise-linear (PL) path carry kink harmonics into new frequency bins. N2's exact FOH stem is invariant.

(B) HAR and irregular time series with fixed physical-time windows:
- HALO (arXiv 2608.27233, Aug 2026) cuts IMU sessions into 1-second patches, pools them adaptively, and runs a Transformer on the patch clock. It claims to accept "any sampling rate". Its within-patch CNN is still nonlinear at every sample, its rate test is confounded with channel-description changes, and UCI-HAR is only a training set.
- t-PatchGNN (ICML 2024) uses fixed-time-span patches and runs a Transformer and GNN on the patch clock. Inside each patch it aggregates with a softmax over observations, so it depends on observation density.
- Hasegawa (IEEE Sensors J. 2021, 2101.00812) is the HAR instance of the mandatory baseline: linear interpolation to a fixed length, a CNN, plus adversarial training on the sampling rate. The key point for N2: the rate discriminator reaches 96.9% on interpolated inputs. Real downsampling followed by PL interpolation stays detectable, which is consistent with N2's point that refinement invariance does not extend to real downsampling. It also gives calibration numbers: HASC accuracy 85-87% down to 12.5 Hz, collapsing to 39-46% at 4 Hz.
- Phased LSTM (2016) gates nonlinear LSTM updates with a learned oscillation in physical time. It tests 10x oversampling (apparently trained per condition), asynchronous sampling, and zero-shot event-drop (N-MNIST ρ=0.4/1.0). Updates still happen at every observation that falls in an open phase.

(C) Alias-free nonlinearities for time series, via antiderivative anti-aliasing (ADAA):
- DAFx25 applies ADAA to RNNs; Pupu-Vocoder (2512.20211) applies it to vocoders and codecs.
- Both evaluate each activation in closed form as a rectangular-window average over the linear-interpolation (PL) reconstruction of its argument. Both still output on the sample grid, still need oversampling, and make no refinement-invariance claim.
- So "closed-form continuous-time treatment of the PL reconstruction" is already known on the nonlinearity side. N2 must not claim alias-free nonlinearities, and should present the stem's exactness only for the linear SSM integral.

Net effect on N2's novelty: the fixed-clock component is now covered by prior work in audio SFI (2021-2025), HAR (HALO), irregular time series (t-PatchGNN, HiSS) and signature models (RFormer, NRDE). The remaining defensible core is narrow and has three parts:
- an exact closed-form FOH integral by a learned diagonal SSM, read out at clock times not aligned with the observations;
- an exact theorem for virtual-knot refinement;
- a three-way protocol that separates knot refinement, real downsampling and missing observations.
That protocol must include SFI-STFT/mel frame-clock baselines, which also have a fixed clock but are not refinement-invariant. It must also include linear-interpolation resampling baselines, which are refinement-invariant.

Found but NOT read, so no claims are made about them:
- TF-Refiner 2609.29463 (Sep 2026, SFI speech enhancement across sampling rates)
- SFI neural audio codec 2607.01865 (IWAENC 2026, adjustable token rate)
- NCDSSM 2301.11308
- Khatri-Rao Neural Operators (ICML 2025)
- CaMBRAIN 2605.28792 (EEG SSM with 62.5 ms patches)
- WaveSSM 2602.22266
- Neural distortion anti-aliasing by fine-tuning, 2505.11375
- ReIMTS 2602.21498 (ICLR 2026)
- MambaRate 2507.12090
- the GP adapters Li & Marlin 2016 and MGP-RNN (Futoma 2017)

Calibration: the new items report no UCI-HAR test numbers, no EigenWorms and no PDM results.

papers.title: HALO: A Heterogeneity-Aware Language-Aligned IMU Foundation Model for Open-Set Human Activity Recognition
papers.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv 2608.27233 (v1, 27 Aug 2026; the paper's own note calls it a 'Preprint of work completed in March 2026')
papers.sections_read: Abstract, 1 Introduction, 2 Related Work, 3.1, 3.3, 5.1.1 (Adaptive-Pooling Tokenization), 5.1.2, 5.1.3, 6.1 (dataset table), 6.2 (Table 3 text), 6.3.2 with Table 7, 6.4 (patch size), 7 Conclusion
papers.mechanism: Each IMU session is split into patches of fixed physical duration (default 1.0 s; 0.75-1.25 s random augmentation during training) at the native sampling rate. Each patch and channel is z-normalised on its own. A tokenizer maps it to a 384-d token through two branches: a multi-scale 1-D CNN (kernel sizes 3/5/7 in samples) followed by adaptive average pooling, and a fixed-n FFT magnitude followed by an MLP. Tokens are conditioned on sensor text and fed to an 8-layer dual-branch Transformer that attends over patches and over channels, with sinusoidal PE over the patch index. Multi-query attention pooling follows, then contrastive alignment with SBERT label text.
papers.input_reconstruction: none: raw native samples go into the per-patch CNN and adaptive pooling. The paper does not describe interpolation or resampling at native rates. The 'fixed-n FFT' is not specified further; I did not see a padding/truncation rule.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated:
Two stages:
- Inside each patch: at every native sample, because CNN kernels are defined in samples, so the physical receptive field scales with 1/fs, and the per-patch z-normalisation is also nonlinear.
- After tokenization: every Transformer, FFN and attention nonlinearity runs on the fixed 1-s physical-time patch clock.
papers.time_handling: Fixed physical-time patching ('seconds rather than samples') and a positional encoding over the patch index. There is no dt and no timestamps inside the patch; within-patch length L varies with the sampling rate and is absorbed by adaptive pooling.
papers.invariance_claim: Empirical and qualitative only. The tokenizer 'natively accepts any sampling rate' and seconds-based patching 'decouples temporal resolution from patch semantics'. There is no exact or approximate invariance statement or proof, and the per-sample CNN makes tokens rate-dependent by construction.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Cross-dataset evaluation at native rates (20-100 Hz) versus the same test data resampled to 20 Hz. That comparison is confounded with a switch from rich to generic channel descriptions (Table 7). Also a patch-duration sweep. There is no knot refinement, controlled downsampling of one dataset, random drop or irregular timing.
evidence_quotes: Sec 5.1.1: "Rather than resampling, HALO segments sessions in seconds rather than samples, so every patch spans the same physical duration regardless of rate."

Sec 5.1.1 (Spectral-temporal tokenizer): "The temporal branch applies a multi-scale 1-D CNN (kernel sizes 3, 5, 7) followed by adaptive average pooling to produce a fixed-length output regardless of L"
Sec 3.1: "A fixed positional encoding tied to timestep index conflates physical time with sequence length, causing identical motions at different rates to appear structurally different."
Sec 5.1.1: "Because both branches use adaptive pooling, the tokenizer natively accepts any sampling rate without resampling or architectural changes"
papers.reported_numbers:
Table 7 reports average accuracy (%) over five test datasets:

| Setting | ZS-O | ZS-C | 1% | 10% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HALO, native Hz + rich descriptions | 42.0 | 53.1 | 76.5 | 85.7 |
| HALO, 20 Hz resampled + generic descriptions | 30.6 | 49.4 | 71.7 | 84.7 |
| Best baseline (MOMENT) | 28.3 | 44.7 | 73.8 | 81.3 |

UCI-HAR (50 Hz, 30 subjects, 6 activities, 9 channels) is one of the 10 TRAINING datasets, so there is no UCI-HAR test accuracy. The paper states a fixed 1.0 s patch is within 1.3 pp of the per-dataset optimum.
papers.code_url_and_license: Not released. The paper says 'The source code and pretrained models for HALO will be released upon publication.'
papers.notes: Most relevant 2026 HAR near-work. A hostile reviewer could cite it as 'nonlinear layers on a fixed physical-time clock for multi-rate HAR already exists'. Rebuttal: the stem is a per-sample nonlinear CNN whose kernels are defined in samples, not an exact linear integral. Tokens therefore change under both knot refinement and real rate changes, and the only rate test is confounded. It should be a task-matched near-work baseline for multi-rate HAR, a 'seconds-patching + adaptive pooling' variant, alongside fixed-grid resampling + SSM.

papers.title: Toward Universal Speech Enhancement for Diverse Input Conditions (USES)
papers.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv 2309.17384; IEEE ASRU 2023 (as cited by USEMamba's reference list)
papers.sections_read: Abstract, 1 Introduction, 2.1 Overview, 2.2 Sampling-Frequency-Independent design, 3.1 Data (part), 3.2 configs (STFT settings), 3.3 with Table 2, Table 4 caption
papers.mechanism: A sampling-frequency-independent (SFI) STFT/iSTFT with fixed-duration window and hop (32 ms and 16 ms), so the frame count is independent of the sampling frequency while the number of frequency bins grows with it. A 2-D conv encoder feeds dual-path Transformer blocks that model the frequency sequence and the time sequence separately (plus TAC across channels), followed by PReLU, a transposed-conv decoder and iSTFT. Complex spectral mapping.
papers.input_reconstruction: none. The STFT is a linear map of the point samples, not an integral over a reconstructed path.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: On the STFT frame clock, which is fixed in physical time (16 ms hop), and along the frequency-bin axis, whose length varies with the sampling rate. No nonlinearity is applied at the raw-sample rate.
papers.time_handling: Fixed physical-time frames: window and hop are set in ms and the sample counts are recomputed per sampling rate. There is no dt parameter.
papers.invariance_claim: Representation-level and approximate: fixed-duration STFT gives 'constant T-F resolution' across sampling rates. Generalisation from 8 kHz training to 16/48 kHz testing is empirical. There is no exact invariance or proof.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Train at 8 kHz, test at 16 kHz (WSJ0-2mix; real higher-rate measurements that also carry extra bandwidth) and at 48 kHz on other corpora. Compared against a 'resampling' route: down to 8 kHz, run the 8 kHz model, up to 16 kHz. There is no knot refinement, drop or irregular timing.
evidence_quotes: Sec 2.2: "if we use fixed-duration STFT window and hop sizes (e.g., 32 and 16 ms) for different SFs, the resultant spectra will have constant T-F resolution."
Sec 2.2: "the STFT spectra of the same signal sampled at different SFs will have the same number of frames and different numbers of frequency bins, while the resolution is always consistent."

Sec 3.3: "first downsampling 16 kHz mixtures to 8 kHz, then applying TFPSNet trained at 8 kHz for separation, and finally upsampling the separation results to 16 kHz (denoted as “resampling” in the second row) suffer from severe SI-SNR degradation."
Sec 1: "the proposed model can be trained on 8 kHz data alone and then tested on data with much higher sampling frequencies (e.g., 48 kHz)."
papers.reported_numbers:
Table 2 reports WSJ0-2mix SI-SNRi (dB). All models were trained on 8 kHz only.

| Model | 8 kHz | 16 kHz |
|---|---|---|
| TFPSNet (reproduced) | 21.0 | 12.0 (via resampling) |
| + SFI STFT/iSTFT | – | 19.7 |
| USES (1ch) | 20.3 | 19.8 |
| USES + mem tokens | 20.9 | 19.3 |

No HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM numbers.
papers.code_url_and_license: Not checked in this session (likely released through ESPnet, but not verified).
papers.notes:
Missing from the digest. It is the canonical speech-enhancement statement that a linear front end on a fixed physical-time frame clock, with all nonlinearities on that clock, gives sampling-rate generalisation. Together with Saito/Imamura SFI and Boulanger & Wood, N2 cannot claim the fixed clock.

Caution: its 'resampling' baseline discards the 4-8 kHz band. It is a real-downsampling baseline, not N2's mandatory fixed-grid resampling of the same content.

N2 can make a distinction here and should test it, not assert it. An STFT of point samples is not invariant to virtual-knot insertion on a PL path, because the added samples expose kink harmonics in new bins. An exact FOH stem is invariant.

papers.title: Universal Speech Enhancement with Regression and Generative Mamba (USEMamba)
papers.sections_read: Abstract, 1 Introduction, 2 Related Work (2.1 SEMamba), 3 intro, 3.2 Feature Mapping and SFI, 3.3, 4.1-4.3 (partial)
papers.mechanism: SEMamba-style time-frequency Mamba blocks (N1=10, N2=4 layers) on an SFI STFT/iSTFT front end with fixed-duration window and hop. Magnitude is predicted by mapping (Softplus) rather than masking. A flow-matching generative variant is used for bandwidth extension and packet loss.
papers.input_reconstruction: none: STFT of the samples.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: On STFT frames at a fixed physical-time hop: selective Mamba scans with per-frame input-dependent gates, plus MLP and Softplus. Scans also run along the frequency bins.
papers.time_handling: Fixed-duration frames (hop in seconds). The Mamba Δ is the usual input-dependent selective step per frame, not a physical dt.
papers.invariance_claim: Qualitative and empirical: SFI feature extraction 'ensuring robustness across varying sampling rates'. There is no per-rate ablation and no invariance statement.
papers.grid_changes_tested: URGENT 2025 challenge data with mixed sampling rates (8, 16, 22.05, 24, 32, 44.1, 48 kHz). There is no controlled rate change, refinement or drop test in the paper.
evidence_quotes: Sec 3.2: "the model dynamically adjusts the FFT window and hop size length (fixed time duration) based on the input sampling rate, maintaining a consistent duration of feature frames across different sampling rates."
Abstract: "a state-space speech enhancement model designed to handle long-range sequence modeling, time-frequency structured processing, and sampling frequency-independent feature extraction."
Sec 1: "the model employs a sampling frequency-independent (SFI) feature extraction mechanism, ensuring robustness across varying sampling rates."
papers.reported_numbers: 2nd place in Track 1 (blind test) and 2nd in the non-blind phase of the URGENT 2025 challenge. No per-sampling-rate numbers. No HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM numbers.
papers.code_url_and_license: Not found or checked in the text read.
papers.notes: The 2025 deep-SSM instance of 'linear front end + deep SSM on a fixed physical-time clock across sampling rates'. It weakens any N2 claim that a multirate SSM with a fixed clock is new. It is not exact and makes no refinement claim.

papers.title: Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting: A Transformable Patching Graph Neural Networks Approach (t-PatchGNN)
papers.arxiv_or_venue: ICML 2024, PMLR 235 (zhang24bw); OpenReview UZlMXUGI6e; arXiv id unknown (not found by arXiv API title search)
papers.sections_read: Abstract, 1 (part), 4.1.1 Transformable Patching, 4.1.2 Patch Encoding (Eqs 3-7), 4.2.1 Transformer, 4.2.2 (part), 5.1.1 Datasets, Table 1, 5.5 Effect of Patch Size, App A.5 dataset descriptions
papers.mechanism: Each univariate irregular series is split into patches of fixed physical time span s (for example 2 h). Each patch holds a variable number of observations. Each observation gets a learnable continuous time embedding (linear + sin) concatenated with its value. A Transformable Time-aware Conv (TTCN) aggregates observations inside the patch with meta-filter weights normalised by a softmax over the observations, and a patch mask flags empty patches. A Transformer runs over the patch sequence and a time-adaptive GNN runs across variables, followed by a decoder at the query times.
papers.input_reconstruction: none: observations are used directly, with no interpolation.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated:
Two stages:
- Per observation inside each patch: time embedding, meta-filter F_d, and the softmax over observations, which is density-dependent.
- Then on the fixed physical-time patch clock: the Transformer, GNN, and gated ReLU/tanh graph construction.
papers.time_handling: Time enters as a channel through the continuous time embedding. Patching uses a fixed physical time span, with positional encodings over the patch index.
papers.invariance_claim: None about sampling rate. The claim is a 'consistent temporal resolution across time and variables' of the patch sequence.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Only naturally irregular datasets (PhysioNet, MIMIC, Human Activity, USHCN), plus a patch-size sweep. No refinement, downsampling or controlled drop.
evidence_quotes: Sec 4.1.1: "Each transformable patch spans a patch window size s with a unified time horizon (e.g., 2 hours) to guarantee a consistent temporal resolution across time and variables."
Sec 4.1.2: "By normalizing the derived filter parameters along the temporal dimension, TTCN ensures consistent scaling of the convolution results for sequences with varying lengths."

Sec 4.1.2: "Considering that some patches may have no observations in the cases of sparse time series or high time horizon resolution, we additionally incorporate a patch masking term into the patch embedding"
Sec 4.1.1: "a patch composed of five sequential observations might span merely a few minutes for densely sampled scenarios and could cover several days in cases of sparse sampling."
papers.reported_numbers:
Table 1 (t-PatchGNN, MSE / MAE):
- PhysioNet: 4.98±0.08 (×1e-3) / 3.72±0.03 (×1e-2)
- MIMIC: 1.69±0.03 (×1e-2) / 7.22±0.09 (×1e-2)
- Human Activity: 2.66±0.03 (×1e-3) / 3.15±0.02 (×1e-2)
- USHCN: 5.00±0.04 (×1e-1) / 3.08±0.04 (×1e-1)

'Human Activity' here means 12 variables of 3-D positions from 4 body sensors on 5 people, forecasting 1000 ms from 3000 ms (App A.5). It is not UCI-HAR.
papers.code_url_and_license: https://github.com/usail-hkust/t-PatchGNN. No LICENSE file was found (raw LICENSE, LICENSE.md and LICENSE.txt all return 404 on the main and master branches).
papers.notes: Missing from the digest. It is a mainstream irregular-time-series model that already runs its deep nonlinear stack on a clock of fixed physical-time windows that does not depend on observation positions. N2's counterexample applies inside the patch: the softmax-weighted observation average changes when virtual knots are inserted. The empty-patch mask handles missing observations but does not separate virtual knots from measurements. It is a useful near-work baseline for missing and irregular protocols.

papers.title: Phased LSTM: Accelerating Recurrent Network Training for Long or Event-based Sequences
papers.sections_read: Abstract, 1 Introduction, 2 Model Description (Eqs 1-11), 3 Results intro, 3.1 Frequency Discrimination, 3.3 N-MNIST (Table 1), 3.4 Lip reading, 4 Discussion
papers.mechanism: An LSTM with an extra time gate k_t. The gate is a piecewise-linear function of the phase ((t−s) mod τ)/τ, with a learnable real-time period τ, phase shift s and open ratio r_on. The cell and hidden states are updated only in proportion to k_j (Eqs 7-10), and there is a small leak α when the gate is closed. Updates can occur at arbitrary irregular timestamps t_j.
papers.input_reconstruction: none. In the lip-reading experiment the gates are deliberately aligned to the input sampling times to avoid 'artificial interpolations'.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every observation or update time t_j: the candidate c~_j and h~_j are computed with sigmoid/tanh gates on x_j. Whether they take effect is gated by a physical-time periodic clock. The number of effective nonlinear updates therefore still scales with how many observations fall inside the open phases.
papers.time_handling: The timestamp drives the gate phase; τ is in real time (ms). There is no dt inside the recurrence. In multi-layer use the timestamp is shared by all layers.
papers.invariance_claim: Qualitative and empirical: the model 'naturally integrates inputs from sensors of arbitrary sampling rates'. There is no invariance statement.
papers.grid_changes_tested:
Four settings:
- Sine frequency discrimination under a standard 1 ms grid, a 10x oversampled 0.1 ms grid and asynchronous 0.02-10 ms sampling. These are real measurements, not virtual knots, and each appears to be trained separately.
- N-MNIST event inclusion probability ρ: trained at 0.75, tested at 0.4 and 1.0 without retraining. This is a random-drop / density change.
- GRID lip reading with MFCC at 25 Hz versus 100 Hz, trained separately.
- No knot refinement.
evidence_quotes: Sec 2: "updates to the cell state c_t and h_t are permitted only when the gate is open. The first parameter, τ, controls the real-time period of the oscillation."
Sec 2: "In contrast to traditional RNNs, and even sparser variants of RNNs [19], updates in Phased LSTM can optionally be performed at irregularly sampled time points t_j."
Sec 3.1: "for the oversampled condition, Phased LSTM actually increases in accuracy, as it receives more information about the underlying waveform."
Sec 3.3: "The Phased LSTM RNNs seem to have learned a stable spatio-temporal surface on the input and are only slightly altered by sampling it more or less frequently."
Sec 3.4: "This prevents presenting zeros or artificial interpolations to the network when data is not present."
papers.reported_numbers:
N-MNIST (Table 1), trained at ρ=0.75:

| Model | ρ=0.75 | test ρ=0.4 | test ρ=1.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phased LSTM (τ=100 ms) | 97.28±0.1 | 95.11±0.2 | 97.27±0.1 |
| BN-LSTM | 96.93±0.12 | 94.79±0.03 | 96.55±0.63 |
| CNN | 95.02±0.3 | 90.67±0.3 | 94.99±0.3 |

Phased LSTM uses 159±2.8 LSTM updates per neuron versus 3153 for BN-LSTM. GRID video-only peak accuracy is 81.15%. No HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM numbers.
papers.notes: A classic early precedent for putting nonlinear recurrent updates under a physical-time clock rather than the observation index. It does not decouple the two: each observation inside an open window triggers a nonlinear update, so densifying the grid changes the state. It also treats denser real samples as 'more information', with no notion of lossless virtual knots. It is a candidate 'physical-time-clock RNN' near-work baseline, and a natural target for N2's per-observation counterexample.

papers.title: Smartphone Sensor-based Human Activity Recognition Robust to Different Sampling Rates
papers.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv 2101.00812; IEEE Sensors Journal 21 (2021), DOI 10.1109/JSEN.2020.3038281 (ADS bibcode 2021ISenJ..21.6930H)
papers.sections_read: Abstract, II-C, III-A Overview, III-D, III-E Data augmentation by downsampling, IV-A, IV-B, V-A1, V-A2, V-A3, V-A4 with Table II, V-B3, V-C Limitations, VI Conclusion
papers.mechanism: A VGG16-based CNN feature extractor E, an activity classifier C, and a sampling-rate discriminator D trained adversarially (DANN-like) so features make the sampling rate 'unspecifiable'. Training data are augmented by downsampling (low-pass filter then thinning). Every input is linearly interpolated to a common length before the CNN.
papers.input_reconstruction: Linear interpolation onto a fixed-length grid, i.e. fixed-grid resampling to the 256-sample frame length used at 100 Hz.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: On the fixed resampled grid (CNN, then FC ReLU layers).
papers.time_handling: Fixed-grid resampling. The true sampling-rate label is used only as the adversarial target. There is no dt and no timestamps.
papers.invariance_claim: The target is a representation from which the sampling rate cannot be identified, pursued empirically through adversarial training. There is no exact or approximate invariance statement.
papers.grid_changes_tested:
Four settings, none of them knot refinement or random drop:
- Real downsampling simulated with LPF + thinning from 100 Hz to 50, 25, 12.5 and 6.25 Hz (rates seen in training).
- Unseen rates of 33.3, 20, 10, 5 and 4 Hz.
- Actually measured 40 Hz HASC data from 20 subjects.
- A mixed-rate training environment.

papers.notes:
The HAR-specific instance of N2's mandatory 'fixed-grid resampling + network' baseline, with a sampling-rate robustness claim. It is useful calibration for how HAR accuracy degrades under real downsampling.

It also supports N2's three-way separation. After real LPF downsampling, the linearly interpolated inputs remain rate-identifiable (96.9%), so resampling is not invariant to real downsampling. It would be exactly invariant to virtual knots on the same interpolant, and so would N2's stem.

The paper's distinction between 'pseudo-reproduced' downsampling and actually measured 40 Hz data is a simulated-versus-real-measurement issue, not a virtual-knot one.

papers.title: Antiderivative Antialiasing for Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.arxiv_or_venue: DAFx25, Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Digital Audio Effects (Ancona, Italy, 2-5 Sep 2025), paper 72; page headers start at 39. No arXiv id found.
papers.sections_read: Abstract, 1 Introduction, 2.1 ADAA, 2.2 Sample Rate Independent RNNs, 3 Method, 3.1 GRU (Eqs 16-36), 3.2 LSTM (part), 4.1 Models and Baselines, 4.2 Evaluation, 4.3 Implementation, 5.1 Alias Rejection
papers.mechanism: Every activation in an explicit RNN (GRU, LSTM) is replaced by its antiderivative-antialiased (ADAA) form of order o. Order-dependent synchronization filters H_o re-align the internal signals delayed by ADAA's group delay. The recurrence is then re-timed with the sample-rate-independent RNN technique h'_n = f(x'_n, h'_{n−M}), so the continuous-time state delay matches training. The system becomes native to an oversampled rate (o+1)f_SR, optionally times M_OS.
papers.input_reconstruction: Linear interpolation (piecewise-linear) of each activation's argument between consecutive samples, with a continuous-time rectangular anti-aliasing kernel. Higher orders use higher-order antiderivatives and difference operators.
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every sample of the (oversampled) grid. Each output is the closed-form rectangular-window average of f over the linear-interpolation (PL) segment of its argument.
papers.time_handling: Fixed sample rate. The recurrence delay is matched to a physical-time delay: an integer M is exact, a non-integer M uses fractional-delay filters.
papers.invariance_claim: No invariance claim. The claim is reduced aliasing (higher SNRA) with a moderate change in tonality.
papers.grid_changes_tested: Pretrained at 44.1 kHz and run at 44.1, 88.2 and 176.4 kHz (integer oversampling). Evaluated with sine tones from A0 to C8 and with sweeps. No refinement, drop or irregular timing.
evidence_quotes: Sec 2.1: "Parker et al. [8] derive an expression for a discrete-time approximation of Eq. (2) by assuming a piecewise-linear x(t) and applying an antialiasing filter in continuous time using a rectangular kernel."
Sec 2.2: "This is achieved by delaying the state recursion such that the continuous-time delay matches that seen during training"
Sec 2.2: "In the general case of M∈R+, the required past states can be approximated by using a fractional delay filter, resulting in modifications in model tonality."
Sec 3.1: "Note that both the Hadamard product and the (memoryless) activations inherently expand the spectrum, making them susceptible to aliasing."
papers.reported_numbers:
SNRA results:
- GRU at 88.2 kHz: 1st-order ADAA gives about +20 dB over the baseline where values start dropping from 100 dB.
- GRU at 176.4 kHz: about +20 dB (1st order) and about +30 dB (2nd order).

Models: GRU size 32 (Blackstar HT-1) and LSTM size 40 (Mesa Mini Rectifier), trained at 44.1 kHz. Computed in float64 with ε=1e-3. No HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM numbers.
papers.code_url_and_license: Accompanying webpage https://otto-soundtoys.github.io/dafx25-adaa-for-rnns/. The paper is CC BY 4.0. Code availability and license were not checked.
papers.notes:
This is the alias-free-nonlinearity-for-recurrent-time-series literature the digest missed. Evaluating a nonlinearity in continuous time over the PL reconstruction, in closed form, is known (Parker 2016 ADAA and its extensions). N2 must not claim alias-free nonlinearities or continuous-time nonlinearity evaluation.

ADAA outputs stay on the sample grid and add grid-dependent memory, so it is not refinement-invariant. The paper also shows float64 plus an ε-guard is needed for small input differences. That is directly relevant to N2's small-dt stability checks, and an analogous cancellation issue arises for the φ-functions.

papers.title: Aliasing-Free Neural Audio Synthesis (Pupu-Vocoder / Pupu-Codec)
papers.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv 2512.20211 (v1; the paper states 'Received 23 December 2025; revised 2 April 2026'); journal submission, venue not verified
papers.sections_read: Abstract, I Introduction, II-A Artifacts due to Non-Linear Activation Functions (Eqs 1-8), II-B (part), III-A Anti-Aliased Activation Functions (Eqs 10-18), V-A2/V-A3 (configs), V-B1 (metrics), V-C1 effectiveness, V-C2 (RTF paragraph), V-C4 (oversampling ablation sentence), VII Future Works
papers.mechanism: A BigVGAN/DAC-style vocoder and codec in which every activation is an oversampled (2x) ADAA SnakeBeta: a closed-form average over a linearly interpolated segment, stable because of a sinc form. ConvTranspose upsampling is replaced by zero-interlacing, low-pass filtering and a high-pass noise prior.
papers.input_reconstruction: Linear interpolation between consecutive samples (Eq. 4) with a unit-width rectangular kernel (Eq. 6), giving the closed form y_t = (F(x_t) − F(x_{t−1}))/(x_t − x_{t−1}).
papers.where_nonlinearity_evaluated: At every sample of the internal (2x oversampled) grid, as a PL-segment average.
papers.time_handling: A fixed 44.1 kHz sample rate, with no dt and no rate change.
papers.invariance_claim: None about sampling rate. The paper claims aliasing suppression and says the method is 'domain-agnostic'.
papers.grid_changes_tested: None. Evaluated on an aliasing test-signal benchmark (AHR), sine sweeps, and speech, singing, music and audio quality.
evidence_quotes: Sec II-A: "Its main idea is to convert the discrete signal to a continuous one before applying the activation function. Since the signal is continuous, there are no sampling frequency constraints, and therefore, no aliasing artifacts."
Sec I: "the unconstrained nonlinear activation generates infinitely many harmonics that exceed the Nyquist frequency, resulting in “folded-back” aliasing artifacts"
Sec V-C1: "our ADAA SnakeBeta without oversampling achieved anti-aliasing performance comparable to SnakeBeta with a 2× oversampling factor."
Sec I: "Beyond audio synthesis, we emphasize that our method is domain-agnostic, making it applicable to other domains where aliasing is a concern, such as image generation."
papers.reported_numbers:
No HAR, EigenWorms, Speech Commands or PDM numbers.
